title: GPT-5.5 rolls out to ChatGPT paid users
summary: OpenAI began a gradual rollout of GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise ChatGPT subscribers today. The new Thinking variant is pitched as the most capable reasoning model in ChatGPT, able to handle complex multi-step tasks, while API access will follow later with additional safeguards in place.

title: OpenAI splits ChatGPT Pro into $100 and $200 tiers
summary: OpenAI restructured its Pro offering into two tiers: $100/month for 5x usage versus Plus, and $200/month for 20x usage, both including access to GPT-5.5 Pro, Codex, and Deep Research. The $100 tier launches with a temporary 10x Codex bonus through May 31 to sweeten the deal.

title: ComfyUI hits $500M valuation after $30M raise
summary: ComfyUI, the open-source node-based tool that gives creators granular control over AI image, video, and audio generation, closed a $30 million funding round at a $500 million valuation. The raise reflects growing demand from creators who want more hands-on control than turnkey AI apps provide.

title: Replicate adds Moonshot Kimi-K2 and Alibaba Happy Horse
summary: Replicate's official model catalog expanded this week with Moonshot AI's Kimi-K2, a one-trillion-parameter open model built for long-horizon coding and agent swarms with a 262k context window. Alibaba's Happy Horse 1.0 also landed, offering text-to-video and image-to-video generation at 720p and 1080p.

title: DeepMind's David Silver raises $1.1B for data-free AI lab
summary: Ineffable Intelligence, a British AI lab founded just months ago by AlphaGo creator David Silver, secured $1.1 billion at a $5.1 billion valuation. The lab is pursuing AI systems that learn without human-labeled data, a fundamental departure from how most frontier models are trained today.

title: Google commits up to $40B to Anthropic
summary: Google announced plans to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic in a combination of cash and compute, cementing its position as the startup's largest backer. The deal follows the limited release of Anthropic's cybersecurity-focused Mythos model and comes as Anthropic's annualized revenue reportedly surged past $30 billion.

title: OpenAI resolves Microsoft conflict over AWS deal
summary: OpenAI has secured major concessions from Microsoft that clear the path for it to sell products on Amazon Web Services, ending a legal dispute between the two companies. In exchange, Microsoft receives an expanded revenue-share agreement, signaling a careful rebalancing of one of AI's most important partnerships.

title: Sierra acquires YC-backed Fragment
summary: Sierra, the AI customer service agent company co-founded by Bret Taylor, has acquired Fragment, a French YC-backed startup. The acquisition is expected to deepen Sierra's capabilities as demand for enterprise-grade AI agents accelerates across industries.

title: 120,000 authors chase share of Anthropic's $1.5B copyright settlement
summary: Nearly 120,000 authors and copyright holders have filed to claim a portion of a $1.5 billion class-action settlement with Anthropic over unauthorized use of their books in AI training data. The settlement is among the largest copyright resolutions in the AI industry and could set precedent for future training-data disputes.

title: Musk vs. Altman trial kicks off with $150B on the line
summary: Jury selection began Monday in San Francisco for Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI, with opening arguments set for Tuesday. Musk claims OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit charter when it pivoted toward profit, and he is seeking up to $150 billion in damages for its charitable arm — a verdict that could reshape AI governance and nonprofit law.

title: 600 Google employees demand CEO reject classified Pentagon AI deal
summary: More than 600 Google staff signed an open letter urging CEO Sundar Pichai to turn down a proposed Defense Department contract that would extend Gemini's capabilities into classified military operations. Google already holds a non-classified AI contract with the DoD, making this a direct escalation of the long-running employee activism over military AI.

title: US judges scramble to set AI policies for their chambers
summary: Federal judges across the country are grappling with how AI tools should — and should not — be used in court filings and legal research, with policies ranging from outright bans to cautious endorsements. The patchwork approach reflects broader uncertainty about AI reliability after several high-profile incidents of AI-generated errors in legal documents.

title: BXAI-OS listed in NIST catalog ahead of Colorado AI deadline
summary: BXAI-OS has been officially cataloged as a NIST Informative Reference, providing organizations a machine-executable framework for AI governance compliance ahead of Colorado's June 30, 2026 SB 24-205 deadline. The listing arrives as California and New York move toward their own AI regulations, tightening a growing patchwork of state-level AI rules.

title: GitHub Copilot adds Claude and Codex to Agent HQ
summary: GitHub's Agent HQ now lets developers pick between Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex directly inside GitHub and VS Code. The feature is in public preview for Copilot Pro+ and Enterprise subscribers, expanding the platform's multi-agent orchestration ambitions first unveiled at Universe 2025.

title: GitHub Copilot SDK opens to all developers
summary: A new GitHub Copilot SDK is now in technical preview, letting any application embed a programmable agent layer that can plan tasks, invoke tools, edit files, and run commands. GitHub is positioning this as a way to bake AI-native workflows into third-party apps, not just its own surfaces.

title: OpenAI restructures ChatGPT Pro into two tiers
summary: OpenAI has split its $200 ChatGPT Pro plan, adding a new $100 mid-tier that offers 5x usage limits over Plus and 10x Codex access through May 31. The restructure reflects growing demand for Codex and Deep Research among professional users who don't need the full unlimited-tier firepower.

title: Google donates Agent Payments Protocol to FIDO Alliance
summary: Google open-sourced version 0.2 of its Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) on GitHub and handed stewardship to the FIDO Alliance. The update introduces 'Human Not Present' payment flows, allowing AI agents to autonomously complete pre-authorized purchases — like snagging concert tickets the instant they go on sale.

title: FLUX.2 family brings sub-second image gen to production
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 lineup on Replicate now spans three tiers: Max for ultra-high-fidelity product photography, Pro for high-volume editing with structured JSON prompting, and Klein 4B — a 4-billion-parameter distilled model capable of sub-second generation for real-time apps. All tiers support multi-reference image blending.

title: DeepMind co-founder raises $1.1B for Ineffable Intelligence
summary: David Silver, the DeepMind researcher behind AlphaGo, has secured $1.1 billion for his new British AI lab Ineffable Intelligence at a $5.1 billion valuation. The startup is pursuing AI systems that learn without human-labeled data, betting on reinforcement learning as the path to more autonomous AI.

title: Tencent and Alibaba circle DeepSeek at $20B+ valuation
summary: Chinese tech giants Tencent and Alibaba are in advanced talks to invest in DeepSeek, the AI lab owned by hedge fund High-Flyer Capital Management, at a valuation exceeding $20 billion. It would be DeepSeek's first external fundraise, underscoring how seriously Chinese incumbents are taking the upstart's rapid rise.

title: Space defense startup True Anomaly lands $650M Series D
summary: True Anomaly, which builds autonomous spacecraft and software for U.S. national security missions, closed a $650 million Series D that lifts its total funding to $1 billion. The round signals sustained investor appetite for AI-driven defense technology as geopolitical tensions around space assets intensify.

title: Counterpart raises $96M to insure AI-related damage
summary: Insurtech startup Counterpart closed a $96 million round, bringing total capital to $106 million, to expand its AI-powered liability insurance products. The raise comes as enterprises face mounting legal exposure from AI errors, bias claims, and regulatory penalties.

title: Windmill pulls $12M to reinvent AI-era performance reviews
summary: HR tech startup Windmill raised $12 million across pre-seed and seed rounds to build fairer, more frequent performance evaluations using AI. The founders argue that as AI-driven workplace anxiety grows, companies need objective and auditable feedback systems that reduce managerial bias.

title: Musk vs. Altman trial kicks off in California
summary: Jury selection began Monday in San Francisco for Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI, with opening arguments set for Tuesday. Musk is seeking up to $150 billion in damages, alleging OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit charter when it pivoted toward a for-profit structure — a case that could redefine how AI companies are legally obligated to honor their founding missions.

title: DOJ backs xAI lawsuit to kill Colorado's AI Act
summary: The Department of Justice intervened on April 24 in xAI's lawsuit challenging Colorado's sweeping AI Act, marking the first time the federal government has moved to invalidate a state AI law under Trump's Executive Order 14365. The DOJ argued the law violates the Equal Protection Clause by compelling AI companies to factor demographic characteristics into model design, framing state-level AI regulation as a barrier to national competitiveness.

title: China blocks Meta's $2B acquisition of Manus
summary: Beijing formally blocked Meta's $2 billion bid to acquire Manus, an AI agent startup, following a months-long regulatory probe. The decision underscores how cross-border AI acquisitions are increasingly caught in geopolitical crossfire, with data sovereignty and AI agent capabilities now treated as strategic national interests.

title: OpenAI ends Microsoft exclusivity, expands to AWS
summary: OpenAI has resolved its long-running legal and commercial tensions with Microsoft, clearing the way to offer its models on Amazon Web Services and potentially other cloud providers. The deal marks a significant shift from the exclusive Azure partnership that defined OpenAI's commercial infrastructure for years.

title: AI's regulatory honeymoon is officially over in 2026
summary: A wave of major AI regulations is hitting simultaneously: the EU AI Act's high-risk provisions take full effect in August with penalties up to €35 million, Colorado's AI Act is due June 30, California's AI Transparency Act kicks in by August, and a 42-state attorney general coalition is ramping up coordinated enforcement. Companies that treated compliance as optional are now facing a hard reckoning.

title: Gemini remembers you — and will steal your ChatGPT history
summary: Google is rolling out a Memories feature to UK Gemini users that lets the assistant learn preferences across conversations over time. More aggressively, it now lets users import their full chat history and saved memories from rival AI apps via ZIP file or a copy-paste prompt flow. The move is a direct shot at user lock-in across the AI assistant market.

title: Kiri.ai drops a 1-trillion-parameter open model on Replicate
summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi model — 1 trillion parameters, 262k context window, with vision and tool use — is now available via Replicate's API alongside a wave of other frontier models. The Replicate catalog now spans everything from OpenAI's GPT image generation to Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 and ByteDance's multimodal video model. The breadth signals that production-ready model access is becoming a commodity.

title: FLUX 2 Max targets product photography and character consistency
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 family now covers the full spectrum from sub-second prototyping with FLUX 2 Klein to premium fidelity with FLUX 2 Max, which supports up to 8 reference images for character and product consistency. Structured JSON prompting and precise hex color control make it a serious contender for commercial creative workflows. The family is available production-ready via Replicate.

title: Google Translate turns 20 with Gemini-powered idiom smarts
summary: Google marked the 20th anniversary of Translate by integrating Gemini models into its Live interpretation feature, which now handles slang, idioms, and tonal nuance rather than just literal translation. Earbuds can now act as real-time interpreters that preserve a speaker's rhythm and register. The upgrade reflects how Gemini is quietly becoming the engine behind Google's entire product surface.

title: FIDO Alliance sets safety rules for AI agents buying things online
summary: The FIDO Alliance announced new authentication standards specifically designed for AI agents that shop, log in, and transact on users' behalf. The initiative addresses a fast-growing identity problem: as agents proliferate, most organizations have no controls over which agents access which data or accounts. The standards aim to prevent agents from going rogue with payment credentials before the problem becomes widespread.

title: Scout AI raises $100M to train models for battlefield ATVs
summary: Scout AI, a self-described frontier lab for defense founded in 2024, closed a $100M Series A led by Align Ventures and Draper Associates. The startup builds autonomous military all-terrain vehicles and trains the AI models that operate them. It previously raised a $15M seed in January 2025, making this a rapid scale-up in a sector attracting serious venture capital.

title: Aidoc pulls in $150M Series E for clinical AI imaging
summary: Clinical AI provider Aidoc secured $150M in a Series E led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with General Catalyst, SoftBank, and NVIDIA's NVentures also participating. The company, which applies AI to medical imaging workflows, has now raised $520M in total. The round comes weeks after rival RadAI closed a $60M Series C at a $525M valuation, signaling fierce competition in radiology AI.

title: BMW i Ventures launches $300M fund with AI and robotics thesis
summary: BMW's independent venture arm announced a $300M third fund focused on agentic AI, physical AI, robotics, and industrial software for the automotive sector. The new fund brings BMW i Ventures to $1.1B in total capital under management and will invest from early stage through Series B in North America and Europe. No investments from the new fund have been announced yet.

title: Pursuit lands $22M seed to help companies win government contracts
summary: Pursuit, a platform that helps businesses find and win government contracts, announced a $22M seed round led by OpenGov co-founder Mike Rosengarten, with backing from Bill Gurley, Jack Altman, and Sam Hinkie. The company launched in 2023 out of a simple observation: selling to government is surprisingly hard for most companies. Total funding now stands at $25.5M.

title: Shapes raises $8M for AI characters in your group chats
summary: Shapes, an app that embeds AI characters directly into human group conversations, emerged from stealth with $8M in seed funding led by Lightspeed. Think Discord, but where AI personas are full participants in the chat alongside real users. The company plans to use the capital to accelerate user acquisition in what is shaping up to be a crowded social AI space.

title: EU AI Act talks collapse after marathon session
summary: After 12 hours of negotiations, EU member states and European Parliament lawmakers failed to agree on amendments to the AI Act that would have delayed high-risk compliance deadlines from August 2026 to 2027 or later. The core sticking point is whether AI embedded in already-regulated products like medical devices and toys should be exempt from additional AI Act requirements. If talks stall through May and June, companies that built their timelines around the extension could face immediate compliance obligations they are not ready for.

title: Google signed a classified AI deal with the Pentagon — quietly
summary: Google reportedly agreed to let the US Department of Defense use its AI models for any lawful government purpose under a classified contract, placing it alongside OpenAI and xAI in the set of companies with secret military AI agreements. The deal reportedly bars the company from blocking lawful government uses and requires it to help adjust safety filters when asked. The contract was finalized less than a day after Google employees publicly asked Sundar Pichai to block Pentagon access.

title: Musk takes the stand in his OpenAI trial
summary: Elon Musk began testifying in his lawsuit against OpenAI, Sam Altman, and Greg Brockman in a California federal courtroom. Musk is alleging fraud, breach of charitable trust, and unjust enrichment, and is seeking to unwind OpenAI's for-profit restructuring and strip Altman and Brockman of authority. The trial is expected to call major industry witnesses including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati.

title: AI regulation is fracturing into sovereign bubbles
summary: A new analysis argues that the long-anticipated convergence of global AI rules is not happening — instead, 2026 is seeing a mosaic of incompatible national regimes. Australia is advancing workplace AI law, Pakistan is restricting government hiring AI, US states are passing a flurry of bills while the White House pushes federal preemption, and the EU can't even agree with itself. For multinationals, the compliance burden is becoming a competitive disadvantage, and shadow AI use is growing as strict internal policies push employees toward personal accounts.

title: The US should build AI standards, not bully AI companies
summary: A sharp analysis argues that the Trump administration's confrontation with Anthropic — threatening to blacklist the company for refusing to remove safety guardrails from Pentagon access — is the wrong play, and risks damaging US credibility in international AI governance. The piece draws a historical parallel to how the US shaped the internet by leading protocol standards through DARPA and NIST, and argues that CAISI's new AI Agent Standards Initiative is the right model to follow. Countries considering adopting US-led AI infrastructure are watching the Anthropic episode carefully.

title: Google AI Max turns one, goes shopping
summary: Google's AI Max for Search celebrates its first birthday by expanding into Shopping campaigns and travel-specific ad formats. A new Gemini-powered tool called AI Brief lets advertisers steer messaging, audience targeting, and search matching in plain language before committing to any changes. Text disclaimers for regulated industries are also rolling out, finally letting compliance-heavy advertisers use Final URL expansion.

title: inclusionAI drops a trillion-parameter open-source model
summary: Ling-2.6-1T is a one-trillion-parameter model that combines MLA and Linear Attention for lower VRAM and faster inference on long contexts. The team claims open-source SOTA on AIME26, SWE-bench Verified, and several agent execution benchmarks. A 'fast thinking' mechanism cuts chain-of-thought verbosity, reducing token costs without sacrificing reasoning quality.

title: IBM Granite gets a multilingual embedding upgrade
summary: IBM's Granite-Embedding-97M-Multilingual-R2 swaps XLM-RoBERTa for ModernBERT and stretches context from 512 to 32,768 tokens. The 97M parameter model supports 200-plus languages with enhanced retrieval training across 52 of them, plus nine programming languages. It ships with ONNX and OpenVINO exports and posts a 14.5-point average gain over its predecessor on multilingual benchmarks.

title: FLUX 2 lands on Replicate with sub-second generation
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 family is now fully available via Replicate's production API, covering Max, Pro, and the four-billion-parameter Klein model that generates images in under a second. The lineup supports up to ten reference images for multi-image blending and structured JSON prompting for precise camera and lighting control. FLUX.1 Fill, Depth, and Canny round out the suite for inpainting and structure-preserving edits.

title: Anthropic eyes $50B raise at a $900B valuation
summary: Sources say Anthropic is in talks to close a new $50 billion funding round that would push its valuation toward $900 billion, a figure that would make it one of the most valuable private companies ever. The round comes as the company's Claude models gain traction across enterprise and consumer use cases. No lead investor has been named publicly yet.

title: Netomi raises $110M with Accenture and Adobe leading
summary: AI customer-service startup Netomi closed a $110 million round led by Accenture Ventures, with Adobe Ventures, Silver Lake Waterman, and WndrCo also participating. DreamWorks co-founder Jeffrey Katzenberg joins the board, and Accenture has signed a global alliance to bring Netomi to its Fortune 100 client base. The raise lands in a crowded field where Sierra is valued at $10 billion and Decagon at $4.5 billion.

title: 137 Ventures pulls in $700M for growth-stage bets
summary: SpaceX backer 137 Ventures announced two new growth-stage funds totaling more than $700 million, focused on defense, AI, and industrial systems. Founded by former Founders Fund investor Justin Fishner-Wolfson, the firm says it has deployed over a billion dollars in the past year alone. The raise signals continued appetite for late-stage private market exposure in hard-tech.

title: Cresta quietly hits $100M ARR
summary: a16z and Sequoia-backed Cresta has crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, competing in the same AI customer-service arena as Netomi, Sierra, and Decagon. The company was last valued at $1.6 billion in 2022 and raised a $125 million round in late 2024 at an undisclosed valuation. With revenue now at nine figures, a re-pricing is likely overdue.

title: Legora extends Series D to $600M with Nvidia aboard
summary: Swedish legal-tech unicorn Legora added a $50 million extension to its Series D, bringing the total to $600 million and valuing the company at $5.6 billion. Nvidia's venture arm NVentures and Atlassian joined as new corporate investors alongside Adams Street Partners, Barclays, and Insight Partners. The extension follows a $550 million raise just six weeks earlier in March.

title: EU Omnibus collapses, AI Act deadline holds
summary: Twelve hours of trilogue negotiations in Brussels ended Monday without a deal, meaning the EU AI Act's Annex III high-risk system deadline remains August 2, 2026 — not pushed to December 2027 as founders had hoped. The next trilogue is scheduled for May 13, but nothing has changed legally in the meantime. Startups banking on the delay now face a hard compliance sprint.

title: White House AI framework pushes federal preemption — courts will decide
summary: The White House's March 2026 National Policy Framework for AI strongly endorses federal preemption of state AI laws covering development, liability, and AI-enabled activities, while carving out zoning, fraud, and child safety. Legal experts note an executive order cannot actually preempt state law — only Congress or the courts can — and no court has struck down any state AI statute yet. The DOJ AI Litigation Task Force has already joined xAI's lawsuit against Colorado's SB 205 as its opening move.

title: State AI rules are getting teeth — and deadlines
summary: New York mandates AI-generated performer disclosure starting June 9, California requires embedded metadata on all AI content by August 2 with $5,000-per-day fines for stripping it, and Tennessee already treats unauthorized AI voice cloning as a criminal misdemeanor under the ELVIS Act. The FTC, meanwhile, has ramped up AI-washing enforcement with a 40% increase in actions in 2025 and penalties up to $51,744 per violation. Legal experts say the only safe strategy is to build compliance around the strictest applicable state standard now.

title: Elon Musk takes the stand again in OpenAI trial
summary: Musk appeared for a second day of testimony in his ongoing legal challenge against OpenAI, a case that observers say could reshape governance norms across the AI industry. The trial centers on whether OpenAI violated its founding nonprofit mission by pursuing a for-profit restructuring. No verdict is expected imminently, but each day of testimony generates fresh public attention on AI corporate structure.

title: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Nano rewrites on-device AI
summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Nano on Hugging Face, a hybrid Mamba-2 + Transformer MoE model with 30B total but only 3B active parameters, a 1-million-token context window, and up to 4x faster inference than its predecessor. It features reasoning ON/OFF modes with configurable thinking budgets and is served via vLLM and SGLang. NVIDIA simultaneously dropped Nemotron Nano VL, Cosmos Predict 2.5, and millions of open training samples — making this one of the largest single-day open-model drops in recent memory.

title: Kling Video 3.0 and MiniMax Speech 2.6 land on Replicate
summary: Replicate added Kling Video 3.0 Omni — a unified multimodal video generation model with native audio, reference images, video editing, and multi-shot control — alongside MiniMax Speech 2.6 Turbo, which brings 300+ voices and multilingual emotional text-to-speech at real-time-friendly pricing. The additions round out a growing production-ready video and voice stack on the platform.

title: FLUX.2 family goes deep on multi-reference editing
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 line — Max, Pro, and the sub-second Klein 4B — now supports up to 10 reference images for character and product consistency, structured JSON prompting for precise camera and lighting control, and hex-code color matching for brand work. FLUX.2 Klein generates images in under a second, making it practical for live-preview and consumer hardware use cases.

title: Microsoft embeds a legal agent directly into Word
summary: Microsoft is rolling out a new legal AI agent inside Word, targeted at in-house and firm legal teams. The move follows a broader pattern of Microsoft weaving Copilot-style agents into existing Office surfaces rather than standalone apps, lowering the adoption barrier for professional users who live in Word already.

title: Anthropic's $900B+ valuation round could close within two weeks
summary: Sources tell TechCrunch that Anthropic is in late-stage talks for a $50B raise that would peg its valuation north of $900 billion — a figure that would make it one of the most valuable private companies ever. The timing tracks with growing interest from sovereign wealth and strategic investors looking to lock in positions before a potential public offering. If it closes, it sets a new ceiling for AI startup valuations.

title: Meta acquires humanoid robotics startup Assured Robot Intelligence
summary: Meta has bought ARI — Assured Robot Intelligence — for an undisclosed sum, folding its founding team into the Superintelligence Labs division. ARI had raised only a seed round from AI-focused Aix Ventures, making this an acqui-hire at the frontier of embodied AI. The deal mirrors Meta's acquisition of Fauna and signals the company is racing to staff up physical AI capabilities alongside its model research.

title: Anduril closes ~$4B round at $60B valuation
summary: Defense tech startup Anduril is finalizing roughly $4 billion in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz and Thrive Capital, valuing the company at $60 billion. The round cements Anduril as the most valuable private defense-tech company in the US and reflects surging investor appetite for AI-powered national security infrastructure.

title: Legal AI startup Legora hits $5.6B valuation
summary: Legora, a legal AI platform, has reached a $5.6 billion valuation in its latest round, putting it in direct competition with Harvey — the other high-profile AI legal unicorn. The dual-unicorn dynamic in legal AI mirrors what happened in cybersecurity AI a year ago, and both companies are now racing to lock up BigLaw and enterprise contracts.

title: Skio sells for $105M after raising just $8M
summary: Y Combinator alum Skio, a subscription commerce platform, was acquired for $105 million in cash — despite having raised only $8 million total, according to its founder. The outcome is a rare clean capital-efficient exit in a funding climate dominated by mega-rounds, and will likely circulate widely in founder communities as a counternarrative to the raise-at-all-costs playbook.

title: Musk's OpenAI testimony backfired, say observers
summary: After a week on the stand in his lawsuit against OpenAI, Elon Musk reportedly spent much of the time arguing with opposing and even his own lawyers while struggling to maintain a consistent account of his founding role. Commentators describe his testimony as unlikely to sway a jury that already needed persuading. With the dramatic narrative faltering, legal watchers say the case may now hinge on the paper trail of corporate history rather than courtroom theater.

title: Pentagon cuts Anthropic, keeps xAI and OpenAI for classified AI work
summary: The Department of Defense has granted classified operational AI contracts to OpenAI, Palantir, and xAI while labeling Anthropic a supply chain risk — a sharp reversal after the company had previously worked with the Pentagon on classified systems. Anthropic had refused to loosen its red lines on mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, was subsequently banned from federal use, and won a temporary injunction after suing. The standoff sets up a defining question about whether national security AI contracts will reward compliance over safety constraints.

title: DOJ joins xAI's lawsuit to kill Colorado's AI Act
summary: The Department of Justice has filed a motion to intervene in xAI's federal suit against Colorado's attorney general, seeking to block enforcement of the state's AI discrimination law on constitutional grounds. Andreessen Horowitz has separately published a framework arguing Commerce Clause doctrine should be used to strike down state AI regulations. The coordinated federal and industry push signals a major legal campaign to establish national preemption before more states pass similar laws.

title: Dark money campaign pays influencers to push pro-US AI messaging
summary: Wired reports that a group called Build American AI, tied to a super PAC called Leading the Future with backing from tech figures, is paying content creators thousands of dollars per video to promote American AI dominance and frame China as a threat. The campaign runs in phases, starting with lifestyle influencers before escalating to more policy-oriented messaging. OpenAI and Palantir both deny corporate involvement, but the operation raises pointed questions about undisclosed lobbying through creator channels.

title: South Korea mandates AI labels across the full content distribution chain
summary: South Korea is finalizing amendments that would require AI-generated photos and videos to carry clear labels, with obligations falling not just on developers but on uploaders, distributors, and platform operators. The framework targets fake celebrity endorsements and synthetic personas used in advertising, and includes faster takedown authority and stiffer financial penalties. For global brands using AI-enhanced content tied to Korean IP or distributed on Korean platforms, compliance workflows may need a full redesign.

title: NVIDIA floods Hugging Face with open models
summary: NVIDIA released a sweeping collection of open weights and datasets on Hugging Face, anchored by Nemotron 3 Nano — a 30B-total/3B-active hybrid Mamba-2 + Transformer MoE model with a 1M-token context window and reasoning ON/OFF modes. The release also includes Nemotron Nano VL (12B) for vision-language tasks, Cosmos Predict 2.5 for physics-aware video generation, and millions of rows of multilingual and OCR datasets. Everything ships under permissive licenses with training recipes included.

title: FLUX.2 Max raises the bar for image APIs
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 Max is now the top-tier option on Replicate, supporting up to 8 reference images for character consistency, hex color control for brand accuracy, and structured JSON prompting for precise composition. A distilled 4B-parameter FLUX.2 Klein variant delivers sub-second generation for real-time apps. The lineup cements FLUX as the go-to family for production image pipelines.

title: Kling Video 3.0 lands on Replicate with native audio
summary: Kling Video 3.0 Omni arrived on Replicate with unified multimodal video generation, supporting reference images, video editing, native audio, and multi-shot control in a single model. The standard 3.0 tier generates cinematic clips up to 15 seconds with improved consistency. It joins a growing slate of production-ready video models now available via one-line API calls.

title: Microsoft embeds a legal agent inside Word
summary: Microsoft is rolling out a new legal AI agent directly inside Word, designed for legal teams to draft, review, and analyze documents without leaving their workflow. The move is part of a broader push to embed autonomous agents into Microsoft 365 applications. It signals that agentic features are shifting from standalone tools into the software people already use daily.

title: Anthropic closing in on a $900B+ valuation round
summary: Sources tell TechCrunch that Anthropic could raise a new $50B round at a valuation exceeding $900 billion, potentially closing within two weeks. The round would be one of the largest private financings in tech history and comes as the company faces simultaneous pressure from a Pentagon ban and a high-profile copyright lawsuit. If it closes, it repositions Anthropic as the most valuable private AI lab on earth.

title: Meta acquires humanoid robotics startup ARI
summary: Meta has bought Assured Robot Intelligence for an undisclosed sum, folding the team and its co-founders into the Superintelligence Labs research division. The deal is part of a broader industry sprint into humanoid robotics, where forecasts range wildly from Goldman Sachs' $38B by 2035 to Morgan Stanley's $5T by 2050. Meta has now made multiple robotics bets in quick succession as it races to compete in physical AI.

title: Legal AI startup Legora hits $5.6B valuation
summary: Legora has reached a $5.6 billion valuation, intensifying its rivalry with Harvey in the fast-growing legal AI sector. The milestone comes as law firms and enterprise legal teams race to adopt AI-powered drafting and research tools. The competition between Legora and Harvey is shaping up to be one of the defining startup battles of 2026.

title: Anduril raises ~$4B at a $60B valuation
summary: Defense tech giant Anduril is closing a roughly $4 billion round led by Andreessen Horowitz and Thrive Capital, valuing the company at $60 billion. The raise cements Anduril's position as the dominant private player in AI-powered defense infrastructure. It also reflects how national security spending is increasingly funneling into AI-native startups rather than legacy contractors.

title: Y Combinator alum Skio exits for $105M on just $8M raised
summary: Skio, a subscription commerce startup that went through Y Combinator, sold for $105 million in cash despite having raised only $8 million — a rare capital-efficient exit in a market obsessed with mega-rounds. The founder confirmed the deal publicly, making it an instant case study in lean startup strategy. It stands out sharply against the billion-dollar raises dominating the AI headlines this week.

title: Musk's courtroom week against OpenAI went sideways
summary: Elon Musk took the stand in his lawsuit against OpenAI and reportedly spent much of the week arguing with lawyers — including his own — and shifting his account of events. Commentators at the Vergecast described him as unlikely to sway a jury that may have already needed heavy persuading. If Musk can't make his version of OpenAI's origins stick, the legal pressure shifts back to the company and the fight moves to documentary evidence.

title: Pentagon cuts Anthropic, calls it a supply chain risk
summary: The Defense Department has designated Anthropic a supply chain risk and barred its products from classified use, a notable reversal after the company had previously worked with the Pentagon. Anthropic had refused to loosen red lines on mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons, and after its products were banned it sued and won a temporary injunction. The DoD meanwhile signed classified AI deals with OpenAI, xAI, and Palantir.

title: Dark money campaign pays influencers to push pro-US AI talking points
summary: Wired reports that Build American AI, a dark money group tied to a super PAC called Leading the Future and backed by tech figures, is paying creators thousands of dollars per video to promote American AI and frame China as a threat. The campaign uses lifestyle influencers to launder policy messaging as organic content. It raises sharp questions about transparency in AI policy debates happening on social media.

title: xAI sues Colorado over its AI Act; DOJ joins in
summary: xAI filed suit in a Colorado federal court arguing the Colorado AI Act violates the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment, and the DOJ has moved to intervene in support of xAI's position. Colorado has agreed to a temporary stay on enforcement while the case proceeds. The case is shaping up as a key test of whether states can regulate AI discrimination without running afoul of federal constitutional limits.

title: South Korea moves to label all AI-generated media
summary: South Korea is finalizing amendments that would require AI-generated photos and videos to carry clear labels, while extending compliance obligations across the full content distribution chain — not just AI developers. Authorities would gain faster tools to block manipulated content, with tougher financial penalties for violations. The framework targets fake celebrity endorsements and synthetic personas in advertising, with ripple effects for any global brand using Korean IP.

title: ChatGPT Go launches worldwide
summary: OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT Go globally — a budget tier sitting between Free and Plus that bundles unlimited GPT-5.3 Instant chats, extended image generation, file uploads, and a larger memory window. The tier is explicitly designed to pull in price-sensitive users, and OpenAI has flagged it may eventually carry ads. Enterprise customers retain the option to set Go-grade models as their default routing choice.

title: GPT-5.4 Thinking lands, mini fallback quietly added
summary: OpenAI's model changelog shows GPT-5.4 Thinking shipped in early March as the single flagship combining reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows. The companion GPT-5.4 mini was introduced in mid-March as an automatic fallback when rate limits are hit, and will not appear as a selectable model option within 30 days. The previous GPT-5 Thinking mini is being deprecated on the same timeline.

title: FLUX 2 family brings sub-second generation and 10-image blending
summary: Black Forest Labs' second-generation FLUX lineup is now available via Replicate, spanning Max (highest fidelity, hex-color control, 8-reference character consistency), Pro (structured JSON prompting, multi-reference editing), and Klein-4B (sub-second generation from a 4B-parameter distilled model). Editing tools including Fill, Depth, and Canny round out the suite for inpainting, retexturing, and style transfer.

title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron agentic datasets on Hugging Face
summary: NVIDIA published a new collection on Hugging Face under the Nemotron Agentic & Tool-Use banner, providing datasets specifically built for function calling, multi-step agent tasks, terminal use, and software-engineering workflows. Separately, NVIDIA also announced the Ising model family aimed at using AI to advance practical quantum computing.

title: Google Gemini becomes Kevin Pietersen's cricket co-creator
summary: Google India announced a partnership with cricket icon Kevin Pietersen in which Gemini serves as the creative backbone of his new YouTube series The Switch — generating player cards, composing match anthems, building quizzes, and distilling complex stats for global audiences. The series drops twice weekly starting May 4, featuring an extensive lineup of international cricket stars.

title: Anthropic may close $50B round at $900B valuation within days
summary: Anthropic has asked investors to submit allocations within 48 hours for what could be a $50B fundraise, with pre-emptive offers landing in the $850B–$900B valuation range, according to TechCrunch sources. If it closes at the top of that range it would be among the largest private company fundraises in history, making Anthropic worth roughly as much as Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley combined.

title: David Silver's Ineffable Intelligence raises $1.1B on day one
summary: Ineffable Intelligence, a British AI lab founded just months ago by DeepMind legend David Silver — the researcher behind AlphaGo — has secured $1.1B in funding at a $5.1B valuation. The lab's thesis is that AI should be able to learn powerful representations without relying on human-labeled data, a direct challenge to the dominant RLHF paradigm.

title: 137 Ventures raises $700M to back SpaceX, Anduril-style growth bets
summary: SpaceX-backer 137 Ventures closed over $700M across two new growth-stage funds, doubling down on the defense-tech and deep-tech companies that defined its first vintage. The firm's portfolio includes SpaceX, Anduril, and Hadrian, and the new capital will target similar companies at later stages before IPO.

title: BMW i Ventures launches $300M fund for agentic and physical AI
summary: BMW i Ventures unveiled its third fund at $300M, bringing total capital under management to $1.1B and signaling the auto industry's conviction that agentic AI will reshape manufacturing and supply chains. The fund targets early-stage through Series B startups in North America and Europe working on physical AI, advanced materials, and industrial software.

title: Skio sells for $105M after raising just $8M — a rare clean exit
summary: Y Combinator alum Skio, a subscription commerce platform, was acquired for $105M in an all-cash deal despite having raised only $8M in outside funding, making it one of the more capital-efficient exits in recent memory. The founder confirmed the sale price publicly, offering a counterpoint to the mega-round frenzy dominating AI headlines this week.

title: Connecticut passes sweeping AI bill; Florida's collapses
summary: Connecticut's SB 5 — covering frontier models, chatbots, employment decisions, and content provenance — cleared the legislature and Governor Lamont says he will sign it, marking the state's third attempt after two prior vetoes. Meanwhile Florida's special session ended in failure: the Senate passed an AI Bill of Rights in hours, but the House killed it immediately, leaving Governor DeSantis' signature AI initiative dead for this session.

title: Colorado moves to gut its own AI Act
summary: Senate Majority Leader Robert Rodriguez introduced SB 189, a bill to repeal and replace Colorado's landmark AI Act with a disclosure-only regime, stripping away the algorithmic-impact assessments and high-risk-use restrictions that made the original law controversial. The bill is the product of Governor Polis' own workgroup and must pass before the legislature closes May 13.

title: DOJ joins xAI in fighting Colorado's existing AI Act in court
summary: The Department of Justice filed a motion to intervene in xAI's federal lawsuit challenging the Colorado AI Act, arguing the law violates the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. The move signals that the Trump administration is willing to deploy federal legal resources to block state-level AI regulation, a precedent with significant implications for the patchwork of bills advancing in over a dozen states.

title: Musk's $130B OpenAI lawsuit hits day one in court
summary: Elon Musk took the stand in his $130B lawsuit against OpenAI, arguing that CEO Sam Altman effectively converted a charitable organization for private gain and that allowing it would undermine American philanthropic structures. OpenAI's defense framed the suit as sour grapes from a founder who left and watched the company succeed, with hundreds of pages of private messages set to become public over the coming month.

title: Google signs classified Pentagon AI deal despite 600-employee revolt
summary: Google finalized a classified AI contract with the Pentagon the same week more than 600 employees published an open letter demanding leadership reject military AI workloads. The contract reportedly grants the Department of Defense access to Google's AI models for any lawful government purpose, with no veto rights reserved for Google — a definitive reversal of the company's 2018 no-weapons pledge, which was removed from its AI principles earlier this year.

title: GPT-5.5 lands for paid users
summary: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-5.5 Thinking and GPT-5.5 Pro to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise ChatGPT subscribers today, retiring GPT-4o and older models entirely. Context windows stretch to 400k tokens for Pro-tier Thinking users, and GPT-5.3 Instant now serves as the default fast model across all tiers. API access for GPT-5.5 is still pending, with OpenAI citing additional safety reviews before a wider release.

title: FLUX 2 brings sub-second images and 10-reference blending
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 family is now fully available via Replicate's API, spanning FLUX.2 Max for premium product photography, a Pro tier with structured JSON prompting, and FLUX.2 Klein — a 4-billion-parameter model distilled for sub-second inference on consumer hardware. New editing tools like Fill, Depth, and Canny handle inpainting, retexturing, and sketch-to-image workflows. The suite supports up to 10 reference images for multi-image blending, a significant leap for character and product consistency.

title: Runway Gen-4.5 tops video benchmarks as the field explodes
summary: Replicate's image-to-video collection now ranks Runway Gen-4.5 number one on the Artificial Analysis text-to-video benchmark, with Google's Veo 3.1 and ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 close behind. Veo 3.1 adds native audio — dialogue, sound effects, and ambient soundscapes — while Seedance 2.0 accepts up to nine reference images, three video clips, and three audio files in a single prompt. The pace of new model launches has made production-ready video generation a commodity API rather than a research demo.

title: Google opens Play Accelerator India for AI-powered startups
summary: Google has opened applications for the third cohort of Google Play Accelerator India, an equity-free three-month program offering mentorship, technical audits, and AI integration support to Indian app and game startups. Applications close June 1, with the program kicking off in July and a demo day set for November 2026. The initiative targets builders working on AI-native mobile products for a market that now has over 700 million smartphone users.

title: Suno eyes $5B+ valuation in new round
summary: AI music generation startup Suno is approaching the close of a funding round that would push its valuation above $5 billion, Axios reports. The company has become one of the most-used generative audio platforms since launching, competing with Udio and a growing field of music AI tools. The raise would cement Suno as one of the most highly valued AI-native consumer startups outside of the coding and enterprise categories.

title: Anduril closes in on $60B raise led by a16z and Thrive
summary: Defense-tech giant Anduril is finalizing a roughly $4 billion funding round that would value the company at $60 billion, with Andreessen Horowitz and Thrive Capital leading, according to The Information. A third investor is notable for the size of its check, though not yet named. The round reflects sustained investor appetite for AI-driven defense and autonomous systems as global defense budgets expand.

title: Starcloud targets $2.2B valuation for orbital data centers
summary: Two-year-old startup Starcloud, which is building data centers in orbit, is in talks to raise at least $200 million at a $2.2 billion post-money valuation — doubling its valuation from a $170 million round just one month ago. SpaceX's interest in the company has stirred additional investor attention as the space-compute category heats up. The raise is part of a broader wave of infrastructure bets tied to the assumption that terrestrial data center capacity will be a bottleneck for AI scaling.

title: Linkerbot doubles to $6B valuation on robotic hand demand
summary: Chinese robotics startup Linkerbot, the global market leader in dexterous robotic hands for humanoid robots, is seeking a $6 billion valuation in its next financing round — double the valuation it achieved in a round that just closed. The company's hands are increasingly being integrated into humanoid robot platforms from manufacturers competing to build general-purpose labor robots. Demand from automotive, logistics, and electronics assembly customers is driving the rapid re-rating.

title: Reserv lands $125M from KKR to automate insurance claims
summary: Reserv, an AI-driven insurance claims platform, announced a $125 million Series C led by KKR, targeting the slow-moving property and casualty claims market with automated workflows. The raise underscores continued investor conviction in vertical AI for regulated industries, where legacy processes remain largely manual. Reserv's technology handles claims analysis end-to-end, reducing cycle times and adjuster workload.

title: xAI sues Colorado, DOJ piles on, judge freezes enforcement
summary: xAI filed suit against Colorado's AI Act alleging First Amendment and equal protection violations, and the Department of Justice quickly moved to intervene — on xAI's side. A federal judge then approved a joint motion by xAI and the Colorado Attorney General to stay enforcement while the law is revised, marking the first time the federal government has actively backed a private company in blocking a state AI law. Colorado is now rewriting the Act to strip its algorithmic discrimination provisions, though legal observers note the revisions don't resolve all of xAI's constitutional claims.

title: EU AI Act enforcement begins August 2026 — and most firms aren't ready
summary: Starting this August, organizations operating in Europe must classify their AI systems by risk level, conduct red-team adversarial testing, and publish transparency reports — or face fines of up to 7% of global turnover, higher than GDPR penalties. High-risk applications in employment, credit, education, and public services face the strictest scrutiny, including mandatory post-market monitoring. Legal experts warn that many mid-size firms are still behind on compliance, particularly on the red-team testing requirement, which demands documented and regulator-reviewable adversarial testing.

title: Trump's AI order is freezing state legislatures — Congress steps in
summary: Virginia's General Assembly left multiple AI protection bills on the table after Trump's December executive order threatened to strip states of over $800 million in broadband funding if they passed 'onerous AI laws.' Bills covering companion chatbot harms to minors, AI in insurance claims, and mental health AI were all stalled or deferred to study committees. In response, Virginia's congressional delegation — including Sen. Mark Warner and Rep. Morgan Griffith — are advancing federal measures to fill the gaps, including the bipartisan GUARD Act protecting children from AI chatbots and the Workforce Transparency Act tracking AI's employment impact.

title: China blocks Meta's $2B acquisition of agent startup Manus
summary: China's National Development and Reform Commission formally blocked Meta's $2 billion bid to acquire Manus, the Chinese AI agent startup, in what is described as the first state-level prohibition of an inbound AI acquisition by China. The decision signals Beijing's intent to keep high-value AI assets domestic as agent technology becomes a strategic priority. The move is likely to accelerate scrutiny of cross-border AI deals in both directions.

title: Qwen3.6 goes open-weight with agentic coding chops
summary: Alibaba dropped Qwen3.6 in 27B and 35B-A3B variants, with the standout feature being Thinking Preservation — the ability to retain reasoning context across conversation turns for more consistent, efficient agent workflows. The model supports a native 262K-token context window extensible to over 1 million tokens, and ships with improved tool-calling and developer role support for environments like Codex. Unsloth has already released multiple quantized builds for Apple Silicon via MLX.

title: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Nano: 3B active params, 1M context
summary: NVIDIA unveiled Nemotron 3 Nano, a hybrid Mamba-2 and Transformer MoE model with 30B total but only 3B active parameters, designed for on-device agentic tasks. It features a 1-million-token context window, toggleable reasoning mode with configurable thinking budgets, and claims up to 4× faster inference than its predecessor. The model is served via vLLM and SGLang and is part of NVIDIA's broader open-model push on Hugging Face.

title: Google Marketing Live 2026: Meridian Studio and GeoX debut
summary: At Google Marketing Live, Google announced Meridian Studio, a Google Cloud-powered enterprise platform that lets marketing teams build and manage high-volume Marketing Mix Models at scale. Alongside it, Meridian GeoX brings open-source geo-experimentation for measuring media channel performance with CFO-ready ground-truth validation. A no-code Google Tag upgrade and a new Data Manager map view round out the measurement overhaul.

title: Sierra hits $15.8B after $950M raise
summary: Agentic enterprise AI startup Sierra closed a $950 million funding round led by Tiger Global and GV, pushing its valuation up nearly 60% to $15.8 billion. The round underscores surging investor appetite for companies building autonomous AI workflows for enterprise customers. Sierra is now one of the most valuable private AI companies in the agentic space.

title: ElevenLabs crosses $500M ARR, names BlackRock and Jamie Foxx as backers
summary: Voice AI company ElevenLabs revealed the full investor roster for its February $500M Series D, including institutions BlackRock, Wellington, and D.E. Shaw alongside enterprises like NVIDIA, Salesforce, and Deutsche Telekom, plus celebrities Jamie Foxx, Eva Longoria, and Squid Game creator Hwang Dong-hyuk. The company simultaneously announced it surpassed $500M in ARR after adding $100M in net new ARR in Q1 2026 alone. A second $100M tender offer and a planned Robinhood Ventures retail investment opportunity were also disclosed.

title: CopilotKit raises $27M to wire AI agents into apps
summary: Seattle-based CopilotKit closed a $27M Series A led by Glilot Capital, NFX, and SignalFire to help developers embed app-native AI agents directly into their products. The 25-person team plans to use the capital to grow engineering and go-to-market functions. The raise reflects continued investor conviction in developer tooling for agentic AI deployment.

title: Lithosquare raises $25M to find critical metals with AI
summary: Paris-based Lithosquare secured a $25M equity seed round co-led by World Fund and Kindred Capital to use AI in accelerating the discovery of copper and other critical metal deposits globally. The startup competes in a space occupied by Kobold Metals, which raised $537M at a $3B valuation last year. Lithosquare's model charges an upfront baseline payment for exploration with outcome-based payments and eventual revenue-sharing on future mines.

title: India's Krutrim pivots from model-builder to cloud services
summary: Krutrim, India's first GenAI unicorn founded by Bhavish Aggarwal, is stepping back from its ambition to build domestic foundation models and shifting toward AI cloud services. The company posted roughly $31.5M in revenue for FY2026 — a 3× year-over-year increase — and recorded its first annual net profit with margins exceeding 10%. The pivot signals how difficult it is for regional players to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI on raw model capability.

title: Google, Microsoft, xAI sign pre-release government review deals
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation announced that Google, Microsoft, and xAI have agreed to give the government early access to AI models before public release, joining OpenAI and Anthropic in the program. The agreements were catalyzed by alarm over Anthropic's Mythos model, which cybersecurity officials say has an unprecedented ability to identify and exploit software vulnerabilities. The White House is also reportedly drafting an executive order to formalize a government AI vetting working group — a sharp reversal from Trump's day-one repeal of Biden's AI safety order.

title: Mythos rattles Washington: the model that changed the conversation
summary: Anthropic's Mythos AI system has become the unlikely catalyst for a U.S. regulatory pivot, after demonstrations showed it could autonomously identify cybersecurity weaknesses in ways that alarmed officials including White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross. The NSA is reportedly already deploying Mythos against Microsoft software to probe federal infrastructure, while the Pentagon has simultaneously moved to phase out Anthropic as a supplier — creating a paradox where the government both fears and uses the model. The dueling lawsuits between DoD and Anthropic add another layer of tension to any formal review agreement.

title: The OpenAI trial: Musk's threatening text takes center stage
summary: The Musk v. OpenAI trial continued in Oakland before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, with a court filing revealing a text Musk sent to OpenAI president Greg Brockman on April 25: "By the end of this week, you and Sam will be the most hated men in America." Musk had already testified that his company distilled OpenAI's model outputs to train Grok, and faced questions about his own 2017 attempt to convert OpenAI to a for-profit — the same act he is suing OpenAI for. Brockman is expected to testify this week.

title: OPM goes all-in: five LLMs on every federal desk
summary: Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor revealed that OPM has deployed five separate LLMs on employees' computers, claiming this puts the agency in the top fraction of federal AI adoption. An AI ambassador program now covers more than 10% of OPM's 2,000 employees, with a mandate to replace routinized tasks rather than eliminate jobs outright. All models are FedRAMP-approved versions with PII and security rules baked in, and employees are required to log AI use in official records for FOIA purposes.

title: GPT-5.5 ships to paid ChatGPT users
summary: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-5.5 today for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers in ChatGPT and Codex. The new Thinking tier claims to cut hallucinations by over half and handles multi-step tasks — spreadsheets, frontend code, advanced math — far better than its predecessors. API access is coming soon but isn't live yet, as OpenAI says it requires additional safety work at scale.

title: xAI retiring eight Grok models on May 15
summary: xAI's API docs confirm that eight models — including grok-4-fast variants, grok-3, grok-code-fast-1, and grok-imagine-image-pro — will be switched off on May 15 at noon PT. Developers are being pushed toward the newer Grok 4.3 lineup, which xAI says excels at agentic reasoning and tool use. A migration guide is live now.

title: FLUX 2 brings sub-second image gen to production apps
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 family is now fully available on Replicate, headlined by FLUX.2 Klein 4B — a 4B-parameter distilled model that generates images in under a second, suited for real-time applications and consumer hardware. The flagship FLUX.2 Max supports up to eight reference images for character consistency and precise hex-level color control. Replicate recommends FLUX.2 Pro as the practical default for most production use cases.

title: Google pumps $10M more into Asia-Pacific AI education
summary: Google expanded its AI Opportunity Fund for Asia-Pacific today with an additional $10 million, bringing total regional commitment to $37 million. The program targets 4.7 million learners and educators across 19 countries, including Indonesia, with structured AI learning pathways and a new AI Playbook for Educators. It partners with over 20 local organizations to align training with national digital agendas.

title: QuTwo valued at $380M on a scrappy angel round
summary: Finnish AI lab QuTwo, founded by former AMD Silo AI CEO Peter Sarlin, raised a €25M angel round at a €325M ($380M) post-money valuation. Backers include Yuri Milner, Xavier Niel, Supercell's Ilkka Paananen, and Hugging Face's Thomas Wolf. The company already has $23M in committed revenue from design partnerships including Zalando, and Sarlin says the modest round size is intentional — less pressure, more focus.

title: Natural raises $30M for AI-native payments
summary: Natural, a startup building payment infrastructure for AI agents, is closing a $30M Series A at a $150M post-money valuation, per Axios Pro. The raise signals growing investor conviction that autonomous agents will need their own financial rails — not just API keys. Terms were still being finalized at time of reporting.

title: Bessemer backs AI architecture platform Illoca at seed
summary: Illoca, which brings AI-assisted design tools to architects, raised $13M in seed funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners. The raise is an early signal that AEC (architecture, engineering, construction) software is becoming a serious vertical for AI investment. Details on the product roadmap were not disclosed.

title: Public buys Treasury App in AI investing push
summary: Brokerage platform Public acquired Treasury App, an investment education startup, in a move to deepen its AI-powered financial guidance offering. The deal was confirmed exclusively to Axios by Public COO Stephen Sikes, though financial terms were not disclosed. Public has been positioning itself as an AI-first retail investing platform.

title: CellCentric banks $220M for myeloma drug, eyes IPO
summary: Biotech firm CellCentric closed a $220M Series D led by Venrock, with co-investors including Pfizer and the American Cancer Society's BrightEdge fund, to advance its multiple myeloma treatment into late-stage trials. The company is now approaching a $1B valuation and has enough runway through 2029. CEO Will West told Axios a potential IPO is under consideration for the coming year.

title: Trump's government will preview AI models before launch
summary: The US government announced Tuesday that it has secured pre-deployment review agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI — a sharp U-turn from the Trump administration's earlier hands-off posture. The Commerce Department's CAISI will conduct evaluations of frontier models before public release. The direct catalyst, officials and reporters confirm, was Anthropic's Mythos model, which the NSA is now testing after concerns it can autonomously exploit zero-day software vulnerabilities.

title: White House drafts executive order for AI review board
summary: Politico reports the White House is drafting a 16-page executive order that would create a working group of tech executives and government officials to review frontier AI models, address cybersecurity risks from open-weight models, and potentially involve the intelligence community. The apparent reversal is alarming some laissez-faire Silicon Valley voices who worry it will slow innovation relative to China. The draft remains in flux.

title: Connecticut passes landmark AI workplace transparency law
summary: Connecticut's legislature passed the AI Responsibility and Transparency Act 131-17 in the House and 32-4 in the Senate, and Governor Lamont confirmed he will sign it. The law requires employers to disclose when AI is used in hiring, promotion, or termination decisions, and crucially mandates that any federal WARN-notice layoff disclose whether AI drove the job cuts — a provision taking effect October 1, 2026. It directly amends anti-discrimination law to prevent AI tools from serving as a legal shield against bias claims.

title: Federal court freezes Colorado's AI Act weeks before deadline
summary: A federal court paused enforcement of Colorado's sweeping AI Act on April 27, just weeks before its June 30 effective date, after a leading AI developer filed a constitutional challenge and the DOJ intervened — marking the federal government's first litigation move against a state AI law. Colorado's legislature is now racing to amend or replace the statute before its session ends May 13. Even with enforcement frozen, legal experts warn employers still face liability under existing anti-discrimination and privacy laws.

title: Musk vs. Altman trial continues to heat up
summary: The courtroom battle between Elon Musk and Sam Altman over OpenAI's mission and governance continued Wednesday, with Musk's legal team arguing the company abandoned its nonprofit mandate in pursuit of profit. Altman's side contends the commercial evolution was necessary to compete at the frontier. Legal observers say the outcome could set major precedents for how AI companies are structured and governed globally.

title: GPT-5.5 lands for paying ChatGPT users
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro today for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers inside ChatGPT and Codex, with a 256K context window on the Thinking variant. The rollout is gradual and API access is coming soon, pending additional safety measures for scale. Enterprise workspaces can also redirect Auto routing to the cheaper Thinking mini to save credits.

title: ChatGPT moves into your spreadsheets
summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets is now available globally to Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu, and K-12 users as a sidebar add-in. It can build, update, and explain multi-tab spreadsheets with complex formulas using natural language. Business and Enterprise customers get a free preview through June 2, 2026, after which credits and usage terms apply.

title: xAI sunsets Grok 4 fast models on May 15
summary: xAI announced it will retire eight Grok models — including grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, grok-4-fast-non-reasoning, grok-code-fast-1, and grok-imagine-image-pro — effective May 15 at noon PT. Any API requests to these endpoints after that date will fail, and developers are urged to migrate now. xAI hinted at exciting new model releases in the coming weeks.

title: FLUX 2 brings sub-second image gen to production apps
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 model family — including Max, Pro, Flex, and the 4B Klein variant — is now available via Replicate's API with structured JSON prompting, hex color control, and support for up to 10 reference images. The Klein 4B model generates images in under one second, making it viable for real-time applications. FLUX.2 Pro handles both generation and editing at a lower price point than Max.

title: Moonshot AI raises $2B at a $20B valuation
summary: China's Moonshot AI closed a $2 billion funding round valuing the company at $20 billion, riding surging demand for open-source frontier models. The company's flagship Kimi model features a 1-trillion-parameter architecture, a 262K context window, and capabilities spanning vision, tool use, and autonomous software engineering. The raise signals that Chinese AI labs are increasingly competitive with their U.S. counterparts on both capability and capital.

title: DeepSeek eyes $45B valuation in debut funding round
summary: DeepSeek, the Chinese AI lab that stunned the industry in early 2025 with its highly efficient models, is in discussions for its first-ever investment round at a potential $45 billion valuation. The lab rose to prominence by training frontier-level models at a fraction of the compute cost of U.S. competitors like OpenAI and Google. A deal at that valuation would make it one of the most valuable AI startups globally without a prior institutional round.

title: Quantum Motion raises $160M Series C
summary: UK-based quantum computing startup Quantum Motion closed a $160 million Series C co-led by DCVC and Mundi Ventures, one of the largest European quantum fundraises to date. The round included the British Business Bank, Firgun Ventures, Oxford Science Enterprises, and strategic investors Bosch Ventures and Porsche. The raise comes as European quantum startups secured €1.6B in 2025, more than doubling the prior year's total.

title: SAP pays $1.16B for 18-month-old German AI lab
summary: SAP is acquiring Prior Labs, a German AI startup, in a deal valued at $1.16 billion — extraordinary for a company less than two years old. The acquisition signals SAP's aggressive push to embed advanced AI into its enterprise software stack. SAP also announced it is restricting its customers' AI agents to a select list of approved providers, including Nvidia's NemoClaw.

title: a16z leads $16M seed in Stockholm AI startup Pit
summary: Pit, a Stockholm-based AI-native startup co-founded by the team behind scooter company Voi, raised a $16 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz with participation from Lakestar and angels from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Deel, and Revolut. The round also saw backing from Swedish industrial families Stena and Lundin. Details on Pit's product remain sparse, but the caliber of backers signals high expectations.

title: White House eyes pre-release AI model approval
summary: The Trump administration is drafting an executive order that could require government testing and sign-off before powerful AI models are released to the public, with one official comparing it to FDA drug approval. The proposal emerged after meetings about Anthropic's Mythos model and its potential cybersecurity implications. Free-market groups and industry advisers are pushing back hard, warning that any veto power over model releases could violate First Amendment principles.

title: DOJ sides with Colorado against xAI in landmark AI lawsuit
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice intervened in xAI's lawsuit challenging Colorado's high-risk AI law, arguing the legislation violates the 14th Amendment's equal protection clause. xAI has separately raised First Amendment concerns about the law, which takes effect June 30 and requires developers to guard against discriminatory outcomes in employment, housing, healthcare, and financial services. The DOJ's entry into the case significantly raises the legal stakes for state-level AI regulation nationwide.

title: House introduces sweeping bipartisan AI bill
summary: Representatives Ted Lieu and Jay Obernolte introduced the American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Act, a package combining more than 20 bipartisan proposals drawn from the 2024 AI Task Force report. The bill covers AI standards through NIST, federal procurement reform, workforce development, and safeguards against AI-enabled crime and synthetic media. Connecticut also passed its own comprehensive AI bill this week, covering employment decisions, youth protections, and a regulatory sandbox.

title: South Africa pulls AI policy over fake citations
summary: South Africa's government withdrew its draft national AI policy after officials discovered the document contained fictitious references that appeared to be AI-generated. Communications Minister Solly Malatsi confirmed the sources were included without proper verification, an embarrassing episode for a policy meant to govern AI use. The draft had proposed creating a National AI Commission and an AI Regulatory Authority; no revised timeline has been announced.

title: Chinese court: firing workers for AI replacement is illegal
summary: The Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court ruled that employers cannot terminate workers solely because AI has automated their role, ordering compensation for a quality-assurance employee who was fired after his LLM-output review job was automated away. The employer had offered a demotion with a pay cut, which the worker refused before being let go under a staffing-reduction rationale. The ruling sets a significant precedent as AI-driven workforce displacement accelerates across China.

title: ChatGPT moves into your spreadsheets
summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets, a sidebar-native AI that can build, edit, and explain complex multi-tab spreadsheets in plain language. It's available to all plan tiers globally, with Free and Go users getting limited access. Business, Enterprise, and Edu customers get a free preview through June 2, 2026, after which usage follows their plan credits.

title: GitHub Copilot deprecates GPT-4.1, ships security upgrades
summary: GitHub's May changelog is packed: GPT-4.1 is being retired on June 1 across all Copilot experiences, and GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.2-Codex are also on the chopping block. On the upside, secret scanning via the GitHub MCP Server is now generally available, dependency scanning is in public preview, and the Rubber Duck CLI review agent now supports cross-model critic pairing.

title: FLUX 2 brings character consistency to image generation APIs
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 models are now available via Replicate's API, with the flagship flux-2-max accepting up to 8 reference images for consistent character generation across batches. The family supports precise hex-color control, cinematic keyframes, and 3D view generation. A lighter 4-billion-parameter variant, flux-2-klein-4b, supports up to 5 references for faster turnaround.

title: OpenAI hands GPT-5.5-Cyber to the US government before launch
summary: OpenAI gave CAISI early access to ChatGPT 5.5 ahead of its public release for national security testing, and is co-developing a responsible deployment strategy for GPT-5.5-Cyber — a specialized model aimed at strengthening cyber defense. The model is currently limited to a first-access group while a distribution playbook for government use is being finalized.

title: DeepSeek targets $7.35B in its first-ever funding round
summary: Founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng plans to write the single largest check in DeepSeek's debut funding round, which aims to raise up to 50 billion yuan ($7.35B). If completed, it would be the biggest funding round ever for a Chinese AI company. The raise comes as the company begins plotting its first serious revenue efforts.

title: Six-week-old ex-OpenAI startup eyes $4B valuation
summary: An unnamed startup founded by a former OpenAI researcher is already in talks to raise funding at a $4 billion valuation, according to The Information. Nvidia's aggressive investment spree in GPU-heavy AI startups is drawing in traditional VCs, enabling brand-new companies to run back-to-back fundraises within weeks of founding.

title: Lime files for IPO after years of scooter scaling
summary: Lime, the Uber-backed micromobility company known for its electric scooters and bikes, has filed for an IPO. The filing marks a major milestone for a company that survived the pandemic-era collapse of shared mobility and has since expanded globally. No pricing details have been disclosed yet.

title: Anti-drone AI startup Allen Control targets $2B valuation
summary: Allen Control Systems, a four-year-old defense-tech startup building an autonomous weapons station capable of shooting down drones, is raising roughly $200M at a pre-money valuation of $2 billion. The raise reflects surging investor appetite for AI-powered defense hardware as drone warfare escalates globally.

title: Develo raises $14M for pediatrics-focused medical records
summary: Develo, which builds electronic medical records tailored specifically for pediatric practices, closed a $14M Series A led by Blueprint Equity. The raise reflects continued investor interest in vertical-specific health tech as generic EMR platforms struggle to serve specialty care workflows.

title: Google, Microsoft, and xAI agree to pre-launch government AI testing
summary: All three companies signed new agreements with the Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) to submit their models for safety evaluations covering cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons risks before public release. The deals represent a notable pivot for the Trump administration, which has otherwise championed deregulation. The Pentagon confirmed it will 'never again' rely on a single AI provider, framing the agreements as a counterstatement to its ongoing dispute with Anthropic.

title: White House backs away from mandatory AI pre-release vetting
summary: After reports of a potential executive order requiring government review of frontier AI models before launch, the White House clarified it favors voluntary industry partnerships over mandatory oversight — citing concerns that approval gates could hand market advantages to whichever lab clears the process first. Behind the scenes, officials are still discussing whether the intelligence community should pre-assess powerful models to exploit capabilities before adversaries do.

title: EU strikes provisional deal to water down AI Act timelines
summary: EU lawmakers and member states reached a provisional agreement to push back key AI Act deadlines: standalone high-risk AI systems now face a December 2027 compliance date, and AI embedded in regulated products gets until August 2028. The deal also extends simplification measures to small mid-caps and reinforces the AI Office's enforcement powers. The text still needs formal endorsement from both the Council and Parliament.

title: US and China weigh formal AI governance talks
summary: Washington and Beijing are considering launching official discussions on AI governance and risk — including concerns about erratic model behavior and autonomous weapons — potentially at an upcoming summit. The move would mark a rare diplomatic thaw in the tech rivalry between the two countries and signal that both sides recognize some coordination on frontier AI may be unavoidable.

title: Take It Down Act goes into effect May 19 — deepfakes included
summary: The federal Take It Down Act (TiDA) takes effect on May 19, 2026, making it illegal to knowingly publish or threaten to publish non-consensual intimate images — including AI-generated deepfakes. Covered platforms will be required to remove such content within 48 hours of a victim's notice. It's the first major federal law directly targeting AI-generated sexual imagery.

title: ChatGPT moves into your spreadsheets
summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets is now available globally across all plan tiers, living as a sidebar inside your spreadsheets. It can build, update, explain, and summarize workbooks using natural language — including large multi-tab files with complex formulas. Business and Enterprise customers get a free preview through June 2, after which credits and usage terms apply.

title: FLUX 2 lands on Replicate with character consistency
