summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 Max is now available via Replicate's API, supporting up to 8 reference images to maintain character consistency across image batches. The model targets product photography, cinematic frames, and precise color control. A lighter 4B variant, FLUX 2 Klein, supports up to 5 references for faster generation.

title: Hugging Face ships a linter for Transformers model files
summary: Hugging Face quietly released mlinter, a linting tool designed specifically for Transformers modeling files. The tool aims to catch common errors and enforce consistency in model code before they ship. It's a small but telling sign that AI model development tooling is maturing toward software engineering best practices.

title: DeepSeek targets $7.35B in its first-ever funding round
summary: DeepSeek is planning to raise up to 50 billion yuan — roughly $7.35 billion — in its first external funding round, which would make it the largest raise by a Chinese AI company ever. Founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng is expected to personally write the largest check into the round. The move signals DeepSeek is shifting from a scrappy cost-cutter to a well-capitalized contender.

title: Six-week-old OpenAI spinout eyes $4B valuation
summary: A startup founded by a former OpenAI researcher is already in talks to raise funding at a $4 billion valuation — despite being just six weeks old. The raise reflects a broader trend of Nvidia's equity investments in AI chip-heavy startups igniting VC interest and enabling back-to-back rounds at breakneck speed. Anthropic and OpenAI now face well-funded new challengers launching almost monthly.

title: Nvidia has committed $40B to equity AI deals in 2026 alone
summary: Nvidia's equity investment spree has already hit $40 billion this year, spanning a wide range of AI startups that rely on its chips. The strategy is effectively turbocharging valuations across the sector by signaling Nvidia's blessing to traditional VCs. Critics are asking whether this creates a self-reinforcing cycle that inflates both chip demand and startup prices.

title: Ramp in talks to reach $40B+ valuation
summary: Fintech darling Ramp is reportedly in talks for a new funding round that would push its valuation above $40 billion, just six months after it was valued at $32 billion. The jump reflects surging enterprise demand for AI-powered spend management and cost automation tools. Ramp has been aggressively integrating AI into its core product over the past year.

title: Anti-drone AI startup targets $2B valuation
summary: Allen Control Systems, a four-year-old startup building an autonomous weapons station capable of shooting down drones, is seeking roughly $200 million in new funding at a $2 billion pre-money valuation. The raise reflects surging defense and national security interest in AI-powered counter-drone technology. The deal would mark a major step up for the company as drone threats escalate globally.

title: White House blinks on mandatory AI model vetting
summary: After NEC Director Kevin Hassett floated the idea of FDA-style mandatory reviews for frontier AI models, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles quickly walked it back, posting that the administration favors empowering innovators over bureaucracy. Tech lobbyists say the reversal was welcome but left them more confused about the White House's actual plan. The episode exposed real disorganization at the top of AI policy inside the Trump administration.

title: Big AI labs sign voluntary testing deal with federal government
summary: Google, Microsoft, xAI, Anthropic, and OpenAI have all agreed to pre-release model testing through CAISI, NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation, covering cyber, biological, and chemical risk evaluations. The deal is the Trump administration's preferred alternative to binding regulation, keeping oversight voluntary and industry-led. Advocates say it's a meaningful first step; critics argue it lacks teeth for high-risk systems.

title: Florida moves on AI 'bill of rights' targeting chatbots and minors
summary: A special session of the Florida legislature has begun considering an AI bill of rights championed by Governor Ron DeSantis, focused on creating guardrails around chatbots to protect children. Industry groups and the Trump White House oppose the measure, arguing it conflicts with the federal push for uniform national standards. The bill puts Florida in the same reform camp as Colorado, which has its own AI law taking effect June 30.

title: DOJ backs xAI's lawsuit against Colorado's AI Act
summary: The Department of Justice has filed a motion to intervene in xAI's lawsuit against the Colorado attorney general, supporting the company's argument that the state's AI non-discrimination law is unconstitutional. The move marks a significant escalation of the federal government's posture against state-level AI regulation. Colorado's law is scheduled to take effect on June 30, 2026.

title: 30 nations gather in Seoul to propose global frontier model registry
summary: Representatives from 30 countries met at the 2026 AI Safety Summit in Seoul to discuss an international registry for frontier AI models, requiring developers above a certain compute threshold to disclose training data and internal safety evaluations. The proposal aims to prevent any country or lab from building a potentially dangerous system entirely without accountability. A parallel consortium also proposed a universal watermarking standard for AI-generated content to combat voice cloning scams.

title: ChatGPT moves into your spreadsheet
summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets, a sidebar-native AI experience available to nearly all plan tiers — from Free to Enterprise. It can build spreadsheets from scratch, explain formulas, and make edits via natural language. Business and Enterprise customers get a free preview through June 2, 2026, after which usage counts against plan credits.

title: GPT-5.4 mini rolls out as a fallback model
summary: OpenAI has deployed GPT-5.4 mini inside ChatGPT, but it won't appear as a selectable option in the model picker. Instead, it acts as a fallback for Plus, Pro, and paid users who hit their GPT-5.4 Thinking usage limits, keeping reasoning capabilities available during heavy use sessions. Free and Go users can access it via the 'Thinking' menu toggle.

title: FLUX 2 arrives with 8-reference character consistency
summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 2 Max model now accepts up to eight reference images and maintains character consistency across image batches, making it useful for product photography, e-commerce, and cinematic keyframe generation. A lighter sibling, FLUX 2 Klein 4B, supports up to five references and generates images faster. Both are available via Replicate's API.

title: Anthropic's Mythos finds bugs in Firefox
summary: Anthropic's ultra-powerful Mythos AI model was used by Mozilla to identify high-severity security bugs in Firefox, marking one of the first high-profile cases of a frontier model being applied directly to open-source software vulnerability discovery. The news follows Mythos's debut, which prompted the federal CIO to convene discussions about releasing a modified government version.

title: Ramp eyes $40B+ valuation in fresh talks
summary: Fintech darling Ramp is in advanced discussions for a new funding round that would value the company at more than $40 billion — up from $32 billion just six months ago. The rapid valuation climb reflects sustained investor appetite for AI-powered financial tools even as broader markets remain choppy.

title: Kalshi doubles to $22B in five months
summary: Prediction market platform Kalshi has doubled its valuation to $22 billion just five months after its last raise, signaling strong momentum for regulated event-contract markets. The company has benefited from surging user interest in political and economic prediction markets as U.S. policy uncertainty climbs.

title: Nvidia pours $40B into AI equity deals this year
summary: Nvidia has already committed $40 billion to equity investments in AI companies in 2026, cementing its role not just as a chip supplier but as a major strategic investor across the AI stack. The scale of the bets underscores how chipmakers are racing to lock in relationships with frontier labs and cloud infrastructure players before the market consolidates.

title: $340M: tech's Q1 lobbying splurge
summary: Technology and telecom interests spent more than $340 million on federal lobbying in just the first quarter of 2026 — more than the entire 2022 midterm cycle. OpenAI, Meta, and Coinbase have each more than doubled their in-house lobbying staff since January, with a new industry group called the American Innovation Compact running TV ads framing AI oversight as a threat to U.S. competitiveness.

title: Congress closes in on a national AI framework
summary: Reps. Lieu and Obernolte introduced the American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Act, a consolidated bipartisan bill that pulls together provisions from prior legislation and the 2024 AI Task Force report. Separately, a White House official signaled states may retain some AI regulatory authority — particularly on child safety and government procurement — while a national baseline takes shape.

title: Pentagon breaks up with single-vendor AI
summary: The Pentagon's Under Secretary for Research and Engineering declared the Defense Department will 'never again' rely on a single AI provider, announcing new flexible contracts with multiple Big Tech firms as a direct counterstatement to its ongoing conflict with Anthropic. The Commerce Department's AI safety center is simultaneously opening classified model evaluations to Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI.

title: AI regulation: when, not if
summary: A new analysis finds that 1,561 AI-related bills have been introduced in U.S. states so far in 2026 — a record — even as federal legislation stalls across fragmented committee jurisdictions. Polling shows 68% of voters now call tech regulation a top priority, up from 41% in 2024, and more Americans worry federal AI rules won't go far enough than worry they'll go too far.

title: GUARD Act sparks First Amendment fight
summary: The Senate Judiciary Committee's passage of the GUARD Act — targeting AI chatbots with age verification, content mandates, and criminal penalties up to $100,000 per violation — has ignited a First Amendment debate. Critics argue the bill forces companies to suppress constitutionally protected speech and compels government-scripted disclosures in every user interaction, a model they say Congress cannot constitutionally impose.

title: Google Finance goes AI-native across Europe
summary: Google's redesigned Finance product is rolling out across Europe with full local-language support, bringing AI-powered stock research, Deep Search for complex market questions, and live earnings calls with synchronized transcripts. New charting tools let users view technical indicators and tap price-chart moments to understand why a stock moved. Real-time commodity and crypto data round out the upgrade.

title: FLUX.2 Max raises the bar for product photography via API
summary: Replicate's FLUX.2 Max now supports up to eight reference images for character and brand consistency across batches, plus hex-code color control for precise brand matching. The model handles cinematic keyframes, 3D view generation, and polished product shots transformed from raw phone photos. A lighter sibling, FLUX.2 Klein 4B, cuts inference time while still accepting five references.

title: GPT-5 model family reshapes ChatGPT Business tiers
summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Business and Enterprise plans have transitioned fully to the GPT-5 family, with GPT-4o retired as of early April. The new lineup splits into Instant (32K context, near-unlimited usage) and Thinking (196K context, 3,000 requests per week) modes, plus a Pro tier capped at 15 requests per month for the most compute-intensive tasks. All tiers support documents, images, CSV, and audio inputs.

title: DeepSeek chases $7.35B in its first-ever funding round
summary: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is targeting up to 50 billion yuan — roughly $7.35 billion — in its debut fundraise, which would be the largest round ever by a Chinese AI company. Founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng is expected to contribute the single biggest check. The raise comes as DeepSeek begins plotting its first serious revenue efforts after disrupting the global model market with its open-weight releases.

title: Cowboy Space lands $275M to solve the rocket shortage for orbital data centers
summary: Space infrastructure startup Cowboy Space closed a $275 million Series B at a $2 billion post-money valuation, led by Index Ventures with participation from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, IVP, Construct Capital, and SAIC. The company is betting that demand for space-based compute will outpace available launch capacity and is building the hardware to bridge that gap. The round is framed as a down payment on a much larger infrastructure build.

title: Config wins $27M seed to become the TSMC of robot training data
summary: Config, a Seoul- and San Jose-based startup building the data infrastructure layer for robotic foundation models, raised a $27 million seed led by Samsung Venture Investment at a valuation north of $200 million — bringing its total to $35 million. Strategic backers include Hyundai's ZER01NE Ventures, LG Tech Ventures, and SKT America, signaling deep buy-in from Korea's industrial giants. Covariant AI co-founder Pieter Abbeel also joined as an angel.

title: Kuaishou plans to spin off Kling AI video unit at $20B valuation
summary: Chinese social media giant Kuaishou is preparing to spin out its Kling AI video business ahead of a 2027 IPO, capitalizing on investor appetite for AI pure-plays. The company has begun pre-IPO funding talks with potential investors at a $20 billion target valuation. Kling has quickly become one of the most-watched video generation platforms globally since launching last year.

title: Fifth Dimension raises $26M to bring AI to real estate investing
summary: Real estate investment platform Fifth Dimension secured a $26 million Series A led by HV Capital, with CEO Kate Jarvis telling Axios the funds will accelerate its AI-driven deal analysis and portfolio management tools. The startup targets institutional and professional investors looking to move beyond spreadsheet-based underwriting. It joins a growing cluster of property-tech AI plays attracting early venture attention in 2026.

title: GSA draft clause could hand government ownership of AI contractors' IP
summary: The General Services Administration has circulated a draft procurement clause that would transfer ownership of any custom AI development — including fine-tuned models, configurations, and enhancements — from vendors to the federal government. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce and other industry groups warn the language is so broad it could cover embedded AI in standard commercial software, chill competition, and deter participation in federal contracts. Businesses are pushing the GSA to narrow definitions and explicitly preserve pre-existing IP rights.

title: Trump EO takes aim at state AI laws as Florida debates AI bill of rights
summary: President Trump signed an executive order targeting state-level AI legislation, attempting to preempt a patchwork of rules with federal standards — a move that faces immediate legal and political challenges. Simultaneously, Florida's legislature opened a special session on Gov. DeSantis's proposed AI bill of rights, focused on protecting minors from chatbots, which the Trump White House and industry groups both oppose. The divergence highlights a widening fault line between state ambitions and federal deregulatory instincts.

title: Google Gemini becomes football's AI sponsor
summary: Google announced Gemini as the official Technology Sponsor of the Iraq and Morocco national football teams, marking a novel sports-meets-AI marketing push across the MENA region. Fans will be able to use Gemini's text-to-image and text-to-music models to generate custom cheering visuals and team anthems. The partnership runs a series of fan activations over the next three months.

title: Isomorphic Labs lands $2.1B to build AI drugs
summary: Alphabet's DeepMind spinout Isomorphic Labs closed a $2.1 billion round led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet, Abu Dhabi's MGX, Singapore's Temasek, and the UK's Sovereign AI fund also participating. The company is betting that AI-designed molecules — built on the AlphaFold foundation — can compress the drug discovery timeline from decades to years. It's the startup's second major outside funding round.

title: Vapi hits $500M valuation after beating 40 rivals for Amazon Ring
summary: Voice AI platform Vapi raised a $50M Series B led by Peak XV Partners at a ~$500M post-money valuation, with Microsoft M12, Kleiner Perkins, and Bessemer also joining. The deal was catalyzed by Amazon Ring choosing Vapi over 40 competing vendors for its AI voice deployment. The startup is tracking healthy eight-figure ARR and has now raised $72M in total.

title: Wispr Flow in talks for $260M at $2B valuation
summary: AI voice dictation startup Wispr is in advanced talks to raise roughly $260 million led by Menlo Ventures, which would more than double its valuation to $2 billion. Wispr Flow has built a loyal following among knowledge workers who prefer dictating over typing. The deal is not yet finalized and terms could shift.

title: A-Star closes $450M Fund III with a discipline-first pitch
summary: Early-stage VC A-Star, co-founded by former Coatue investor Bennett Siegel and Julia Hartz, announced a $450 million third fund — its largest ever but deliberately far smaller than mega-funds dominating AI investing. The firm plans to back just 30–40 seed companies with $3–5M checks targeting 10%+ ownership. The fund will be deployed over roughly three years.

title: Qwen3.6 arrives with think-first coding chops
summary: Alibaba has released Qwen3.6, the first open-weight model in its 3.6 series, in 27B and 35B-A3B MoE sizes with a 262K-token context window. The model defaults to a reasoning 'thinking' mode before responding and ships with improved agentic coding, frontend workflow handling, and better tool-calling for nested objects. It supports developer roles for use in Codex and OpenCode, and can be run or fine-tuned directly in Unsloth Studio.

title: Google brings Personal Intelligence to Australia
summary: Google is expanding its Personal Intelligence feature in the Gemini app to Australian users, connecting Gmail, Google Photos, YouTube, and Search so the assistant can reason across a user's personal data. The rollout starts with AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers before reaching free accounts. Users control exactly which apps are linked, and the experience works across web, Android, and iOS.

title: Infinity-Parser2 tops document-parsing benchmarks
summary: Infly has released Infinity-Parser2-Pro and Infinity-Parser2-Flash, document understanding models that claim state-of-the-art results on olmOCR-Bench (87.6%) and ParseBench (74.3%), beating DeepSeek-OCR-2 and MinerU-2.5. The Flash variant runs 3.68x faster than its predecessor, jumping from 441 to 1,624 tokens per second. Both models are trained on a 5-million-sample synthetic dataset using a multi-task reinforcement learning approach.

title: NVIDIA drops 8M-sample open dataset for vision tasks
summary: NVIDIA has released an eight-million-sample open dataset alongside new tooling designed to accelerate OCR, image reasoning, and image and video question-answering tasks. The release is part of the Nemotron family of foundation models, which spans language, vision, retrieval, speech, and safety. The datasets and model weights are hosted publicly on Hugging Face.

title: SenseNova U1 unifies vision understanding and generation
summary: SenseTime has open-sourced SenseNova U1, a multimodal model series that handles visual understanding, reasoning, and image generation within a single architecture rather than relying on modality adapters. Two sizes are available — an 8B dense model and an A3B MoE variant — along with GGUF quantized weights for low-VRAM inference. The companion OpenClaw toolkit ships U1 as a ready-to-use agent skill with a unified tool-calling interface.

title: Isomorphic Labs banks $2.1B for AI drug discovery
summary: Isomorphic Labs, the Google-originated AI drug discovery spinout, has closed a $2.1 billion Series B. The round positions the company to scale its AlphaFold-derived platform toward clinical drug development pipelines. It is one of the largest single raises in biotech AI to date.

title: Qwen's ex-lead researcher seeks $2B valuation for new lab
summary: Junyang Lin, the former lead researcher behind Alibaba's Qwen model family, is raising several hundred million dollars for a new independent AI lab expected to be valued at around $2 billion. The discussions are ongoing, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter. Lin's exit from Alibaba follows a broader wave of top Chinese AI researchers spinning out to launch their own frontier labs.

title: White House AI policy stalls in public infighting
summary: Internal disagreements are blocking any White House executive action on frontier AI, with officials openly contradicting each other after NEC Director Kevin Hassett floated an FDA-style review process for powerful models only to be walked back by Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and former AI advisor David Sacks. The delay is compounded by Trump's upcoming Beijing summit, with industry insiders saying the administration may hold all AI policy decisions until after China talks conclude. NIST's recently announced frontier model testing agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI were quietly pulled from its website days after publication, with no official explanation.

title: GitHub Copilot picks its own model now
summary: GitHub quietly shipped auto model selection for Copilot's cloud agent, letting it choose the best available model for each task rather than relying on a user's manual pick. The Copilot CLI also expanded model support for its Rubber Duck debugging assistant. Small quality-of-life updates, but they signal a shift toward agents that manage their own tooling.

title: Google turns Gemini into a national art project
summary: Google Arts & Culture launched 'A National Portrait' at the UK's National Portrait Gallery, letting anyone 18+ submit a selfie that gets transformed into an animated charcoal-style portrait using the Gemini image model. The collective piece evolves in real time on display at the gallery through October. It's one of the more imaginative public deployments of a frontier image model to date.

title: ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets goes global
summary: OpenAI made ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets available worldwide for ChatGPT Business, giving teams a native sidebar to build, clean, and explain spreadsheets with full app and skills support. Business customers get a free preview until June 2, after which standard plan credits apply. It's a direct play for the enterprise workflow market currently dominated by Microsoft Copilot.

title: Kling Video 3.0 lands on Replicate
summary: Kling Video 3.0 is now available via Replicate, offering cinematic video generation up to 15 seconds with multi-shot control, native audio, and improved consistency. The Omni variant adds multimodal reference inputs and video editing capabilities. ByteDance's model is increasingly competitive with Sora and other frontier video generators.

title: Cerebras goes public at $40B, blows past its range
summary: Cerebras Systems priced its IPO at $185 per share — well above its initial $115–$125 range and a revised $150–$160 band — raising $5.6 billion in what is the largest IPO of the year so far. The AI chip maker's market cap at launch sits near $40B, a 73% jump from its Series H valuation just four months ago. Early backers including Foundation Capital and Fidelity are among the winners.

title: Wirestock raises $23M to feed AI labs creative data
summary: Wirestock, a platform that sources creative multi-modal data from a community of contributors, closed a $23M Series A led by Nava Ventures, with SBVP (co-founded by Sheryl Sandberg) and others participating. The company has an annual run-rate of $40M and has paid out $15M to its contributor network. As AI labs' hunger for high-quality training data grows, Wirestock is positioning itself as a premium supplier.

title: Nectar Social pulls $30M to run brand DMs with AI
summary: Nectar Social, which builds AI agents to manage brand social media accounts including direct messaging, raised a $30M Series A disclosed exclusively to Axios. The bet is that brands want personalized audience engagement at scale and will pay for AI to handle it. The round reflects growing investor appetite for vertical AI agents tackling specific marketing workflows.

title: Synthetic gets $10M from Khosla to do your startup's books
summary: Synthetic raised a $10M seed round led by Khosla Ventures to build an AI-native bookkeeping service aimed specifically at software startups. Founder Ian Crosby told Axios the company runs the entire bookkeeping process with AI, with minimal human intervention. It's a crowded space, but Khosla's backing gives the startup serious credibility.

title: Modal in talks to raise at $4.5B, up 80% from months ago
summary: Modal, which rents Nvidia GPUs and developer tooling to teams building and running AI models, is in advanced discussions to raise at a roughly $4.5B valuation — an 80% premium to its last round from just a few months prior. The surge reflects explosive demand for GPU-backed infrastructure as agent workloads scale. No close date has been announced.

title: 50 state AI law updates in one week
summary: Trackers logged 50 AI bill updates across 14 states this week alone, touching everything from landlord price-fixing algorithms and mental health chatbots to deepfake protections for K-12 students and AI companion regulation. The sheer volume underscores how state legislatures have become the de facto arena for AI governance while federal action stalls. Iowa's Conversational AI Safety Act and New York's annual AI hiring impact reporting requirement were among the notable moves.

title: Trump's EO on state AI laws faces a legal gauntlet
summary: A new CSIS podcast unpacks Trump's executive order targeting state-level AI regulations, noting that while the final version is somewhat narrowed from an earlier draft, it still faces significant legal and political headwinds. Critics argue the EO overreaches federal authority by attempting to preempt state laws. The episode also examines Meta's reliance on scam-driven ad revenue as a parallel case study in the risks of light-touch tech regulation.

title: PwC goes all-in on Claude
summary: Anthropic and PwC expanded their strategic alliance, with PwC rolling out Claude Code and Claude Cowork to its global workforce of hundreds of thousands of professionals. The firm is standing up a new Office of the CFO business unit built entirely on Claude — the first standalone practice anchored in a single AI provider's stack. Claude is already live in production across insurance underwriting, mainframe modernization, and private equity deal-making, cutting delivery times by up to 70%.

title: ChatGPT lives inside your spreadsheet now
summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets, a sidebar-native AI that can build, update, and explain multi-tab spreadsheets using natural language. It's available globally to Free through Enterprise users, though Business and Enterprise customers get a free preview only through June 2, 2026. The feature sits directly inside the spreadsheet environment rather than requiring a context switch to the main ChatGPT interface.

title: Video generation gets crowded and capable
summary: Replicate's model catalogue now spans ByteDance's Seedance 2.0, Google's Veo 3.1, Runway Gen-4.5, and Alibaba's Happy Horse 1.0 — all accessible via a single API line. Runway Gen-4.5 currently tops the Artificial Analysis text-to-video benchmark, while Veo 3.1 adds native audio including dialogue and ambient soundscapes. The open-source Wan 2.7 rounds out the options for teams that want to self-host.

title: Fractile raises $220M to put AI on custom silicon
summary: UK chip startup Fractile closed a $220 million Series B led by Accel, Factorial Funds, and Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, with Felicis, 8VC, and Conviction also participating. The company previously raised just $22.5 million in January, making this a dramatic step-change in backing. Fractile is building chips designed to run large language models locally rather than in the cloud — a direct bet against Nvidia's data-center dominance.

title: Runway: $5.3B valuation, $40M ARR added in one quarter
summary: Runway is now valued at $5.3 billion after raising $860 million in total, including a $315 million round from AMD Ventures and Nvidia in February. The company added $40 million in annual recurring revenue in Q2 2026 alone and is expanding into Japan with a $40 million commitment. Founded without Stanford pedigree or a nine-figure seed, Runway is now going head-to-head with Google in AI video generation.

title: Anduril raises $5B, doubles valuation to $61B
summary: Defense tech company Anduril closed a $5 billion round that doubled its valuation to $61 billion, cementing its position as one of the most valuable private defense companies in the world. The raise comes as investment in defense-tech startups is on pace to significantly exceed last year's total, with software for autonomous systems drawing particular interest. Arkeus, a smaller defense-software startup focused on autonomous systems, separately disclosed an $18 million Series A on the same day.

title: GPT-5.5 Arrives in Codex
summary: OpenAI has made GPT-5.5 available to all paid users inside Codex, its AI coding environment. The rollout follows earlier video generation issues that have since been resolved. Users on older Codex versions are advised to update to get access.

title: ChatGPT Goes Free for US Teachers
summary: OpenAI is offering a dedicated ChatGPT plan for verified K–12 teachers in the US at no cost through June 2027. The plan includes GPT-5.1, voice mode, image generation, deep research, and admin controls built for school compliance including FERPA protections. Students are explicitly excluded for now, with a separate offering potentially coming later.

title: Replicate's Model Buffet Keeps Growing
summary: Replicate's explore page is overflowing with fresh model drops: Alibaba's Happy Horse 1.0 for text-to-video, ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 with native audio, Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7, and MiniMax's Music 2.6 for full-song generation. Google's Veo cost-efficient video model and a sub-dollar avatar lipsync model round out the week's additions. The breadth signals that multi-modal generation is quickly becoming a commodity API.

title: Seedream 5.0 Lite Brings Reasoning to Image Gen
summary: Seedream 5.0 Lite, now on Replicate, pairs image generation with built-in reasoning and example-based editing, plus deep domain knowledge for specialized use cases. It joins a competitive image-editing tier alongside GPT Image 1.5 and FLUX.2, which Replicate now openly benchmarks for product photography and portrait preservation tasks.

title: Sierra Space Pulls in $550M for Defense Push
summary: Sierra Space Corp. has raised $550 million as it accelerates a pivot toward becoming a serious US defense contractor. The round gives the space startup fresh runway to compete for government contracts in an era where space infrastructure is increasingly treated as a national security asset.

title: Two-Thirds of Americans Say Government Is Asleep on AI
summary: A new nationally representative survey from Penn's Annenberg Public Policy Center finds that nearly two-thirds of Americans — cutting across party lines — believe the government has done too little to regulate AI. Only 21% would support a new data center in their area, and anxiety about jobs and energy costs is running high. The findings land six months before midterms, making AI regulation a live electoral issue for the first time.

title: House Talks Float Blocking State AI Laws
summary: Congressional negotiations between Reps. Trahan and Obernolte are exploring a federal preemption that would override some state AI regulations, framed narrowly around cutting-edge model development. Safety advocates are alarmed, warning it will become a 'litigation magnet' that companies use to challenge kids' safety and privacy laws in court. The talks sparked immediate Democratic blowback, with Massachusetts legislators urging Trahan to walk away.

title: EU's AI Omnibus Lands, Critics Call It Timid
summary: The European Union's long-awaited AI Omnibus has arrived, consolidating and adjusting obligations under the AI Act, but critics say it lacks ambition and waters down key provisions. Attention is already shifting to the accompanying Digital Omnibus package, which will govern the data infrastructure underpinning AI development. The twin packages represent Europe's most significant attempt yet to balance innovation incentives with regulatory guardrails.

title: ChatGPT Lands Inside Excel and Google Sheets
summary: OpenAI has launched a spreadsheet-native ChatGPT experience that lives in a sidebar directly inside Excel and Google Sheets. Users can build, update, and interrogate multi-tab spreadsheets using natural language without leaving the app. It's available globally to Free through Enterprise tiers, with Business and above getting a free preview through June 2, 2026.

title: ByteDance and Google Flood Replicate With New Models
summary: Replicate's explore page is seeing a surge of new releases, including ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 for multimodal video with native audio, Seedream 5 Lite for reasoning-enhanced image generation, and Google's Nano Banana 2 image model with multi-image fusion and 4K output. The pace of model drops is accelerating across every modality.

title: Anthropic Eyes $900 Billion Valuation
summary: Anthropic is reportedly fielding new investment interest at a $900 billion valuation, a figure that would make it one of the most valuable private companies in history. Observers note that at its prior valuation Anthropic looked underpriced relative to OpenAI, giving investors a perceived entry opportunity. The round has not yet closed.

title: China Drafts Its First Comprehensive AI Law
summary: China's State Council has confirmed for the first time that it is drawing up a comprehensive national AI law, with explicit language about accelerating governance across algorithms, data, computing power, and supply chains. Industry insiders say the move signals that Beijing believes it has accumulated enough regulatory experience to codify the rules of the road. The National People's Congress has listed AI legislation for review for a third consecutive year.

title: Data Center Backlash Grows Louder in the US
summary: A majority of Americans now oppose AI data centers being built in their communities, according to a new survey, and Utah's massive new data center plan has drawn particular local backlash over land, water, and power concerns. Washington Examiner op-eds this weekend called on industry to counter 'data center doomers' and Chinese fearmongering on AI infrastructure. The fight over where AI gets built is becoming a genuine political flashpoint.

title: GLM-5 arrives: 744B params, open-source, agentic-first
summary: Zhipu AI's GLM-5 scales to 744B total parameters (40B active) trained on 28.5T tokens, targeting complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks. It integrates DeepSeek Sparse Attention to cut deployment costs and introduces a novel asynchronous RL infrastructure called Slime for post-training. On AIME 2026 and agentic benchmarks, it claims best-in-class performance among open-source models and closes the gap with frontier closed models.

title: Qwen3.5 gets 1.5–2x faster with MTP speculative decoding
summary: Unsloth's GGUF releases of Qwen3.5 (122B and 397B variants) now support Multi-Token Prediction speculative decoding after the llama.cpp MTP branch merged on May 16, unlocking roughly 1.5–2x faster local inference. The models default to thinking mode with a 262K context window and support 201 languages. Unsloth also offers free Colab notebooks for fine-tuning and RL on all Qwen3.5 sizes.

title: IBM launches Open Agent Leaderboard to benchmark full agent systems
summary: IBM Research's new Open Agent Leaderboard evaluates complete agent systems — not just underlying models — reporting both quality and cost side by side. It ships alongside Exgentic, an open framework for running and reproducing evaluations, and covers five models across five agents and six benchmarks. Early results show open-weight models trail frontier closed-source systems by 18–29 percentage points on average.

title: Replicate's explore page overflows with new multimodal models
summary: This week's Replicate catalog additions include Alibaba's Happy Horse 1.0 text-to-video, ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 with native audio, Google's Veo 3.1 Lite for cost-efficient video generation, and xAI's Grok Imagine Video. On the image side, Black Forest Labs shipped Flux 2 Max and Google dropped Nano Banana 2 with conversational editing. The breadth signals a genuine multimodal model explosion across labs of all sizes.

title: Dust raises $40M Series B for human-agent collaboration
summary: Agentic AI platform Dust secured a $40 million Series B led by Abstract and Sequoia, positioning itself as infrastructure for teams that blend human workers with AI agents. The round reflects growing enterprise appetite for structured agent deployment rather than one-off LLM integrations. Snowflake also participated, signaling data-platform convergence with the agentic layer.

title: Playground Global closes $475M fund IV for deep tech
summary: Palo Alto-based Playground Global announced a $475 million fourth fund, its largest yet, focused on deep technology at the earliest stages. The firm previously raised $410 million for fund three and distinguishes itself from conventional venture by betting on hardware, robotics, and frontier science. The close signals that deep tech remains a magnet for LP capital even as software AI dominates headlines.

title: Nectar Social pulls $30M Series A backed by Menlo and Anthropic fund
summary: AI-powered marketing platform Nectar Social raised a $30 million Series A led by Menlo Ventures through its Anthology Fund, which was created alongside Anthropic. The startup positions itself as a full marketing operating system, automating campaign creation, targeting, and performance analysis. The Anthropic connection underscores how Claude's ecosystem is becoming a go-to backing signal for enterprise AI rounds.

title: State AI bill count hits 1,999 as 23 states move this week
summary: As of May 18, ailawsbystate.com counts 1,999 total AI-related bills published across all 50 US jurisdictions, with 80 newly published and activity in 23 states in the past week alone. Notable updates include New Jersey's AI Image Disclosure Act and AI Likeness Protection Act, New York's ban on AI in corrections risk assessments, and Texas bills regulating autonomous vehicles and AI in insurance claim denials. The sheer volume underscores that US AI regulation is happening at the state level whether or not Congress acts.

title: Google + UNICEF bring Gemini to classrooms worldwide
summary: Google announced a three-year partnership with UNICEF to deploy Gemini for Education, NotebookLM, and its ReadAlong reading app across underserved communities globally. The initiative targets both in-school and out-of-school youth, training teachers to use AI for personalized instruction. Separately, Google is expanding access to Gemini and NotebookLM at universities in Ghana, South Africa, and India.

title: Blackstone puts $5B into a Google TPU cloud venture
summary: Blackstone announced a joint venture with Google to stand up a new TPU-powered cloud, with an initial $5 billion equity commitment and a target of 500MW of capacity by 2027. Google will supply the TPUs, software, and services, while Blackstone handles infrastructure. The deal is designed to meet surging demand for AI compute without routing everything through Google Cloud directly.

title: Ettin Reranker family lands six new CrossEncoder models
summary: Hugging Face researcher Tom Aarsen released six new Sentence Transformers CrossEncoder rerankers built on top of ModernBERT encoders, claiming state-of-the-art performance at each size tier. The 1B model processes 928 pairs per second — 2.4x faster than the leading 1.54B competitor — while matching its benchmark score almost exactly. Full training recipes and data are published alongside the models.

title: Stilta bags $10.5M to automate patent research
summary: Stilta, an AI platform that automates the research and analytical grunt work behind intellectual property cases, announced a $10.5 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz. Y Combinator and operators from OpenAI, Legora, and Lovable also participated. The startup was founded by four people who saw an opening to make patent litigation faster and less expensive.

title: Lexroom raises $50M as investors pile into AI legal tech
summary: Italian legal tech startup Lexroom closed a $50 million Series B led by Left Lane Capital, with Base10 Partners, Eurazeo, and others joining the round. The deal is one of several large checks written into AI-powered legal platforms this month, signaling sustained investor appetite for the sector. Lexroom uses AI to streamline legal research and document workflows for law firms.

title: Mistral acquires Austrian AI startup Emmi
summary: Mistral has struck its second acquisition in a matter of months, picking up Austrian AI startup Emmi to strengthen its capabilities for engineering and manufacturing use cases. Emmi had raised a €15 million seed round last year, and while financial terms were not disclosed, Mistral's CEO described the valuation as 'significant.' The Paris-based company has now raised nearly €2.8 billion and sits at an €11.7 billion valuation.

title: Unframe pulls in $50M Series B for enterprise AI delivery
summary: Unframe, which tailors AI applications to specific enterprise needs, secured $50 million in a Series B round led by Highland Europe. The company was co-founded by Shay Levi and Larissa Schneider and positions itself as a layer between generic AI models and the bespoke requirements of large organizations. The raise underscores continued investor confidence in enterprise AI middleware.

title: Bunch raises $35M to bring AI to VC back-office operations
summary: Bunch, an AI-native platform for private markets operations, closed a $35 million Series B to help venture capital firms manage their operational workflows with AI. The company targets the reporting, compliance, and portfolio-monitoring work that has historically been handled manually at VC funds. The raise reflects growing demand from the investment industry to automate its own internal processes.

title: Jury tosses Musk's OpenAI lawsuit in under two hours
summary: A jury in Oakland, California ruled against Elon Musk in his breach-of-contract case against OpenAI and its founders, deliberating for less than two hours before finding the lawsuit came too late. The verdict hands Sam Altman a significant legal and reputational win as OpenAI approaches a likely IPO. Musk had alleged that OpenAI violated founding agreements by abandoning its nonprofit mission.

title: Gemini 3.5 and Omni arrive at Google I/O
summary: Google declared the start of the agentic Gemini era at I/O 2026, launching Gemini 3.5 for complex multi-step workflows and Gemini Omni for video generation from any input type. The announcements were bundled with new hardware — the Googlebook laptop and Fitbit Air tracker — plus a Universal Cart for cross-platform shopping and a revamped Google Health app. Search also gets information agents that monitor topics in the background and send proactive updates.

title: Cohere ships Command A+ open-source for sovereign AI
summary: Cohere released Command A+ today, positioning it as an open-source enterprise model built specifically for sovereign critical infrastructure use cases. The launch targets organizations that need agentic capabilities without relying on cloud-hosted proprietary models. It follows the earlier reveal of North Mini Code, Cohere's first developer-focused model.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs multimodal AI on a laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a mid-sized open model that drops the traditional multimodal encoder architecture and feeds vision and audio directly into the LLM backbone. It runs on consumer laptops with 16GB of VRAM under an Apache 2.0 license, and benchmarks close to the larger 26B MoE model. Native audio input and Multi-Token Prediction drafters round out a model designed to bring agentic multimodal work off the cloud.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam raised $234M in a Series B led by HCLTech, with Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also participating, valuing the company at $1.5B. The round reflects the global push for sovereign AI, with governments and enterprises wanting control over critical AI infrastructure. Sarvam plans to raise a total of $300M for the round and builds large open-source models targeting Indian languages and enterprise use.

title: NewCore raises $66M to give AI agents an identity
summary: Cybersecurity startup NewCore emerged from stealth with $66M in seed funding led by Cyberstarts, with Index Ventures and Evolution Equity Partners participating, at a $300M post-money valuation. The company is building infrastructure to authenticate, govern, and control AI agents at enterprise scale — a problem that barely existed two years ago. The raise reflects growing investor conviction that agentic AI creates an entirely new attack surface.

title: Factory hits $1.5B valuation for enterprise AI coding
summary: Factory reached a $1.5B valuation as it scales AI coding tooling built specifically for large enterprise environments, rather than individual developers. The company differentiates from consumer-focused tools like Cursor by targeting complex codebases and org-wide deployment workflows. Its growth comes as enterprise demand for AI coding infrastructure outpaces the tooling supply.

title: Unconventional AI confirms $475M seed — yes, seed
summary: Unconventional AI officially confirmed a $475M seed round, one of the largest seed raises on record for any startup. Details on the company's product direction remain scarce, but the scale of the raise signals investor appetite for foundation-layer AI bets outside the established labs. Lightspeed is among the backers, according to reports.

title: Colorado rewrites its landmark AI law under industry and DOJ pressure
summary: Governor Polis signed SB 189 on May 14, formally repealing and replacing Colorado's original 2024 AI Act with a narrower transparency-and-notice framework that takes effect January 1, 2027. The rewrite came after xAI sued over the original law's constitutionality and the Department of Justice intervened in support of the challenge. The episode is being cited as a cautionary tale about how quickly compliance roadmaps can be invalidated by political and legal pressure.

title: EU AI Act high-risk obligations pushed to December 2027
summary: The European Council, Parliament, and Commission reached a provisional agreement to delay Annex III use-based high-risk AI obligations by 16 months, moving the deadline from August 2026 to December 2027. However, the grace period for labelling AI-generated content was actually shortened from six months to three, pulling that specific deadline forward to December 2026. Organizations relying on the longer window for synthetic content transparency now have less runway than expected.

title: Google Home Speaker arrives at $99 with full Gemini inside
summary: Google opened pre-orders today for its new Google Home Speaker — the first audio device built ground-up for Gemini for Home — priced at $99.99 with units shipping June 25. It drops rigid wake-word commands in favour of natural multi-step conversation, ships with 10 new voices and Continued Conversation in all supported languages, and pairs with Google TV Streamer for spatial surround sound.

title: Gemini app becomes a small-business sidekick
summary: Google announced new Gemini app features aimed squarely at small business owners, rolling out globally this month. Owners can now connect their Google Business Profile in a single tap so Gemini can access customer reviews, Q&As, and performance data and draft replies accordingly. A new Business notebooks feature keeps workflows, tasks, and brand context organised in one place.

title: Sarvam hits unicorn status with $234M and HCLTech's backing
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam closed $234M of a targeted $300M Series B at a $1.5B valuation, with HCLTech writing a $150M check as lead strategic investor. Bessemer Venture Partners joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV. The round follows Sarvam's release earlier this year of open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters, cementing it as a flagship of India's sovereign AI push.

title: General Intuition in talks to raise $300M at $2B valuation
summary: General Intuition, the New York startup training AI agents on spatial and temporal reasoning using video-game data, is in advanced talks to raise ~$300M at a just-over-$2B valuation. The raise would come only eight months after its $134M seed round, with Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt among new backers joining Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst. The company spun out of gaming clip-sharing platform Medal.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor the age of AI agents
summary: Observability startup Coralogix pulled in $200M in a Series F led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, valuing it at $1.6B — just 11 months after its $115M Series E. The company is betting that autonomous AI agents will create explosive demand for a new monitoring and troubleshooting layer, and has now raised $550M in total.

title: a16z backs compute marketplace Ornn with $33M seed
summary: Ornn, a startup building an open marketplace where AI compute can be bought and sold like a commodity, raised $33M in a seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz's a16z crypto arm. Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel also participated. a16z general partner Ali Yahya called it the firm's first investment in a dedicated compute marketplace — a signal that liquid GPU markets are becoming infrastructure bets.

title: States rush to fill the federal vacuum: Connecticut, California, Vermont
summary: With Congress having already voted 99-1 to kill a proposed 10-year moratorium on state AI enforcement, states are moving fast: Connecticut enacted one of the most comprehensive state AI laws to date covering companion chatbots, employment decisions, and frontier-model whistleblower protections. California Governor Newsom signed an executive order today directing agencies to plan for AI-driven workforce displacement. Vermont enacted neurological-rights protections for AI use in healthcare, effective July 1.

title: Anthropic's Fable 5 is out — and Mythos 5 reportedly broke the NSA
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, its most capable generally-available model yet, alongside the restricted Claude Mythos 5 for vetted cyberdefenders and government partners. Both are priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens — less than half the cost of Mythos Preview. A separate report revealed that Mythos breached 'almost all' NSA classified systems within hours during a red-team evaluation, which preceded a Commerce Department directive limiting access.

title: Google Gemma 4 12B: multimodal on your laptop, no encoders needed
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open Apache 2.0 model that runs on 16GB of VRAM and accepts image, audio, and text inputs directly into its LLM backbone — no separate multimodal encoders required. It's positioned between the lightweight E4B and the larger 26B MoE model, with benchmark performance close to the 26B. Native audio input and Multi-Token Prediction drafters for lower latency make it the most capable mid-size open model Google has shipped.

title: Google I/O recap: Gemini 3.5, Omni, Universal Cart, and the Googlebook
summary: Google's May 2026 I/O blitz introduced Gemini 3.5 for complex agentic workflows and Gemini Omni for mixed-input video generation, alongside Android Halo for managing agents on-device. Hardware announcements included the Googlebook laptop built around Gemini Intelligence and the Fitbit Air health tracker. Universal Cart lets users add items across Search, YouTube, Gmail, and Gemini in one unified shopping flow.

title: ChatGPT gets full-screen writing blocks and a clinician edition
summary: OpenAI rolled out full-screen writing blocks in ChatGPT for long-form documents like essays, PRDs, and reports, with library saving, table of contents, and download support — available first to Plus and Pro users in the US. Separately, OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Clinicians, a free tier for verified US healthcare providers. GPT-5.5 Instant became the new default model for all ChatGPT users, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant.

title: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super scales AV reasoning to 32 billion parameters
summary: NVIDIA expanded its open Alpamayo platform with Alpamayo 2 Super, a 32B-parameter vision-language-action model for autonomous vehicles with full 360-degree surround camera support and high-level meta-action outputs like yield and lane change. The release also includes AlpaGym, an open-source closed-loop reinforcement learning framework that scales from a single GPU to multi-node clusters. Alpamayo Recipes provides end-to-end workflow templates for fine-tuning, quantization, and deployment.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam raised $234M in a Series B led by HCLTech, which contributed $150M, with Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participating. The round values the company at $1.5 billion, making it India's newest AI unicorn as governments globally scramble for sovereign AI infrastructure. Sarvam recently released open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters and hopes to raise a total of $300M for the round.

title: General Intuition in talks for $300M at $2B valuation
summary: General Intuition, the New York startup building foundation models that teach AI agents spatial and temporal navigation through video game data, is in talks to raise roughly $300M, sources told TechCrunch. The raise would value the company at just over $2 billion, up from its $134M seed eight months ago. Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt have joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst in the new round.

title: Swiss privacy AI startup Prem targets $500M valuation with $100M raise
summary: Prem AI, based in Switzerland, is raising a $100M Series A targeting a valuation of at least $500 million. The company helps hedge funds and law firms run AI models entirely on private infrastructure, making it a bet on enterprise demand for sovereign, on-premise AI. The round is expected to close in Q3 2026.

title: Pramaana Labs pulls $27M seed to bring formal verification to AI
summary: Pramaana Labs announced a $27M seed round led by Khosla Ventures, with Accel, BoldCap, Nexus, Premji Invest, and Unbound also participating. The startup is applying formal verification methods — mathematical proofs of correctness — to AI systems, a niche that has gained urgency as agentic AI takes on higher-stakes tasks. The seed size signals serious institutional conviction in AI reliability tooling.

title: FDA-for-AI proposal dead; state patchwork accelerates
summary: The Trump administration formally abandoned its 'FDA for AI' proposal on May 22, 2026, eliminating the prospect of a unified federal AI oversight framework. Connecticut enacted a comprehensive state AI law covering companion chatbots, frontier model governance, and employment AI, while Colorado repealed its landmark AI Act and replaced it with a lighter notice-and-disclosure regime. Louisiana became the 22nd US state to pass a consumer data privacy law, further expanding the compliance surface area for any company deploying AI.

title: AI prompts are now discoverable in federal litigation
summary: In Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil Company, a federal magistrate judge ordered plaintiffs to produce the AI prompts their expert used to prepare her report, ruling that prompts are part of an expert's methodology rather than protected drafting material. The decision marks one of the clearest signals yet that AI-assisted expert work will face full discovery scrutiny. Legal teams relying on AI for expert analysis now face a new and concrete evidentiary risk.

title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.3-Codex, its first unified coding agent
summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex, combining its Codex and GPT-5 training stacks into a single model that is roughly 25% faster than its predecessor and sets new benchmark highs. Unlike earlier code-generation tools, it's designed as a steerable coding agent you can redirect mid-task. A smaller GPT-5-Codex-Mini variant also launched, offering up to 4x more usage within existing ChatGPT subscriptions.

title: Gemma 4 12B brings multimodal AI to your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B under Apache 2.0, a model that runs locally on consumer hardware with just 16GB of RAM. Its encoder-free architecture pipes vision and audio directly into the LLM backbone, cutting latency and memory overhead while matching benchmark performance close to Google's larger 26B model. It's the first mid-sized Gemma model to support native audio inputs.

title: Google gives website owners an AI Search opt-out switch
summary: Google is testing a new Search Console toggle that lets website owners decide whether their content appears in AI Overviews, AI Mode, and related generative search features. Sites that opt out lose the traffic and impressions those features generate, but their organic ranking is unaffected. The rollout begins with a subset of UK publishers before expanding globally.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Sarvam raised $234M at a $1.5B valuation, with $150M coming from HCLTech as lead strategic investor and Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participating. The company builds open-source models in 30B and 105B parameters aimed at Indian languages and enterprise use cases. It's targeting a full $300M Series B close, more than five times its combined seed and Series A total.

title: General Intuition eyes $300M to teach AI agents to move through space
summary: General Intuition, which spun out of gaming clip platform Medal just eight months ago with a $134M seed, is now in talks to raise $300M at a $2B+ valuation. The New York startup builds foundation models that train AI agents on spatial and temporal reasoning, with Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst among its backers. The round would mark one of the fastest valuation climbs for a foundation-model startup this year.

title: a16z backs Ornn's compute marketplace with $33M
summary: Ornn raised $33M in a seed round led by a16z crypto — the firm's first investment in a compute marketplace — alongside Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel. The startup is building a venue where AI compute power can be bought and sold like a commodity exchange. With GPU scarcity still a chokepoint for AI development, liquid compute markets are becoming an investable category.

title: Swiss startup Prem raises $100M to keep AI private
summary: Prem AI, which helps hedge funds and law firms run AI models on their own private infrastructure, is raising a $100M Series A targeting a $500M+ valuation. The Zurich-based company's pitch is simple: enterprise customers who cannot send sensitive data to public clouds still need frontier AI. Founder Simone Giacomelli expects the round to close in Q3 2026.

title: Pramaana Labs raises $27M to make AI provably correct
summary: Pramaana Labs closed a $27M seed led by Khosla Ventures, with Accel, Nexus, Premji Invest, and others joining, to bring formal verification techniques to AI systems. Formal verification — long used in chip design and safety-critical software — mathematically proves that a system behaves as intended, addressing hallucination and reliability at the root level. It's an early but growing bet that the AI industry's next frontier is correctness, not just capability.

title: Trump shelved the frontier-AI review order
summary: The White House postponed signing an executive order that would have created a voluntary federal review process for frontier AI models before public release, after Trump expressed concern it would block AI development. Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI had already agreed to give the Commerce Department's CAISI 30-day early access to unreleased models — but without the order, the arrangement has no legal backbone. The episode leaves the US as the only major AI power with no formal pre-release evaluation mechanism.

title: Colorado's landmark AI law quietly died — and got replaced
summary: Colorado Governor Polis signed SB 189 on May 14, effectively repealing the nation's first comprehensive AI law after xAI sued and the DOJ intervened, replacing it with a much narrower notice-and-disclosure framework effective January 2027. The original law's concept of algorithmic discrimination has been dropped entirely. Companies that spent months building compliance programs around the original rules now have to start over.

title: The "voluntary" AI EO has a hidden hook
summary: A Lawfare analysis of the June 2 executive order on AI innovation argues that the framework's "voluntary" label masks a coercive reality: companies that depend on government contracts face enormous pressure to participate in pre-release model evaluations or risk losing access to the market. The order explicitly disclaims any mandatory licensing regime, but the government-as-customer dynamic creates de facto leverage. It's the same dynamic that has repeatedly turned voluntary standards into effective mandates across tech and defense.

title: Senate hearing: innovation vs. oversight, no resolution
summary: The Senate Banking Committee's June 11 AI hearing surfaced a clean fault line: Republicans framed AI dominance as requiring zero friction, while Democrats led by Elizabeth Warren warned of financial systemic risk and lax chip export controls to China. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang declined to appear, a pointed absence given the committee's focus on the $5T valuation and chip sales to Chinese military-linked buyers. Senators Warren and Blumenthal used the hearing to introduce the AI Bubble Transparency Act, requiring financial regulators to track AI-related exposures.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over ChatGPT safety concealment
summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed the first state-led civil lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly hid serious risks of ChatGPT while marketing it aggressively to Florida residents including children. The complaint covers deceptive trade practices, dependency-inducing design, data collection from minors, and downplayed hallucinations. It follows a federal court dismissal of Musk's $150B OpenAI suit and signals that state AGs are becoming the primary enforcement vector for AI consumer protection.

title: Gemini 3.5 ships with full agent stack
summary: Google launched Gemini 3.5 at I/O 2026, positioning it as the backbone of a new agentic era. The model handles complex multi-step workflows across apps and comes paired with Android Halo, a new phone space for tracking agent progress. Gemini 3.5 Flash also gains built-in computer use, letting developers build agents that see, reason, and click across browser, mobile, and desktop environments.

title: Gemini 3.5 Live Translate speaks 70+ languages in real time
summary: Google's new Live Translate model does near-instant speech-to-speech translation across more than 70 languages, preserving the speaker's intonation and pitch. It's rolling out in Google Translate on Android and iOS now, and arrives in Google Meet for enterprise customers in private preview this month. Google Meet previously supported just five languages for live translation.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs multimodal AI on a laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weights model that handles images, audio, and text without separate encoders — inputs flow directly into the LLM backbone. It runs locally on consumer laptops with just 16GB of RAM and benchmarks close to Google's larger 26B mixture-of-experts model. Multi-state companies now face genuinely incompatible obligations with no federal floor in sight.

title: EU AI Omnibus quietly rewrites the enforcement timeline
summary: At 4:30am on May 7, EU legislators reached political agreement on an Omnibus amendment to the AI Act, pushing compliance deadlines for high-risk AI systems in areas like biometrics, employment, and critical infrastructure to December 2027 — extending the original August 2026 schedule by up to 24 months. Enforcement for certain systems has been centralised in the EU AI Office, and an EU-level regulatory sandbox has been established. The delay is explicitly linked to the absence of published harmonised standards, with none yet appearing in the Official Journal.

title: Trump shelved the 'FDA for AI' — and signed a different order instead
summary: The Trump administration abandoned its proposed 'FDA for AI' oversight framework on May 22, eliminating the prospect of a unified federal review process for frontier models before public release. On June 2, President Trump instead signed an executive order promoting AI innovation and cybersecurity that explicitly disclaims any authority to require licensing or preclearance of AI models. The administration has simultaneously moved to embed commercial AI into classified Pentagon systems through agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI for early access to unreleased frontier models.

title: A court just made AI prompts discoverable in litigation
summary: In Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil, a federal magistrate judge ordered plaintiffs to produce the AI prompts their expert used in preparing her report, treating them as part of the expert's methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that courts view AI-assisted expert work as subject to the same discovery rules as any other methodology. Legal teams using AI in litigation now face real exposure over what they type into the chatbox.

title: Google drops Gemini 3.5, Omni, and a new laptop
summary: At Google I/O 2026, Google announced Gemini 3.5 for agentic and coding workflows and Gemini Omni, a model that generates high-quality video from any input — images, audio, text, or video. The company also unveiled the Googlebook, a laptop built from the ground up around Gemini intelligence, plus a new Google Health app and the Fitbit Air tracker.

title: June Pixel Drop brings AI video and music to your pocket
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop adds Gemini Omni-powered video creation and music generation directly on Pixel phones — describe an idea or upload a photo and get a full audio track with lyrics. The update also brings Android 17, Wear OS 7, floating app multitasking, and emergency sharing integration with crash and fall detection.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop, no encoder needed
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weights multimodal model under Apache 2.0 that fits in 16 GB of VRAM and accepts vision and audio inputs natively — no separate encoders. It lands between the edge-friendly E4B and the larger 26B MoE model, and ships with multi-token prediction drafters to cut latency.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.3-Codex and open-weights reasoning models
summary: OpenAI shipped GPT-5.3-Codex, billed as its most capable agentic coding model by merging the Codex and GPT-5 training stacks, along with a cheaper GPT-5-Codex-Mini for longer sessions. It also released two open-weight models — gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b — for teams wanting to self-host, and updated GPT-5.5 Instant as the new ChatGPT default.

title: Cohere ships Command A+ and its first agentic coding model
summary: Cohere rounded out its Command A family with Command A+, a 218B-parameter MoE model combining vision, reasoning, translation, and agentic tasks in one. It also released North Mini Code, a 30B MoE model small enough to run locally and aimed squarely at agentic coding workflows.

title: Sarvam hits unicorn status with $234M Series B
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, with $150 million coming from HCLTech as lead strategic investor; Bessemer, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also participated. The company, which launched open-source 30B and 105B models earlier this year, is targeting a total of $300 million for the round.

title: General Intuition eyes $300M at $2B valuation
summary: General Intuition, which builds foundation models teaching AI agents to navigate space and time, is in talks to raise roughly $300 million, which would push its valuation just above $2 billion. The New York startup spun out of gaming clip platform Medal just eight months ago with a $134M seed and counts Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst among its backers.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor the agentic stack
summary: AI observability startup Coralogix closed a $200 million Series F at a $1.6 billion valuation, betting that autonomous agent deployments will create massive demand for monitoring and troubleshooting infrastructure. The round was led by Advent and CPPIB and comes just 11 months after its $115M Series E, bringing total funding to $550 million.

title: a16z backs compute marketplace Ornn in $33M seed
summary: Ornn, a marketplace where AI compute can be bought and sold like a commodity, raised $33 million in a seed round led by a16z crypto alongside Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel. General partner Ali Yahya called it a16z's first investment in a compute marketplace.

title: Pramaana Labs snags $27M to bring formal verification to AI
summary: Pramaana Labs closed a $27 million seed round led by Khosla Ventures to apply formal verification techniques to AI systems, with Accel, BoldCap, Nexus, Premji Invest, and Unbound also participating. The startup is targeting a gap in AI reliability that has become increasingly urgent as autonomous agents handle higher-stakes decisions.

title: Senate votes 99-1 to keep state AI laws alive
summary: A House Republican proposal to impose a 10-year moratorium on state AI enforcement was stripped from the budget reconciliation bill by a near-unanimous Senate vote, effectively confirming that federal preemption of state AI law is politically dead for now. All 50 states have now introduced AI-related legislation, and over 2,182 AI bills are active across the country with inconsistent definitions and enforcement mechanisms.

title: Colorado rewrites its landmark AI act — again
summary: Governor Polis signed SB 26-189 on May 14, replacing Colorado's original first-in-the-nation AI law with a narrower transparency-and-notice framework effective January 1, 2027. The rewrite came after xAI sued over the original law's constitutionality and the DOJ intervened to support the challenge, forcing a legislative retreat from the broader algorithmic-discrimination standard.

title: Trump signs AI innovation executive order, skips mandates
summary: President Trump's June 2 executive order on AI directs agencies to harden federal cybersecurity, create a voluntary frontier-model deployment framework, and prioritize criminal enforcement against AI-enabled cyberattacks — but explicitly bars any licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirements for AI development. The order gives frontier model developers a path to a classified federal benchmarking process and a 30-day early-access window before public release.

title: Court rules AI prompts are fair game in discovery
summary: In Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil Company, a federal magistrate judge ordered the plaintiff to produce the AI prompts its expert used to prepare her report, treating them as part of discoverable methodology rather than protected work product. The ruling sets a significant precedent for any litigation where AI-assisted expert analysis is introduced.

title: FTC settles with three firms over fake AI claims
summary: The FTC reached $930,000 in settlements with three marketing companies that made deceptive claims about their AI capabilities, establishing live enforcement precedents under existing consumer protection law in the absence of any federal AI statute. The Take It Down Act also took effect May 19, giving the FTC new tools against non-consensual intimate imagery generated by AI.

title: Gemini Omni can now make videos from anything
summary: Google's May 2026 recap confirms Gemini Omni accepts text, images, audio, and video as input and generates high-quality video grounded in real-world knowledge. The model launched at Google I/O alongside Gemini 3.5, which powers multi-step agentic workflows across apps. Gemini Spark, a 24/7 proactive assistant, is rolling out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers first.

title: June Pixel Drop: music, video, and floating app bubbles
summary: The June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni video creation and original music generation directly to Pixel phones — describe an idea or upload a photo and get a full audio track back. Any app can now be turned into a floating bubble window for smoother multitasking. Emergency Detection now simultaneously calls services and notifies chosen contacts during crashes, falls, or loss of pulse.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs multimodal AI on your laptop
summary: Google's new open-weight Gemma 4 12B model handles vision and audio inputs natively without separate encoders, running on just 16GB of VRAM. It's positioned between the lightweight E4B and the 26B MoE model, and is the first mid-sized Gemma to support native audio. Released under Apache 2.0, it's designed for agentic workflows on everyday hardware.

title: ChatGPT gets personal finance, CarPlay, and a clinician mode
summary: OpenAI is rolling out a personal finance dashboard to Plus users in the US, letting them connect financial accounts and ask ChatGPT questions grounded in their real data. A new ChatGPT for Clinicians version launches free for verified US doctors, with clinical search, CME credit support, and deep medical literature research. CarPlay support also arrives for hands-free voice conversations on iOS 26.4 and newer.

title: Gamer-founded Vast becomes China's newest AI unicorn
summary: Vast, a Beijing-based 3D-modeling startup founded by 29-year-old gamer Luma He, raised nearly $200 million to cross the $1 billion valuation mark. Ince Capital and a China Life Insurance-backed venture fund led the round, with Genesis Capital and existing backers also participating. The company is targeting the booming demand for 3D assets in gaming, film, and industrial design.

title: Sekai raises $20M to let anyone build apps with a text prompt
summary: Sekai, a platform that lets users create mini applications through natural language prompts, has closed a $20 million Series A co-led by Khosla Ventures and Connect Ventures. CEO Lucky Zhang told Axios the funds will go toward expanding the platform's capabilities and user base. The startup previously raised $6 million in seed funding from Mayfield in 2025.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to watch over AI agents
summary: Software-monitoring startup Coralogix closed a $200 million Series F just 11 months after its last raise, valuing it at $1.6 billion post-money. The bet: as AI agents proliferate, enterprises will need a new generation of monitoring and troubleshooting tools to keep autonomous software in check. The round was led by Advent and Canada's CPPIB, bringing total funding to $550 million.

title: Sarvam hits unicorn status with $234M round led by HCLTech
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam has raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, with HCLTech committing $150 million as lead strategic investor. Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV Partners also joined the Series B. Sarvam launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year and is targeting a $300 million total raise.

title: Trump signs AI executive order — voluntary, not mandatory
summary: President Trump signed the executive order 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security' on June 2, cementing an innovation-first posture that explicitly bars any mandatory licensing or permitting for AI model development. The order creates a Treasury-run AI cybersecurity clearinghouse and allows developers to voluntarily give the government up to 30 days of pre-release frontier model access. Critics note the contrast with the stricter pre-release testing framework the White House quietly shelved weeks earlier.

title: GitHub Copilot gets a real desktop home
summary: GitHub launched the Copilot app in technical preview — a full agent-native desktop experience with a unified 'My Work' view spanning repos, pull requests, and background automations. New 'canvases' let humans and agents collaborate on the same live surface, and a public SDK in six languages lets teams build on the same agentic runtime. Available now for Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise users.

title: Google's Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weight multimodal model that fits in 16GB of VRAM and is the first mid-sized Gemma to accept native audio input — no separate encoder needed. It bridges the gap between the lightweight E4B and the heavier 26B MoE model, with benchmark scores close to the larger version. It ships under Apache 2.0, so teams can run, fine-tune, and redistribute freely.

title: ChatGPT lands in CarPlay and Excel
summary: OpenAI pushed ChatGPT into Apple CarPlay for hands-free voice conversations on the road, requiring iOS 26.4 and a supported car. Separately, ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets went globally available, embedding a ChatGPT sidebar directly into the spreadsheet experience. A new personal finance feature is also rolling out to Plus users in the US on web and iOS.

title: Google's May recap: Gemini 3.5, Omni, and the Googlebook
summary: Google's I/O-era product wave is now fully documented: Gemini 3.5 for agentic coding, Gemini Omni for video generation from any input, a Universal Cart across Search and YouTube, a new Google Health app, the Fitbit Air wellness pebble, and the Googlebook laptop built around Gemini Intelligence. It's the broadest single-month hardware-plus-AI launch Google has attempted.

title: Pixel June Drop: AI music, video, and emergency alerts
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop adds Gemini Omni video creation and original music generation directly to Pixel phones — just describe an idea or upload a photo.
