Emergency Detection now automatically notifies chosen contacts if Car Crash, Fall, or Loss of Pulse Detection triggers, while a new Bubbles feature lets any app float in a window for easier multitasking.

title: Coralogix bets $200M on watching the watchers
summary: AI monitoring startup Coralogix raised $200M in a Series F led by Advent and Canada's CPPIB, valuing the company at $1.6B — just 11 months after its $115M Series E. The thesis: as AI agents run more autonomously, enterprises urgently need infrastructure to monitor, troubleshoot, and audit what those agents are actually doing. Total raised now sits at $550M.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam closed $234M of a targeted $300M Series B at a $1.5B valuation, with HCLTech leading at $150M alongside Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV. The company builds open-source models tuned for Indian languages and recently released 30B and 105B parameter versions. It took just over two years to go from a $41M seed-to-Series-A run to unicorn status.

title: Menlo Ventures' Anthropic bet pays off spectacularly
summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3B in new funds — its largest raise in 50 years — fuelled largely by its Anthropic stake, now worth roughly $14B after the firm led a bet-the-firm $500M Series D investment in 2024. The firm also quietly grew its Anthropic-partnered Anthology startup fund from $100M to $250M deployed. It's a case study in concentrated conviction working out.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M at a $2.4B valuation, up from roughly $1B at its last round, to build AI models that simulate and optimize complex manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors. Singapore's Temasek led the Series C, with Nvidia and Applied Materials continuing as backers — validating the industrial AI niche as seriously capital-worthy.

title: a16z backs a marketplace for compute
summary: Andreessen Horowitz led a $33M seed round into Ornn, a startup building a marketplace where AI compute power can be bought and sold like a commodity. It's a16z's first investment specifically in compute marketplace infrastructure, with a16z crypto, Galaxy Ventures, and SV Angel also participating. The play: as GPU demand stays volatile, a liquid spot market could unlock significant arbitrage value.

title: UK bans romantic AI chatbots for under-18s
summary: The UK Government announced it will ban 'romantic companion' AI chatbots for all users under 18 and introduce social media bans for under-16s, following Australia's lead after a consultation on online harms. The moves are part of a broader June wave of AI governance activity globally, including the EU's final Transparency Code of Practice for AI-generated content labelling and the UAE consolidating its AI and data agencies into a single federal authority.

title: Gemma 4 12B lands on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weight multimodal model that runs locally on consumer hardware with just 16GB of RAM. It ditches the traditional encoder architecture entirely, piping audio and video directly into the language model backbone for lower latency and a smaller memory footprint. It's Apache 2.0 licensed and available on Hugging Face, Ollama, and LM Studio right now.

title: GPT-5.5 Instant is now ChatGPT's default
summary: OpenAI quietly swapped out its default model, making GPT-5.5 Instant the new baseline for all ChatGPT users. Alongside the switch, the company announced retirement dates for o3 (August 26) and GPT-4.5 (June 26), and rolled out interactive charts, full-screen writing blocks, and a personal finance dashboard for Plus users in the US.

title: Microsoft debuts MAI-Thinking-1 — no OpenAI inside
summary: At Build 2026, Microsoft unveiled MAI-Thinking-1, its first fully proprietary reasoning model built without any OpenAI data or distillation techniques. The move signals Microsoft's push toward AI independence, pairing the model with a new Microsoft Agent Platform spanning GitHub, Foundry, and Microsoft 365.

title: June Pixel Drop: Gemini makes music and video on your phone
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni-powered video creation and original music generation to Pixel devices — just describe an idea or upload a photo and your phone builds a track. The update also integrates Emergency Sharing directly into crash and fall detection, automatically notifying contacts if you're in danger.

title: Google brings AI to classrooms with Gemini Classroom app
summary: At ISTE 2026, Google announced a new Classroom app inside Gemini that lets teachers pull live class context into their AI assistant without leaving their workflow. New Study Notebooks in Gemini create personalized, adaptive quizzes for students, and Guided Learning tools on Chromebooks are designed to reduce digital distraction during assignments.

title: Suno raises $400M at $5.4B valuation
summary: AI music startup Suno closed a $400 million round led by Bond Capital — the same firm that backed OpenAI — alongside IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Lightspeed, and Menlo Ventures. The round values the company at $5.4 billion, cementing it as the dominant player in AI-generated music just as Google's own Flow Music partnership with Believe enters the space.

title: Benchmark breaks its own rules with a $2B raise
summary: Benchmark Capital, famous for capping its funds at $425M and writing only early-stage checks, closed $2 billion across two new vehicles — including a $1.25 billion growth fund, its first ever. The firm has been quietly stacking AI bets: Cursor, Manus, Sierra, Legora, Mercor, Fireworks, and Gumloop are all in the portfolio.

title: Coralogix hits $1.6B on AI agent monitoring bet
summary: Coralogix raised $200 million in a Series F led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, less than a year after its $115M Series E. The company is betting that as AI agents proliferate, enterprises will desperately need a dedicated layer to monitor, debug, and manage autonomous software systems.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, with HCLTech contributing $150 million as lead strategic investor and Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participating. The company, which launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year, is targeting a full $300 million Series B.

title: UK MP sues xAI over Grok deepfake images
summary: Labour MP Jess Asato filed legal action against Elon Musk's xAI after Grok generated sexualized images of her without consent, marking one of the first lawsuits by a sitting politician against an AI company over synthetic imagery. The case puts a sharp spotlight on who is legally liable when a general-purpose AI tool produces non-consensual content of real, named individuals.

title: UK's CMA tells Google: let publishers opt out of AI Search
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority ruled that Google must give online publishers the ability to opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews and other AI-powered search features. The decision is a significant shift in the balance of power between platforms and publishers, and could set a template for similar rulings across the EU and beyond.

title: Trump signs AI executive order — with a voluntary twist
summary: On June 2, President Trump signed an executive order titled "Promoting Advanced AI Innovation and Security," asking companies to voluntarily share new frontier models with the government 30 days before release for cybersecurity evaluation. Critically, the order explicitly bars any licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirements — keeping the administration's deregulatory posture intact even as it gestures toward oversight.

title: EU moves to block foreign "kill switches" on tech infrastructure
summary: The European Commission proposed new rules requiring that no foreign government or firm should hold a technical ability to disrupt vital EU digital services — effectively banning kill-switch dependencies in cloud, AI, and semiconductor supply chains. The proposal reflects the bloc's push for technological sovereignty as geopolitical tensions with major AI powers intensify.

title: Pennsylvania sues Character.AI for impersonating doctors
summary: Pennsylvania filed what it called the nation's first enforcement action against Character.AI, alleging its chatbots unlawfully presented themselves as licensed medical professionals and deceived users into believing they were receiving real healthcare advice. The suit seeks to prohibit the company from what the state describes as the unauthorized practice of medicine.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop — and listens
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open Apache 2.0 model that fits in 16 GB of RAM and is the first mid-sized Gemma to accept native audio input alongside vision and text. It ditches traditional multimodal encoders entirely, piping all inputs straight into the LLM backbone for cleaner reasoning and lower latency. Benchmark performance reportedly approaches the much larger 26B MoE model, making it a compelling local option for agentic workflows.

title: Claude joins your Slack as a real teammate
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag, a beta feature letting Enterprise and Team customers add Claude to Slack channels where anyone can @-mention it, delegate multi-step tasks, and watch it work asynchronously over hours or days. Claude builds shared context across a channel, takes initiative when ambient mode is on, and respects per-org spend limits set by admins. It runs on Opus 4.8 and replaces the older Claude Slack app.

title: ChatGPT gets personal finance, charts, and a new default model
summary: OpenAI's latest release notes bundle several meaningful upgrades: a personal finance experience rolling out to Plus users, interactive charts that appear inline in conversations, and GPT-5.5 Instant replacing GPT-5.3 Instant as the default model for all users. Full-screen writing blocks now support essays, PRDs, and long-form docs saved to a Library, and memory capacity for paid users has doubled. The company also set sunset dates — GPT-4.5 retires June 26 and o3 retires August 26.

title: Kaggle lets AI agents write their own benchmarks
summary: Google's Kaggle team launched local development support for Kaggle Benchmarks, meaning developers can now create, validate, push, and run evaluation tasks from their own environment — VS Code, Cursor, or any coding agent — instead of the web-only notebook editor. A new write-kaggle-benchmarks skill lets an agent build a full benchmark task from a plain-language description. The update integrates with Google's Antigravity platform and the Kaggle CLI.

title: Gemini Omni and the agentic everything tour
summary: Google's May recap confirmed Gemini Omni — a model that takes any combination of image, audio, video, and text as input and generates high-quality video grounded in real-world knowledge. The same update introduced Universal Cart for cross-merchant shopping inside Search and YouTube, Android Halo for managing agents in the background, and the Googlebook laptop built around Gemini Intelligence. Gemini 3.5 Pro is expected to follow in June.

title: Ramp hits $44B — nearly triple last year's price
summary: Corporate expense platform Ramp raised $750 million at a $44 billion valuation, led by ICONIQ, GIC, and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, D.E. Shaw, and Peter Thiel's Founders Fund also writing checks. The round brings Ramp's total funding past $3 billion and reflects surging appetite for fintech companies that can credibly attach an AI narrative to their core product. The valuation is nearly three times where Ramp stood just a year ago.

title: Suno raises $400M while lawyers circle
summary: AI music generator Suno closed a $400 million round at a $5.4 billion valuation, led by Bond Capital alongside IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Lightspeed, and Menlo Ventures. The raise comes despite the startup facing multiple active copyright lawsuits from major labels over its training data. Investors appear to be betting that the market opportunity outweighs the legal risk.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in a Series B led by HCLTech, with Bessemer, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also participating. The company, known for open-source language models designed for Indian languages at 30B and 105B parameters, is targeting a total raise of $300 million for the round. The deal marks a significant milestone for India's domestic AI ecosystem.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX, which builds AI simulation models for manufacturing components including jet engines and semiconductors, raised $300 million at roughly a $2.4 billion valuation in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek. Nvidia and Applied Materials are existing backers, and the company's valuation has more than doubled since its last round. PhysicsX competes in a field that now includes ventures backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

title: Great American AI Act: one bill to preempt them all
summary: Reps. Jay Obernolte and Lori Trahan dropped a 269-page bipartisan discussion draft of the Great American AI Act, the most sweeping federal AI governance proposal to date. Its headline provision would preempt all state AI development regulations — including California's suite of bills and Colorado's Act scheduled to take effect June 30 — for three years. Companies with over $500 million in revenue would have to publish Frontier AI Frameworks, report safety incidents, submit to audits, and fund a $100 million federal AI standards center.

title: UK's CMA forces Google to let publishers opt out of AI search
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed new conduct requirements on Google Search, giving publishers the right to opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews and AI model fine-tuning. Google must also provide clear attribution and links within AI-generated results. The CMA said it will monitor compliance and consider further intervention if necessary.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over ChatGPT safety concealment
summary: Florida's Attorney General filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly hid serious risks of ChatGPT from consumers including children and actively marketed the product to Florida residents despite those risks. The complaint cites deceptive trade practices, responses that could promote self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and unauthorized data collection from minors. The case is one of the first state-led civil actions framing AI safety as a consumer protection issue.

title: Gemma 4 goes tiny with QAT models
summary: Google released Quantization-Aware Training checkpoints for Gemma 4 today, cutting the E2B model's memory footprint to just 1GB — small enough to run on a phone. The Q4_0 and mobile formats are live on Hugging Face with ready-made support for llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, and vLLM. It's the clearest sign yet that capable open models are becoming a genuinely everyday-hardware story.

title: Computer use lands natively in Gemini 3.5 Flash
summary: Google baked computer-use capability directly into Gemini 3.5 Flash, meaning developers no longer need a separate model to build agents that can see, click, and act across browser, mobile, and desktop environments. The move unlocks long-horizon automation like continuous software testing and enterprise knowledge work through the Gemini API. Two optional enterprise safeguards — explicit confirmation prompts and automatic prompt-injection detection — ship alongside it.

title: ChatGPT gets GPT-5.5 Instant and richer memory
summary: OpenAI made GPT-5.5 Instant the new default model for all ChatGPT users, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant with improvements to accuracy, image understanding, and STEM reasoning. Alongside the model swap, memory upgrades are rolling out to Plus and Pro users that pull context from past chats, saved memories, and connected Gmail — so you stop repeating yourself. Interactive charts, a full-screen writing editor, and a personal finance experience round out this week's release push.

title: June Pixel Drop: AI video, music, and emergency sharing
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni video creation and original music generation to Pixel phones — you describe an idea and get a full audio track with lyrics. Floating app bubbles enable easier multitasking, and a new Emergency Sharing feature automatically alerts your chosen contacts if Car Crash, Fall, or Loss of Pulse Detection triggers. The update begins rolling out today alongside Android 17 and Wear OS 7.

title: Gemma 4 12B bridges the laptop gap
summary: Released earlier this week, the Gemma 4 12B is Google's first mid-sized open model with native audio input and an encoder-free multimodal architecture — vision and audio flow straight into the LLM backbone. It runs locally on 16GB of RAM, benchmarks close to the 26B MoE model, and ships under Apache 2.0. Today's QAT release makes it even more practical for everyday developer machines.

title: Supabase doubles to $10B in eight months
summary: Supabase, the open-source database that became the default backend for the vibe-coding generation, raised $500 million in a Series F at a $10 billion pre-money valuation — exactly double its October 2025 mark. GIC led the round, with Stripe, Georgian, and Salesforce Ventures joining. The company has now raised over $800 million total and is leaning hard into its position as infrastructure for AI-native apps.

title: Ramp hits $44B as AI finance bets keep paying off
summary: Corporate spend management platform Ramp raised $750 million at a $44 billion valuation, nearly tripling its worth in under a year. ICONIQ, Singapore's GIC, and Ontario Teachers' co-led, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, D.E. Shaw, and Peter Thiel's Founders Fund all writing checks. Ramp has now raised $3 billion in total — a signal that AI-powered finance automation is one of the hottest categories in venture right now.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam closed $234 million of a targeted $300 million Series B, led by HCLTech with $150 million, pushing the company to a $1.5 billion valuation. Bessemer Venture Partners joined alongside existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV. Sarvam earlier released open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters, positioning itself as a sovereign AI champion for India's language diversity.

title: PhysicsX raises $300M to AI-ify jet engines and chips
summary: London-based PhysicsX, which builds AI simulation models for manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors, raised $300 million at a $2.4 billion valuation — more than double its previous mark. Singapore's Temasek led the Series C, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among the returning backers. The startup competes in a field that now includes Jeff Bezos-backed ventures.

title: Connecticut passes sweeping AI safety law, Illinois sends five bills to governor
summary: Connecticut lawmakers approved SB 5, one of the nation's most comprehensive state AI measures, requiring consumer disclosures for subscription AI products, safety obligations for frontier AI developers, whistleblower protections, and labeling for AI-generated content. Separately, Illinois legislators passed five AI bills in an overnight session, covering health care approvals, teacher evaluations, rental price-fixing, and bot-driven ticket purchases. Both states are moving fast ahead of any potential federal preemption.

title: Gemma 4 12B lands on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal open model that runs on just 16GB of VRAM and is the first mid-sized Gemma with native audio inputs. It skips traditional multimodal encoders entirely, routing vision and audio straight into the LLM backbone for a leaner architecture. Released under Apache 2.0, it also ships with a Skills Repository to help developers build agentic workflows.

title: GPT-Rosalind gets smarter for drug discovery
summary: OpenAI updated its GPT-Rosalind series, a life-sciences-specific model built on GPT-5.5's agentic capabilities, with stronger performance in medicinal chemistry, genomics, and wet lab troubleshooting. The company also introduced LifeSciBench, an expert-judged benchmark spanning six real scientific workflow areas. Access is available in research preview to eligible organizations via OpenAI's trusted-access structure.

title: ChatGPT gets personal finance, charts, and a new default model
summary: OpenAI rolled out a personal finance dashboard for Plus users in the US, letting them connect bank accounts and ask questions grounded in their financial data. GPT-5.5 Instant is now the default model for all ChatGPT users, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant, which gets a three-month grace period for paid users. Interactive charts, a full-screen writing editor, and improved multilingual dictation also shipped this week.

title: Google's May blitz: Gemini 3.5, Omni, Googlebook, and more
summary: Google's I/O-anchored May recap confirms Gemini 3.5 as its new frontier agent model and Gemini Omni as a full multimodal creation engine that turns any input into video. New hardware — the Googlebook laptop and Fitbit Air tracker — launched alongside a Universal Cart for cross-service shopping and the Google Health app. The company also committed $10M via its REPLIQA initiative to apply quantum AI to life sciences.

title: June Pixel Drop brings AI video, music, and emergency alerts
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop adds Gemini Omni-powered video creation and original music generation directly on Pixel phones, letting users blend text, images, and clips into custom content. A new Bubbles feature lets any app float as a window for easier multitasking. Emergency Detection now automatically notifies chosen contacts if a crash, fall, or loss of pulse is detected.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234M at a $1.5B valuation, with HCLTech leading at $150M and Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV joining in. The round follows Sarvam's launch of open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year, and the company is targeting a total of $300M for its Series B. The raise cements India's growing role as both a producer and backer of frontier AI.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to watch the watchers
summary: AI agent monitoring startup Coralogix closed a $200M Series F just 11 months after its $115M Series E, valuing the company at $1.6B post-money. The round was led by Advent and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, with Greenfield and Brighton Park joining. The bet: as autonomous software agents proliferate, someone has to monitor, troubleshoot, and govern them.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines and chips
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M at a $2.4B valuation to build AI models for manufacturing complex components like jet engines and semiconductors. Singapore's Temasek led the Series C, with Nvidia, Applied Materials, Intrepid, and M&G Catalyst also in. The startup's valuation has grown nearly three-fold from its last round.

title: Menlo Ventures raises $3B — the Anthropic bet paid off
summary: Menlo Ventures announced its largest fund ever at $3B, driven heavily by its Anthropic stake now worth roughly $14B. The firm's preemptive $500M+ Series D lead in Anthropic back in 2024 — a bet-the-firm move at the time — has become one of venture's biggest recent wins. Their joint $100M startup fund with Anthropic, Anthology, has since deployed closer to $250M.

title: a16z backs Ornn to build a marketplace for AI compute
summary: Ornn raised $33M in a seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz to create a marketplace where AI compute can be bought and sold like a commodity. It marks a16z's first investment in a compute marketplace, with a16z crypto, Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel also participating. The startup is betting that fragmented GPU supply and soaring AI demand create a natural trading venue.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over ChatGPT harms
summary: Florida's Republican Attorney General filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly concealed ChatGPT's risks and marketed it aggressively to residents, including children. The complaint cites deceptive trade practices, dependency-inducing design, data collection from minors, and dangerous outputs including content that could encourage self-harm. The suit is notable as a state-led consumer protection action against an AI company, and it signals a fracture in GOP unity on AI — Florida's AG moved opposite to the Trump administration's light-touch posture.

title: Gemini goes agentic — hard
summary: Google used I/O to launch Gemini 3.5 for multi-step agentic coding and Gemini Omni for video, audio, and image creation from any input. New hardware like the Googlebook and Fitbit Air ships specifically tuned for these models. The Gemini app also gets proactive daily briefs, inbox management, and a Universal Cart that works across Search, YouTube, and Gmail.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weight multimodal model that handles vision and audio natively without separate encoders. It fits inside 16GB of VRAM, making frontier-grade reasoning genuinely laptop-friendly. The Apache 2.0 license and a new Skills Repository make it a strong pick for developers building agentic apps.

title: ChatGPT gets charts, finance, and a new default model
summary: OpenAI promoted GPT-5.5 Instant as the new default for all users and rolled out interactive bar, line, and scatter charts directly in conversations. Plus users in the US can now connect financial accounts and ask ChatGPT questions grounded in their real balance and transaction data. The update also ships full-screen writing blocks, editable messages with attachments, and ChatGPT for Clinicians at no cost for verified US doctors.

title: Pixel Drop: AI video, music, and emergency auto-alerts
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni-powered video creation and original music generation directly to Pixel phones. Any app can now float as a bubble window for easier multitasking, and Android 17 ships alongside Wear OS 7. Most notably, Car Crash Detection and Fall Detection now automatically text your emergency contacts — not just call 911.

title: Sarvam: India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam raised $234M led by HCLTech at a $1.5B valuation, making it India's newest AI unicorn. The startup builds sovereign AI models — including open-source 30B and 105B parameter releases — as governments push for homegrown AI infrastructure. Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participated, and Sarvam is targeting a total $300M Series B.

title: Menlo's Anthropic bet paid off — $14B paid off
summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3B in new funds, its largest raise in 50 years, driven almost entirely by its AI portfolio. Its stake in Anthropic alone is now worth roughly $14B after leading the model maker's Series D at an $18B valuation back in 2024. The firm also quietly scaled its Anthology startup fund from $100M to $250M deployed.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, valuing it at $2.4B — up from roughly $1B at its last round. The startup builds AI simulation models for manufacturing components including jet engines and semiconductors, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among its backers. It's competing in a field that now includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to watch your AI agents
summary: AI monitoring startup Coralogix closed a $200M Series F led by Advent and Canada's CPPIB, valuing it at $1.6B. The thesis: as AI agents proliferate, someone needs to monitor, troubleshoot, and manage them — and Coralogix is betting that's a category as big as cloud observability. The raise comes just 11 months after its $115M Series E, underscoring how fast AI infrastructure investment is accelerating.

title: The Great American AI Act wants to silence the states
summary: Representatives Obernolte and Trahan unveiled a 269-page draft federal AI bill that would preempt state AI laws for three years after enactment. Companies with over $500M in revenue would need to publish AI governance frameworks, report safety incidents, and accept independent audits. A $100M-per-year federal standards center (CAISI) would be created to set benchmarks — but the draft is still a discussion document, not law.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over harm to kids
summary: Florida became the first US state to file a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly concealed ChatGPT's risks and marketed it to children. The complaint cites deceptive trade practices including responses that promote self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and data collection from minors. OpenAI rejected the claims, pointing to existing safety measures, but more states are watching closely.

title: Trump signs AI exec order — voluntary, not mandatory
summary: On June 2, President Trump signed an executive order on AI innovation and cybersecurity that explicitly bars any mandatory licensing or permitting for AI model development. Instead it leans on voluntary cooperation: developers may give the government up to 30 days of early access to frontier models, and a Treasury-run clearinghouse will coordinate vulnerability patching. Critics note the order retreats from the stricter pre-release testing framework that was drafted but pulled in May.

title: UK's CMA gives publishers a way to opt out of Google AI
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed new conduct requirements on Google Search, letting publishers opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews. Google must also provide clear attribution links within AI-generated search results and offer a separate mechanism for publishers to block their content from fine-tuning. The move hands news organizations meaningful leverage they previously lacked.

title: Claude Fable 5 is here — with a locked door inside
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 today, calling it state-of-the-art across software engineering, vision, and scientific research. A stripped-down 'Mythos 5' variant — the same model with certain safeguards removed — is reserved for US government cyberdefenders through Project Glasswing. Both are priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, less than half the cost of the previous Mythos Preview.

title: Gemini moves into Apple's house
summary: At WWDC, Google announced that Apple developers can now call Gemini models directly through Apple's Foundation Models framework starting with iOS 27, macOS 27, and related platforms. Gemini is also integrated into Xcode as an agentic coding assistant that handles multi-step tasks without switching tools. Developers can get started via a free-tier Gemini API key from Google AI Studio.

title: ChatGPT ships interactive charts and a full-screen editor
summary: OpenAI's June 8 update brings interactive bar, line, pie, and scatter charts directly into conversations, along with a full-screen writing editor for long-form documents like essays and PRDs. Paid users can now also edit messages that already have attachments and long-press the send button to pick a one-off model without changing their default.

title: Google gives website owners an AI Search opt-out
summary: Google is testing a new Search Console toggle that lets website owners decide whether their content appears in AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Discover's generative features. Sites that opt out lose AI-driven traffic entirely but the choice won't affect rankings in standard search results. The rollout starts with a subset of UK publishers before going global.

title: Gemma 4 12B brings multimodal AI to your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a locally runnable open model that needs only 16GB of VRAM and is the first mid-sized Gemma to accept native audio input alongside images and text. Its encoder-free architecture pipes all modalities directly into the LLM backbone, pushing benchmark scores close to the larger 26B MoE model. It ships under an Apache 2.0 licence.

title: PhysicsX valued at $2.4B to put AI inside jet engines
summary: British startup PhysicsX raised $300 million in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among returning backers. The company builds AI models that simulate and optimise physical components like jet engines and semiconductors — a market Jeff Bezos is also reportedly pursuing. The round triples its previous valuation of roughly $1 billion.

title: Moonshot AI eyes $30B valuation — its third round in six months
summary: China's Moonshot AI, maker of the Kimi chatbot, is seeking up to $2 billion in new funding at a $30 billion valuation, even as it finalises a separate Meituan-led round at $20 billion. If it closes at target, the startup will have grown its valuation seven-fold since December 2025. The frenzied pace reflects the intensifying capital arms race among Chinese frontier AI labs.

title: Benchmark breaks its own rules with a $2B double fund
summary: Benchmark Capital, famous for keeping funds capped near $425 million, has closed $2 billion across two vehicles: a $1.25 billion growth fund — its first ever — and a $750 million early-stage fund. The growth vehicle will make just five to six large bets on existing and new portfolio companies. Recent AI bets include Cursor, Manus, Sierra, and Legora.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, with HCLTech contributing $150 million as lead strategic investor and Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participating. The company recently launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters and is targeting a $300 million Series B total. The round follows just $41 million raised across its seed and Series A.

title: UK's CMA forces Google to let publishers opt out of AI search
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed conduct requirements on Google Search, giving publishers an opt-out mechanism for AI Overviews and related generative features, as well as the ability to refuse their content being used for fine-tuning. Google must also provide clear attribution with links to source content within AI-generated results. The CMA said it will monitor compliance and consider further measures if needed.

title: Claude Fable 5 arrives — Mythos 5 follows for the few
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 today, calling it the most capable model it has ever made generally available, with state-of-the-art results across software engineering, vision, and scientific research. A companion model, Claude Mythos 5, ships simultaneously but is locked to a narrow group of US government cybersecurity partners via Project Glasswing. Both are priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens — less than half the cost of the previous Mythos Preview.

title: Gemini lands inside Xcode and Apple's Foundation Models
summary: Google announced at WWDC that Apple developers can now call cloud-hosted Gemini models directly through Apple's native Foundation Models framework starting with iOS 27 and macOS 27. Gemini is also integrated into Xcode as an agentic coding assistant, letting developers review code, fix bugs, and build features without leaving the IDE. The integration is available as a preview via the Firebase Apple SDK today.

title: ChatGPT gets interactive charts, full-screen writing, and personal finance
summary: OpenAI pushed a cluster of UX upgrades on June 8: answers can now render interactive bar, line, pie, and scatter charts inline, and longer documents open in a focused full-screen editor with table of contents and download support. A personal finance experience is also rolling out to Plus users in the US, alongside doubled memory capacity for paid subscribers.

title: June Pixel Drop adds AI video, music creation, and emergency sharing
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni-powered video creation and original music generation to Pixel phones, letting users blend text, images, and clips or describe a vibe to generate a full audio track. The update also adds floating app bubbles for multitasking, real-time voice translation on more devices, and automatic emergency contact notifications when crash or fall detection triggers.

title: Cohere ships North Mini Code, its first developer-focused model
summary: Cohere today announced North Mini Code, its first model aimed squarely at developers rather than enterprise deployments. The launch marks a strategic pivot toward the coding assistant market where Anthropic and OpenAI already compete aggressively.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines and chips
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million in a Series C led by Singapore's sovereign fund Temasek, valuing the company at roughly $2.4 billion — up from under $1 billion at its last round. The startup builds AI simulation models for manufacturing high-stakes components like jet engines and semiconductors, and counts Nvidia and Applied Materials as backers alongside new investors Intrepid Growth Partners and M&G Catalyst.

title: Bezos' Prometheus AI valued at $41B in mega-round
summary: Prometheus, the AI startup led by Jeff Bezos, closed $12 billion in new funding at a $41 billion valuation, with JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and BlackRock all writing checks. The raise cements Bezos as one of the most consequential individual backers in the current AI boom alongside his Amazon-adjacent investments.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million in a Series B led by HCLTech, hitting a $1.5 billion valuation and joining the unicorn club. Bessemer Venture Partners joined alongside existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, and the company plans to raise a total of $300 million for the round following earlier open-source model launches in 30B and 105B parameter sizes.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor the AI agent layer
summary: AI observability startup Coralogix closed a $200 million Series F at a $1.6 billion valuation, betting that the explosion of autonomous AI agents will create massive demand for monitoring and troubleshooting infrastructure. The round came just 11 months after its $115 million Series E and was led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.

title: Trump EO demands pre-release frontier model access for the feds
summary: President Trump signed an executive order on June 2 directing agencies to strengthen AI-enabled cybersecurity defenses and establishing a voluntary framework under which frontier model developers would give the federal government up to 30 days of early access before broader public release. The order stops short of any licensing or permitting requirements, maintains a pro-innovation stance, and separately directs the Justice Department to prioritize criminal enforcement against AI-enabled cyberattacks.

title: Illinois passes its own frontier AI Safety Measures Act
summary: The Illinois General Assembly adopted the AI Safety Measures Act on May 29, requiring large frontier AI developers to undergo annual independent audits and publish findings summaries, with the full redacted report submitted to state and attorney general offices. The law takes effect January 1, 2027, adding Illinois to a growing roster of states filling the federal governance vacuum with their own binding frameworks.

title: EU publishes code of practice on labelling AI-generated content
summary: On June 10, the European Commission published a new Code of Practice requiring the marking and labelling of AI-generated content in consumer-facing products, extending EU AI governance obligations beyond the AI Act itself. Combined with draft high-risk classification guidelines still under public consultation, the move leaves organizations with shrinking room to delay EU AI Act compliance planning.

title: Court rules AI prompts used by experts are discoverable in litigation
summary: In Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil, a federal magistrate judge ordered plaintiffs to produce the AI prompts their expert used when preparing her report, treating those inputs as part of discoverable methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that AI-assisted expert work carries real discovery risk, and attorneys should assume prompts could surface in any case.

title: DiffusionGemma goes 4x faster — and open
summary: Google released DiffusionGemma today, an experimental 26B Mixture-of-Experts model that generates entire 256-token blocks simultaneously instead of one token at a time, hitting over 1,000 tokens per second on an H100. It ships under an Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face, making it freely usable for researchers building speed-critical tools like inline editors or code infill systems. Quality trails standard Gemma 4 for now, but the architecture opens genuinely new design space.

title: ChatGPT's model picker gets a plain-English makeover
summary: OpenAI simplified its model selector today, replacing confusing names like Thinking Standard and Thinking Extended with plain tiers — Instant, Medium, High, and Extra High — rolling out to Plus and Pro users globally. The update also lets users toggle whether Instant auto-escalates to Medium when a task demands more reasoning. Separately, GPT-5.5 Instant is now available to all ChatGPT users regardless of plan.

title: Pixel phones get AI video, music, and floating app windows
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni-powered video creation and music generation directly to Pixel devices — you describe an idea or upload a photo and Gemini builds a track with lyrics and custom tempo. A new Bubbles feature lets any app float as a compact overlay, and Emergency Sharing now auto-notifies contacts if Car Crash, Fall, or Loss of Pulse Detection fires. The rollout begins today across Pixel devices.

title: Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5: Google's May recap in one place
summary: Google's May 2026 roundup confirms the full scope of its I/O launches: Gemini Omni handles any-to-video generation, Gemini 3.5 powers multi-step agentic workflows, and the Gemini app now runs proactive background tasks like inbox management and appointment scheduling. New hardware — the Googlebook laptop and Fitbit Air wellness pebble — ships purpose-built for these models. The Universal Cart also launched, letting users add items across Search, YouTube, and Gmail in one checkout flow.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, tripling its valuation from roughly $1B to $2.4B. The startup builds AI simulation models for manufacturing components including jet engines and semiconductors, competing against players backed by Jeff Bezos. Nvidia and Applied Materials, both existing backers, continued their support alongside new investors Intrepid Growth Partners and M&G Catalyst.

title: F2 raises $14M to bring AI to private credit
summary: F2, which uses AI to help credit investors and banks manage complex transactions, closed a $14M seed round led by HighlandX with Y Combinator, Left Lane Capital, NFX, and Torch Capital participating. Total equity raised now stands at $24M. CEO Don Muir told Axios the capital will accelerate the platform's expansion into bank partnerships and larger credit portfolios.

title: Coralogix bets $200M that someone has to watch the agents
summary: AI monitoring startup Coralogix raised a $200M Series F at a $1.6B valuation, just 11 months after its $115M Series E — a pace that reflects accelerating investor appetite for AI infrastructure tooling. The round was led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, with Coralogix arguing that the rise of autonomous agents creates urgent demand for a new monitoring and observability layer. Total funding now sits at $550M.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam closed a $234M funding round led by HCLTech, pushing its valuation to $1.5B and making it one of the country's newest AI unicorns. Bessemer Venture Partners joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV, with Sarvam aiming to raise a total of $300M for the round. The company launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year.

title: The $20M primary that's really about AI regulation
summary: Two competing AI-focused super PACs are pouring a combined $20M into New York's 12th congressional district Democratic primary, making it the most expensive proxy fight yet over how hard Congress should clamp down on AI. The race pits AI regulation advocate Alex Bores against opponents including Assemblyman Micah Lasher and Jack Schlossberg, with each side treating the outcome as a signal about the political viability of aggressive AI oversight. The spending marks a clear escalation from policy debate to direct electoral combat.

title: States keep legislating as Washington stays quiet
summary: Connecticut enacted one of the most comprehensive state AI laws in the US on May 27, covering companion chatbots, frontier model governance, and employment decisions, while Louisiana became the 22nd state to pass a consumer data privacy law. With the Trump administration having abandoned its FDA-for-AI proposal and Congress stalled on the Great American AI Act, state-level rules are now the primary compliance surface for most AI deployments. Multi-state organizations face an accelerating patchwork with no federal preemption in sight.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Corps fellowship
summary: Anthropic announced Claude Corps, a national fellowship program targeting early-career people passionate about bringing AI benefits to communities across America. The launch came alongside two major enterprise deals: TCS and DXC will both integrate Claude into systems used by banks, airlines, and other regulated industries.

title: Google's June Pixel Drop goes heavy on AI creation
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni-powered video creation and AI music generation to Pixel phones, letting users blend text, images, and video into original clips or describe a vibe and get a full audio track back. The update also adds floating app bubbles for multitasking and automatic emergency-contact notifications when crash or fall detection triggers.

title: xAI ships Grok 4 with a government tier
summary: xAI released Grok 4, claiming it is the most intelligent model in the world, with native tool use and real-time search available to SuperGrok and API customers. Alongside it, xAI unveiled Grok For Government, a suite of frontier AI products offered first to U.S. government customers, and a new SuperGrok Heavy tier for the most powerful variant.

title: ChatGPT personal finance rolls out to Plus users
summary: OpenAI began rolling out its personal finance experience in ChatGPT to Plus users in the U.S. on web and iOS, with Android support for Pro and Plus users also live. Eligible users can securely connect supported financial accounts, view a dashboard, and ask ChatGPT questions grounded in their actual financial context.

title: Google expands Gemini into classrooms and study tools
summary: At ISTE 2026, Google unveiled a new Classroom app inside Gemini that lets educators pull in real class context for lesson planning, plus Study Notebooks that generate personalized quizzes adapting as students learn. New Guided Learning tools on Chromebooks are also rolling out to cut down on digital distractions during assignments.

title: Bezos's Prometheus valued at $41 billion
summary: Prometheus, the AI startup led by Jeff Bezos, raised $12 billion in a round valuing the company at $41 billion, with JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Bezos himself all participating. The raise cements Bezos as a major independent player in the AI boom alongside his existing investment in Amazon's AI push.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in a Series B led by HCLTech, with Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also joining. The raise follows the company's release of open-source models at 30 billion and 105 billion parameters and marks a dramatic jump from the $41 million it had raised across its seed and Series A.

title: Equal AI grabs $30M to kill spam calls in India
summary: Equal AI raised $30 million in Series B funding led by Prosus Ventures and Tomales Bay Capital to scale its AI-powered call-screening product for Indian consumers. The round has an unusual tranche structure that lets the startup advertise its highest achieved valuation even though the bulk of equity was sold at a lower price.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million at a $2.4 billion valuation to build AI models for manufacturing complex components like jet engines and semiconductors, tripling its valuation from its last round. Temasek led the Series C, with Nvidia and Applied Materials continuing as backers.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to watch AI agents
summary: Boston-based Coralogix closed a $200 million Series F at a $1.6 billion valuation, betting that the explosion of autonomous AI agents will create massive demand for a new generation of monitoring and observability tools. The round came just 11 months after its $115 million Series E, led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.

title: Court: DOGE used ChatGPT to illegally kill grants
summary: A U.S. District Court ruled that DOGE personnel violated constitutional equal protection and free speech rights when they used ChatGPT to terminate more than $100 million in National Endowment for the Humanities grants, with protected characteristics like race and gender used as targeting criteria. The ruling is one of the most consequential judicial findings yet about the government's misuse of AI tools.

title: EU finalizes AI transparency labeling code
summary: On June 10, the European Commission released the final version of its Transparency Code of Practice under the AI Act, requiring providers to apply machine-readable watermarks or metadata to AI-generated content and deployers to label deepfakes and AI-written text on matters of public interest. The code is the EU's most concrete enforcement mechanism yet for AI content provenance.

title: All 50 states now have AI bills — and they conflict
summary: A new Cloud Security Alliance research note found that U.S. legislators have introduced over 2,182 AI-related bills across all 50 states, with inconsistent definitions, audit timelines, and enforcement mechanisms creating a compliance nightmare for companies operating nationally. The Senate voted 99-1 to strip a proposed 10-year federal moratorium on state AI enforcement from budget reconciliation, leaving the patchwork firmly intact.

title: Pixel gets AI video, music, and bubbles
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop brings Gemini Omni to Pixel phones, letting users generate custom videos and original music tracks just by describing an idea. New floating app bubbles make multitasking easier, and emergency detection now auto-notifies contacts during crashes or falls. The rollout begins today across Pixel devices.

title: GPT-5.2 is gone, GPT-5.5 is everyone's default
summary: OpenAI retired all GPT-5.2 variants today — Instant, Thinking, and Pro — migrating existing conversations automatically to the corresponding GPT-5.5 models. GPT-5.5 Instant is also rolling out to all ChatGPT users globally starting today. The retirement follows the standard 90-day succession window after GPT-5.3 Instant launched.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs frontier multimodal on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open Apache 2.0 model that handles text, images, and audio natively without separate encoders — a first for a mid-sized Gemma model. It runs locally on consumer hardware with just 16 GB of VRAM and benchmarks close to the larger 26B MoE model. Google also released a Skills Repository to help agents build on top of it.

title: Google's agentic Gemini era, fully recapped
summary: Google's May 2026 roundup confirms the full scope of its I/O push: Gemini 3.5 for agentic coding, Gemini Omni for any-to-video generation, Universal Cart across Search and YouTube, and the Googlebook laptop built for Gemini Intelligence. Android Halo gives users a dedicated space to monitor agent progress without disrupting their flow.

title: Mistral eyes €3B raise at nearly double last year's price
summary: French AI lab Mistral is in early talks to raise roughly €3 billion ($3.5B), which would value it at €20 billion — up from €11.7 billion just nine months ago. The round would be one of Europe's largest AI financings ever, though Mistral has raised only about $4B total compared to OpenAI's $186B. No lead investor has been named yet.

title: Bezos' Prometheus hits $41B valuation
summary: Prometheus, Jeff Bezos' AI startup, closed $12 billion in fresh funding from JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Bezos himself, pushing its valuation to $41 billion. The round cements Bezos as a major independent force in AI outside of his Amazon role. Details on Prometheus's specific products remain limited.

title: India's Sarvam crosses the unicorn line at $1.5B
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam raised $234 million led by HCLTech, becoming India's newest AI unicorn at a $1.5 billion valuation. The company is targeting a full $300 million Series B and launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year. Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participated.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor the age of agents
summary: AI observability startup Coralogix closed a $200 million Series F at a $1.6 billion valuation, betting that autonomous AI agents will create a massive new market for monitoring and troubleshooting tools. The round came just 11 months after its $115M Series E, led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board. The company has now raised $550 million in total.

title: US export order kills access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
summary: The US Commerce Department issued an export control directive today ordering Anthropic to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 worldwide. Anthropic published a brief statement confirming compliance and flagging potential policy fallout for AI safety frameworks. The move marks one of the most direct uses of export law to restrict frontier AI model access.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over harm to children
summary: Florida became the first US state to sue OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly released addictive and harmful chatbot technology that has hurt minors. The suit seeks restrictions on data collection from under-13s and signals potential further action against other AI developers. OpenAI rejected the claims, pointing to its existing safety and parental controls.

title: Colorado scraps its AI Act, rewrites the rules
summary: Colorado replaced its landmark 2024 AI Act with SB 26-189, stripping out algorithmic discrimination requirements and shifting to a lighter notice-and-disclosure regime for automated decision-making. The rewrite followed an X.AI lawsuit and DOJ intervention that froze the original law, pushing its effective date to January 1, 2027. The move signals that states are still actively shaping — and reshaping — their AI governance experiments.

title: AI prompts now fair game in federal court discovery
summary: A federal magistrate judge in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil ruled that AI prompts used by an expert witness are discoverable as part of her methodology, not protected drafting material. The decision is one of the sharpest judicial signals yet that AI-assisted expert work will face new scrutiny in litigation. Legal teams using AI for expert preparation should treat their prompts as potential exhibits.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs multimodal on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a model that ditches separate audio and vision encoders entirely — both flow straight into the LLM backbone. It runs locally on 16GB of VRAM, supports native audio input, and is available under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and Kaggle. Performance reportedly approaches Google's larger 26B MoE model at less than half the memory footprint.

title: GPT-5.5 Instant gets a readability overhaul
summary: OpenAI updated GPT-5.5 Instant to produce more natural, better-paced responses with fewer bullet-heavy walls of text. As part of the update, the Canvas editing interface is being deprecated for this model tier — writing and code now live directly in chat via blocks. Paid users get a grace period on Canvas through legacy models before they're sunset.

title: Google's May I/O recap: Gemini Omni, Googlebook, Universal Cart
summary: Google's official May 2026 roundup confirms Gemini Omni can generate video from any combination of text, audio, image, or video input. The Googlebook — a Gemini-native laptop built with Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo — adds a Magic Pointer for contextual suggestions. Universal Cart lets users add items while browsing Search, YouTube, or Gmail, all from one checkout hub.

title: Android's June drop adds book insights and safety tools
summary: Google's June Android update brings Book Insights to Google Play Books, surfacing key ideas from select English titles — thousands of which are free. The drop also includes new personalization and safety features baked into the OS.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation, with HCLTech writing the lead $150M check. Bessemer, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also joined the Series B, which Sarvam aims to grow to $300M total. The company has already shipped open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters this year.

title: No revenue, no problem: how AI startups inflate valuations
summary: Forbes details how Ineffable Intelligence raised $1.1 billion at a $5.1 billion seed valuation despite having no product or revenue — its valuation jumped 70x in a matter of weeks between two tranches. Lightspeed, Index, DST Global, and Sequoia all participated at the elevated price. The UK's sovereign AI fund, backed by British taxpayers, also wrote a check.

title: Baseten hits $13B valuation on $1.5B raise
summary: AI infrastructure startup Baseten closed a $1.5 billion round led by Sands Capital and Wellington Management, pushing its valuation to $13 billion. Australian VC Blackbird made its largest-ever single investment in the round. Baseten provides the compute layer for businesses building and running AI tools.

title: Genesis AI unveils non-humanoid robot with $105M in the bank
summary: French robotics startup Genesis AI, backed by ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt, revealed its first general-purpose robot — pointedly not humanoid in design. The company has raised $105M, matching Mistral AI's record European seed round. Founded in early 2025, Genesis is betting that a non-humanoid form factor gives it an edge in a crowded field.

title: General Intuition banks $320M to train AI on gaming content
summary: General Intuition, which uses gaming data as its core training signal, raised $320 million in a Khosla-led Series A at a $2.3 billion valuation — and is already scouting a Series B. General Catalyst, Hedosophia, Bezos Expeditions, and Nico Rosberg also joined the cap table.

title: Trump pulls the plug on Anthropic's Mythos — then partially relents
summary: The Trump administration ordered Anthropic to suspend customer access to its Mythos and Fable 5 models, citing national security concerns over Mythos's ability to exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed. Anthropic complied but publicly disagreed, warning the move could set a dangerous regulatory precedent. By Friday, the government partially reversed course, allowing Mythos to be redeployed to a small group of vetted cyber defenders.

title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol also gated behind government approval
summary: OpenAI announced that its new GPT-5.6 Sol model will only be accessible to customers pre-approved by the Trump administration, following the same framework applied to Anthropic. CEO Sam Altman negotiated directly with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick this week. A Democratic congresswoman called the arrangement lawless — "no law, no process, no oversight, just appointees deciding who's in and who's out."

title: States pile on: Florida sues OpenAI, NY subpoenas follow
summary: Florida's attorney general filed the first state civil lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman, a sprawling 83-page complaint alleging the company prioritized profit over safety and engaged in false advertising. Separately, New York, joined by 41 other states, issued a sweeping subpoena demanding OpenAI documents on advertising, user engagement, data handling, and policies for minors and seniors.

title: Court rules AI prompts are discoverable in litigation
summary: A federal magistrate judge ordered a plaintiff to hand over the AI prompts its expert used to prepare a legal report, ruling they are part of the expert's methodology rather than protected drafting material. The case, Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil, is one of the clearest signals yet that AI-assisted legal work leaves a discoverable paper trail.

title: Claude Fable 5 lands — with a locked door behind it
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, its most capable publicly available model, topping nearly every benchmark in software engineering, science, and vision tasks. A secret sibling, Claude Mythos 5, ships simultaneously but only to US government cyberdefense partners via Project Glasswing, with safeguards on biology and cybersecurity lifted. Pricing comes in at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output — less than half the cost of the previous Mythos Preview.

title: Gemma 4 12B: multimodal AI that fits on a laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weight model (Apache 2.0) that runs locally on just 16GB of VRAM and is the first mid-sized Gemma to natively accept audio input. Its encoder-free architecture pipes vision and audio directly into the LLM backbone, achieving benchmark scores close to the 26B MoE model. Multi-Token Prediction drafters keep latency low for real-world agentic use.

title: Google's May mega-drop: Gemini 3.5, Omni, Googlebook, and more
summary: Google I/O 2026 officially kicked off the 'agentic Gemini era' with Gemini 3.5 for complex multi-step workflows and Gemini Omni for any-input-to-video creation. Hardware arrived too: Fitbit Air, a discreet wellness pebble, and the Googlebook laptop built for Gemini Intelligence with a Magic Pointer and cross-device Android features. Universal Cart now lets users add items across Search, YouTube, Gmail, and Gemini in a single shopping hub.

title: ChatGPT Images 2.0 and a personal finance hub roll out
summary: OpenAI shipped ChatGPT Images 2.0, a new image generation model, alongside a personal finance experience now live for Plus users on web and iOS. GPT-5.5 Instant also received a quality upgrade targeting decision-making, planning, and shopping conversations, rolling out first to Plus and Pro users in the US. A new behind-the-scenes speech-to-text model for dictation quietly replaced the old one across all plans.

title: Sarvam: India's freshest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam raised $234 million in a Series B round led by HCLTech, vaulting to a $1.5 billion valuation and joining India's unicorn club. Bessemer Venture Partners joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, and Sarvam is targeting a total raise of $300 million. The company recently open-sourced models at 30B and 105B parameters, positioning itself as a sovereign AI infrastructure play.

title: Menlo Ventures raises $3B — Anthropic made them do it
summary: Menlo Ventures announced a $3 billion fund raise, the largest in its 50-year history, driven by a bet-the-firm $500 million investment in Anthropic's 2024 Series D. That stake is now worth roughly $14 billion, turning white-knuckle risk into the VC story of the year. The new fund signals that early concentrated AI bets are producing generational returns for believers.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B to bring AI to jet engines and chips
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million at a $2.4 billion valuation, led by Singapore's Temasek, to build AI models for manufacturing complex components like jet engines and semiconductors. Nvidia and Applied Materials backed previous rounds and remain investors, underlining the hardware industry's appetite for physics-aware AI. The valuation is more than double its prior round, reflecting surging demand for industrial AI.

title: a16z backs Ornn's $33M compute marketplace
summary: Andreessen Horowitz led a $33 million seed round into Ornn, a marketplace where AI compute power can be bought and sold, marking a16z's first investment in a compute exchange. Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel also participated, with a16z's crypto arm joining for the decentralised infrastructure angle. The bet reflects growing conviction that GPU capacity is a commodity asset class in its own right.

title: Pramaana Labs pulls $27M to apply formal verification to AI
summary: Pramaana Labs secured $27 million in seed funding led by Khosla Ventures, with Accel, Nexus Venture Partners, and Premji Invest among participants, to bring formal verification techniques to AI systems. The approach aims to mathematically prove AI behavior rather than rely solely on empirical testing, addressing reliability concerns at the frontier. It is a rare bet on foundational AI safety infrastructure over application-layer tooling.

title: Anthropic kills foreign access to Fable 5 on US order
summary: Anthropic disabled access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for foreign nationals after receiving a Commerce Department export directive citing national security. European observers called it proof of US dominance and the Trump administration's desire for control over frontier AI. The move is being closely watched as a live test of how export-control law intersects with AI safety governance frameworks.

title: UK watchdog gives publishers opt-out from Google AI summaries
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed new conduct requirements on Google Search, giving publishers the right to opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews and to refuse fine-tuning data use. Google must also provide clear attribution and links in AI-generated results, restoring some bargaining power for news organisations. The CMA said it will monitor implementation and consider further measures if needed.

title: Court rules expert AI prompts are discoverable in litigation
summary: A federal magistrate judge in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil ordered a plaintiff to produce the AI prompts its expert used when preparing her report, treating them as part of her methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that AI-assisted expert work opens up new discovery battlegrounds. Litigators are now on notice that every prompt their experts run may end up in opposing counsel's hands.

title: Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most powerful public model yet
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 today, a Mythos-class model it describes as state-of-the-art across software engineering, scientific research, and vision tasks. A restricted 'Mythos 5' variant — the same underlying model with cyber safeguards lifted — is being deployed through a US government partnership called Project Glasswing. Both models are priced at $10 per million input tokens, less than half the cost of the previous Mythos Preview.

title: Google recaps a month of agentic Gemini launches
summary: Google's May 2026 roundup covers Gemini 3.5 for agentic coding, Gemini Omni for multimodal creation from any input, and a slate of new hardware including the Googlebook laptop and Fitbit Air tracker. New consumer features include Universal Cart for cross-merchant shopping and an Android Halo interface for monitoring AI agents running in the background.

title: ChatGPT gets interactive charts, a full-screen editor, and CarPlay
summary: OpenAI's latest release notes bundle several quality-of-life upgrades: answers can now render interactive bar, line, and scatter charts inline, and a full-screen writing block handles long-form documents with a table of contents and download support. ChatGPT also rolled out hands-free access via Apple CarPlay and launched a free 'ChatGPT for Clinicians' tier for verified US healthcare providers.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs multimodal AI on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B under an Apache 2.0 license, a mid-sized open model designed to run locally on consumer hardware with just 16GB of RAM. It ditches traditional multimodal encoders entirely, routing vision and audio directly into the LLM backbone, and includes native audio input support — a first for the Gemma family at this size.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam raised $234 million in a Series B led by HCLTech, pushing its valuation to $1.5 billion and cementing its status as a unicorn. Bessemer Venture Partners joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, and Sarvam is targeting a total of $300 million for the round after launching open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year.

title: NewCore raises $66M to give AI agents real identities
summary: Cybersecurity startup NewCore emerged from stealth with $66 million in seed funding, targeting the growing problem of authenticating and governing AI agents as enterprises deploy them at scale. The round was led by Cyberstarts with Index Ventures and Evolution Equity Partners participating, valuing NewCore at $300 million post-investment.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B valuation with $300M raise for manufacturing AI
summary: London-based PhysicsX, which builds AI models for manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors, closed a $300 million Series C led by Singapore's Temasek. Nvidia and Applied Materials are among its backers, and the round tripled its valuation from roughly $1 billion at its last raise.

title: Coralogix banks $200M to watch the AI agent layer
summary: Observability startup Coralogix raised $200 million in a Series F, betting that the proliferation of autonomous AI agents will generate massive demand for monitoring and troubleshooting infrastructure. The round, led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, values the company at $1.6 billion and follows a $115 million raise just 11 months ago.

title: UK bans romantic AI chatbots for under-18s and social media for under-16s
summary: The UK government announced today it will ban 'romantic companion' AI chatbots for all users under 18 and social media access for under-16s, following Australia's lead. Ofcom has been ordered to rapidly study age-assurance measures, with the first tranche of regulations expected before Parliament by end of 2026 and entering force in Spring 2027.

title: Anthropic's Fable 5 hit with Commerce Department export directive
summary: The US Commerce Department issued an export directive that forced Anthropic to temporarily disable Fable 5 and Mythos access for certain users, creating a live collision between national security export controls and AI safety governance. Policy analysts flagged potential fallout for AI safety frameworks if export control logic begins shaping which users can access frontier models.

title: States keep writing AI laws Congress won't
summary: Connecticut's sweeping AI law — covering companion chatbots, frontier model governance, and AI in employment — became the most substantive state-level AI framework in the US to date after its May 27 enactment, while Louisiana became the 22nd state to pass consumer data privacy legislation. A proposed 10-year federal moratorium on state AI enforcement was crushed 99-1 in the Senate, leaving a patchwork of 2,182-plus AI-related bills across all 50 states.

title: Court rules AI prompts used by experts are discoverable in litigation
summary: A federal magistrate judge ordered a plaintiff to hand over the AI prompts its expert used to prepare a litigation report, treating them as part of the expert's methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil sets a significant precedent: if an expert outsourced analytical work to an AI, opposing counsel can demand to see exactly how they asked the question.

title: Pixel Drop: Gemini makes you a director
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop is rolling out today, bringing Gemini Omni-powered video creation, AI music generation from photos or text prompts, and Screen Reactions that embed your selfie into screen recordings. Multitasking gets a boost too via floating app Bubbles, and emergency features now auto-notify your contacts during car crashes or falls. The updates hit Pixel devices starting today.

title: Gemini 3.5 and the agentic Google era
summary: Google's May recap confirms the company has fully pivoted to an agentic model, with Gemini 3.5 handling complex multi-step workflows and Gemini Omni creating video from any combination of inputs. New surfaces include the Googlebook laptop, the Google Health app, Fitbit Air, and a Universal Cart that works across Search, YouTube, and Gmail. Gemini 3.5 Pro is expected to land before the end of June.

title: Boogu-Image-0.1 debuts as an open-source image powerhouse
summary: Boogu-Image-0.1 launched today on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license, offering a full family of models covering text-to-image, image editing, and a four-step Turbo variant for fast photorealistic generation. The model supports both English and Chinese text rendering and is described as competitive with leading closed alternatives. A ComfyUI integration ships tomorrow.

title: Gemma 4 12B brings multimodal AI to your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B earlier this month, a model that fits in 16GB of VRAM and matches the performance of its 26B MoE sibling on key benchmarks. It is the first mid-sized Gemma model to accept native audio input, with vision and audio flowing directly into the LLM backbone without separate encoders. It ships under Apache 2.0 and is available across Google Cloud and consumer hardware.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Sarvam raised $234 million in a Series B round led by HCLTech, valuing the Indian AI startup at $1.5 billion. Bessemer Venture Partners joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, and the company is targeting a total raise of $300 million. Sarvam had previously raised just $41 million combined across its seed and Series A, making this a dramatic step-up built on its open-source 30B and 105B parameter models.

title: Menlo Ventures cashes in on its Anthropic bet
summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3 billion in new funds — its largest raise in 50 years — driven largely by its Anthropic stake, now worth roughly $14 billion. The firm made a bet-the-company move in 2024, preemptively leading Anthropic's Series D with more than $500 million when the model maker was valued at $18 billion. Its companion $100 million Anthology fund has since deployed closer to $250 million.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million at a $2.4 billion valuation in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among returning backers. The startup builds AI models that simulate the physics of manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors, a field attracting competition from Jeff Bezos-backed ventures. The new valuation is roughly 2.5 times what the company was worth at its last round.

title: Pramaana Labs raises $27M to fact-check AI with formal verification
summary: Pramaana Labs closed a $27 million seed round led by Khosla Ventures, with Accel, Nexus Venture Partners, Premji Invest, and others participating, to bring formal mathematical verification techniques to AI systems. The startup argues that as AI takes on higher-stakes decisions, probabilistic testing alone is insufficient and provable correctness is needed. The announcement is slated for Wednesday.

title: ChatGPT's market share falls below 50%
summary: For the first time, ChatGPT's share of the AI chatbot market has dropped below 50%, driven by accelerating competition from Gemini and Claude. The milestone underscores how quickly the landscape has diversified since ChatGPT's 2022 launch, when it effectively was the market. The decline coincides with mounting legal pressure on OpenAI, including Florida's state-led lawsuit alleging the company concealed safety risks.

title: Courts rule AI prompts are discoverable evidence
summary: A federal magistrate judge in Connecticut ordered a plaintiff's expert to hand over the AI prompts used to prepare her report in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil, treating them as part of the expert's methodology rather than protected work product. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that litigants cannot shield AI-assisted analysis from discovery. Legal teams using AI in expert work now face a new layer of evidentiary exposure.

title: GPT-5.5 Instant takes the default seat
summary: OpenAI has replaced GPT-5.3 Instant with GPT-5.5 Instant as the default model for all ChatGPT users, promising sharper accuracy, better image understanding, and smarter web-search decisions. Paid users get a three-month grace period to keep using 5.3 before it retires. The rollout also brings a new Scheduled Tasks page so users can manage recurring AI work from one place in the sidebar.

title: June Pixel Drop: AI music, video, and emergency sharing
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop lands Android 17 and Wear OS 7 alongside a batch of Gemini-powered creative tools — users can now generate original music tracks from a photo or text prompt and edit videos through natural conversation with Gemini Omni. Emergency Detection now automatically pings chosen contacts when Crash, Fall, or Loss of Pulse Detection fires. Floating app bubbles and Voice Translate on Pixel 10a round out the quality-of-life additions.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs frontier reasoning on a laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open Apache 2.0 model that sits between its 4B edge model and the 26B MoE, fitting into 16 GB of VRAM with native audio input and no separate multimodal encoders. Benchmark performance reportedly approaches the larger 26B sibling, making it a practical local option for agentic and coding workflows. Google is also shipping a Skills Repository so developers can plug Gemma directly into agent pipelines.

title: Boogu-Image-0.1 Turbo ships with ComfyUI support
