summary: Boogu released its open-source unified image generation family today, including Base, Turbo, and Edit variants under an Apache 2.0 licence. The Turbo variant uses four-step distillation for fast photorealistic output, while the Edit model handles image-to-image transformations from a single reference. ComfyUI integration also dropped today, making it plug-and-play for existing local-gen workflows.

title: Kling AI eyes $2B raise at $18B valuation
summary: Kuaishou's video AI unit Kling AI is in advanced talks with General Atlantic to anchor a funding round targeting over $2 billion, which would value the company at $18 billion — down from an initial $20 billion ask. The round is being structured ahead of a planned IPO, and landing a major US backer is a key strategic goal for the Chinese firm. Kling competes in an increasingly crowded AI video generation market alongside Sora, Runway, and others.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam has closed $234 million of a targeted $300 million Series B, reaching a $1.5 billion valuation and joining India's unicorn club. HCLTech anchored the round with $150 million, joined by Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV Partners. The company launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year and positions itself as sovereign AI infrastructure for India.

title: Pramaana Labs bags $27M to verify AI with math
summary: Pramaana Labs announced a $27 million seed round led by Khosla Ventures, with Accel, Nexus Venture Partners, Premji Invest, and others participating. The startup is applying formal verification — the technique used to prove chip and software correctness — to AI systems, aiming to give enterprises provable guarantees about model behaviour. It is one of the largest seed rounds in the formal-methods-meets-AI space to date.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B on AI for jet engines and chips
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300 million in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, lifting its valuation to roughly $2.4 billion — up from just under $1 billion at its last round. The startup builds AI models that simulate the physics of high-stakes manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among its existing backers. The raise signals deepening institutional appetite for AI applied to physical-world engineering.

title: Connecticut sets a new US state AI benchmark
summary: Connecticut enacted one of the most comprehensive state AI laws in the US on May 27, covering companion chatbots, frontier model governance, and AI use in employment decisions. The law adds to a rapidly thickening patchwork of state obligations as Congress continues to stall on federal AI legislation. Legal analysts are calling it a new floor for what substantive state-level AI governance looks like.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over ChatGPT safety concealment
summary: Florida's Attorney General filed the first state-led civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly hid serious risks of ChatGPT and marketed it aggressively to residents including children. The complaint cites deceptive trade practices, responses that promote self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and data collection from minors. The suit is being watched as a test of whether consumer protection law can impose AI safety accountability in the absence of federal rules.

title: Gemma 4 12B lands on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, its first mid-sized open model with native audio input and a novel encoder-free architecture that handles vision, audio, and text directly in the LLM backbone. It runs locally with just 16GB of VRAM and benchmarks close to the larger 26B MoE model. Released under Apache 2.0, it also ships with a Skills Repository to help agents build agentic workflows with Gemma.

title: Codex gets plugins, annotations, and Sites
summary: OpenAI expanded Codex today with six new role-specific plugins that make it useful for non-coders, plus inline annotations for refining results in place. A new Sites feature — rolling out in preview for Business and Enterprise — lets Codex generate interactive dashboards and apps shareable via URL within a workspace.

title: ChatGPT gets World Cup mode and pronunciation audio
summary: OpenAI's June 18 release notes add conversational World Cup coverage — schedules, predictions, and team storylines — alongside text-and-audio pronunciation guidance in over 60 languages. The update also streamlines conversation sharing to a single click and lets users highlight text to start a note or save to their Library.

title: ChatGPT Enterprise gets spend controls and credit analytics
summary: OpenAI launched a Global Admin Console for ChatGPT Enterprise that unifies ChatGPT and Codex credit usage into one view, with breakdowns by user, product, and model. Admins can now set workspace-wide default limits, configure group-level caps, and approve individual credit requests — giving large deployments real budget discipline for the first time.

title: June Pixel Drop brings AI video, music, and floating apps
summary: Google's June Pixel Drop rolls out Gemini Omni-powered video creation and music generation directly on Pixel phones — just describe an idea or upload a photo and get a full audio track or video clip. Multitasking gets a boost with Bubbles, which turns any app into a floating window, and emergency features now auto-notify contacts during crash or fall detection events.

title: Baseten raising $1.5B — valuation tripled in five months
summary: AI inference startup Baseten is finalizing a $1.5B round co-led by Spark Capital, Sands Capital, Altimeter, and Wellington Management, which would value it at $13B — up from $5B just five months ago. The WSJ notes it's a split-priced round, with some investors coming in at $11B, a sign of how startups are engineering headline numbers. The speed of re-ups here is a proxy for how hot inference infrastructure has become.

title: General Intuition eyes $300M at $2B to teach agents space and time
summary: General Intuition, a New York startup that spun out of gaming clip platform Medal just eight months ago with a $134M seed, is now in talks to raise $300M at a $2B valuation. The company is building a foundation model that trains AI agents to navigate spatial and temporal environments. Backers reportedly include Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt alongside Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst.

title: Sarvam hits unicorn status with $234M led by HCLTech
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam closed a $234M funding round at a $1.5B valuation, with HCLTech committing $150M as lead strategic investor. Bessemer Venture Partners joined existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners. The raise comes after Sarvam launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year and is targeting a total of $300M for its Series B.

title: Swiss privacy-first AI startup Prem targets $100M Series A
summary: Prem AI, based in Switzerland and focused on helping hedge funds and law firms run AI models on private infrastructure, is raising $100M at a target valuation of at least $500M. CEO Simone Giacomelli says the round is expected to close in Q3. The raise reflects growing enterprise demand for sovereign, on-premise AI deployments that keep sensitive data out of public clouds.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over ChatGPT safety cover-up
summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed the first state-led civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly concealed ChatGPT's serious risks — including responses that promote self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and data collection from minors. The suit is framed under deceptive trade practices law and cites a specific incident in which a man died after interacting with the chatbot. Congress has yet to act, leaving state AGs to advance the accountability fight.

title: Courts rule AI expert prompts are discoverable evidence
summary: A federal magistrate in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil ordered plaintiffs to hand over the AI prompts their expert used in preparing her report, treating them as part of methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that AI-assisted expert work is fully in scope for litigation discovery. Lawyers relying on AI tools for case preparation now face a new exposure they cannot paper over.

title: UK CMA forces Google to let publishers opt out of AI search
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed new conduct requirements on Google Search, giving publishers the right to opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews and for fine-tuning AI models. Google must also provide clear attribution with links inside AI-generated results. The intervention is one of the first concrete regulatory wins for news publishers in the AI era and a model other regulators may follow.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, its first mid-sized open model with native audio and vision inputs and no multimodal encoders — just a clean LLM backbone. It fits in 16GB of VRAM, benchmarks near the larger 26B MoE model, and ships under Apache 2.0. Developers can run it locally via Hugging Face Transformers, llama.cpp, or MLX from day one.

title: ChatGPT gets a personal finance dashboard
summary: OpenAI is rolling out a personal finance experience to Plus users in the US, letting them securely connect bank and investment accounts and ask ChatGPT questions grounded in their actual financial data. The same release bumps GPT-5.5 Instant to default status for all users and ships ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets globally. The spreadsheet integration lives in a sidebar and handles formulas, budgets, and multi-tab cleanup in place.

title: Google's Gemini Omni can create video from anything
summary: Google's May recap confirms Gemini Omni as its new any-in, video-out model — combine images, audio, video, and text as input and get high-quality video grounded in real-world knowledge back out. Alongside it, Gemini 3.5 Flash is live for agentic coding and long-horizon tasks, with the Pro tier expected before end of June. The Googlebook laptop line from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo is built around these models.

title: OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind goes enterprise for drug discovery
summary: OpenAI updated GPT-Rosalind, its life-sciences model, with GPT-5.5's agentic coding layered on top of stronger medicinal chemistry and genomics intelligence. The company also unveiled LifeSciBench, an externally expert-judged benchmark covering six workflow areas from evidence handling to wet-lab troubleshooting. Access is opening in research preview to eligible organizations globally via a trusted-access structure.

title: Gemini comes to Google Classroom
summary: Google unveiled a new Classroom app inside Gemini that lets teachers pull real class context into AI-assisted task planning securely. Students get Study Notebooks — personalized, adaptive lessons and quizzes — rolling out now to personal accounts. Chromebooks are also gaining Guided Learning tools designed to cut digital distractions during assignments.

title: Menlo Ventures closes $3B on the back of Anthropic
summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3 billion in new funds — its largest raise in 50 years — with its Anthropic stake now worth roughly $14 billion after leading the model maker's Series D at an $18B valuation in 2024. The firm's co-investment vehicle Anthology has also grown from $100M to nearly $250M deployed. It's a case study in concentrated conviction paying off spectacularly.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Indian AI startup Sarvam closed $234M of a targeted $300M Series B at a $1.5B valuation, with HCLTech contributing $150M as lead strategic investor. Bessemer, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also joined. The round follows Sarvam's launch of 30B and 105B open-source models and marks its leap from $41M raised across seed and Series A.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor the agent layer
summary: Boston-based Coralogix pulled in $200M in a Series F — just 11 months after its $115M Series E — betting that the proliferation of autonomous AI agents will spike demand for observability tooling. The round, led by Advent and CPPIB, values the company at $1.6B post-money and brings total raised to $550M. The company argues agents fail silently in ways traditional monitoring tools can't catch.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B valuation for manufacturing AI
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, tripling its valuation to $2.4B. The startup builds AI models for designing complex manufactured components like jet engines and semiconductors, and counts Nvidia and Applied Materials among its backers. It's competing in a space that now includes Jeff Bezos-backed rivals.

title: a16z backs compute marketplace Ornn
summary: Andreessen Horowitz led a $33M seed round into Ornn, a marketplace where AI compute capacity can be bought and sold like a commodity. The a16z crypto arm participated alongside Galaxy Ventures and SV Angel — marking a16z's first bet on a compute trading venue. General partner Ali Yahya called it a foundational missing layer in the AI infrastructure stack.

title: AI prompts are now discoverable in court
summary: A federal magistrate judge in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil ordered plaintiffs to hand over the AI prompts their expert used to prepare her report, ruling the prompts are part of the expert's methodology — not protected drafting material. The decision is one of the clearest signals yet that AI-assisted legal work carries new disclosure obligations. Litigators are now rethinking how they document AI tool use in expert work product.

title: Colorado reenacts and expands its AI law
summary: Colorado quietly reenacted its landmark AI legislation in May 2026, replacing the original version with a sharper focus on adverse outcomes in high-stakes decisions — hiring, lending, housing — that use AI. Organizations doing business in Colorado must map their AI decision-making by January 1, 2027. The move adds to the growing state-level patchwork filling the vacuum left by stalled federal legislation.

title: State AGs investigate OpenAI's safety practices
summary: A coalition of state attorneys general has opened a joint investigation into OpenAI, seeking records on advertising, user engagement, data handling, and protections for minors and older adults. The inquiry adds to legal pressure from Florida's civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman over alleged concealment of ChatGPT safety risks. The xAI trade-secret lawsuit against OpenAI was separately dismissed with prejudice by a federal judge this week.

title: Claude Fable 5 arrives — with a built-in safety net
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, calling it state-of-the-art across software engineering, vision, and scientific research — especially on long, complex tasks. The catch: a classifier system intercepts cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry queries and hands them off to the less capable Claude Opus 4.8 instead. Pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output, less than half the cost of the previous Mythos Preview.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop, no encoder needed
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a mid-sized open model that skips the usual vision and audio encoders entirely — inputs flow straight into the LLM backbone, cutting latency and memory use. It fits in 16GB of VRAM, making it the first Gemma model genuinely comfortable on a consumer laptop. The Apache 2.0 license and compatibility with Hugging Face, llama.cpp, and MLX make it an easy grab for developers.

title: ChatGPT gets a personal finance dashboard and clinician mode
summary: OpenAI rolled out a personal finance experience letting Plus users in the US securely link bank accounts and interrogate their spending through chat. Separately, verified US clinicians can now access a free ChatGPT tier built for real clinical work, including evidence review, documentation support, and CME credit eligibility. Both features reflect OpenAI's push to move ChatGPT from general assistant toward domain-specific professional tool.

title: Google's agentic era: Gemini 3.5, Universal Cart, and the Googlebook
summary: Google's May recap confirmed the full scope of its Google I/O push: Gemini 3.5 for agentic coding and long-horizon tasks, a Universal Cart that lets you add items across Search, YouTube, and Gmail in one place, and the Googlebook — a new laptop form factor built for Gemini Intelligence, made by Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo. summary: Groq closed a $650 million round led by existing investors Disruptive and Infinitum, aiming to expand its data center capacity and reposition itself as an AI computing provider rather than a chip maker. summary: London-based PhysicsX, which builds AI models for manufacturing components like jet engines and semiconductors, raised $300 million at a $2.4 billion valuation — up from roughly $1 billion at its last round. Temasek led the Series C, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among the returning backers. The company competes in a field that now includes Jeff Bezos-backed entrants.

summary: Cybersecurity startup NewCore came out of stealth with $66 million in seed funding to solve what it calls the coming crisis of AI agent authentication — how to verify, govern, and revoke access for autonomous systems acting as employees. Cyberstarts led the round, with Index Ventures and Evolution Equity Partners participating, valuing NewCore at $300 million post-investment.

summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, its first mid-sized open-weight model with native audio input and no separate multimodal encoders — vision and audio flow straight into the LLM backbone. title: Google Home Speaker brings Gemini to your living room
summary: Google's first Gemini-native smart speaker is available for pre-order at $99.99, shipping June 25. It ditches rigid command phrases for natural multi-step conversation, ships with 10 new voices and a short-term conversational memory, and pairs with Google TV Streamer for spatial surround sound. A Google Home Premium subscription unlocks camera history search and home briefs.

title: Gemini 3.5 and Omni anchor Google's agentic era
summary: Google's May I/O recap confirms Gemini 3.5 as the backbone for multi-step agentic workflows across Search, the Gemini app, Stitch, and the new Googlebook laptop line. Gemini Omni extends the model to unified video, audio, image, and text generation. Highlights include Android Halo for managing agents, Universal Cart for cross-merchant shopping, and information agents that monitor the web 24/7.

title: OpenAI's model cadence: GPT-5.5, Codex Remote, and personal finance
summary: OpenAI has been shipping fast: GPT-5.5 Instant is rolling out to all ChatGPT users, Codex Remote is now generally available on all plans, and a personal finance dashboard launched for Plus users in the US. ChatGPT for Clinicians — a free, CME-eligible tool for verified US doctors — also went live, alongside ChatGPT Images 2.0 on all tiers.

title: Claude Opus 4.1 quietly upgrades Anthropic's top model
summary: Anthropic pushed Claude Opus 4.1 as an incremental update to Opus 4, improving performance on complex reasoning, analysis, and creative tasks. The release notes also confirm a new sandboxed Python code execution tool via API and expanded controls for Team and Enterprise plans to manage desktop extensions.

title: Menlo Ventures closes $3B fund on the back of its Anthropic jackpot
summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3 billion in new funds — its largest raise in 50 years — largely powered by its early bet on Anthropic, whose stake is now estimated at $14 billion. title: Groq raises $650M to reinvent itself as an AI compute provider
summary: Groq secured $650 million led by existing investors Disruptive and Infinitum to expand data center capacity and pivot from chip design toward selling AI inference infrastructure. The round comes after Groq's high-profile Nvidia deal shifted its strategic focus away from its LPU hardware roots. The company is now positioning itself as a cloud-like compute marketplace for AI workloads.

title: Bezos's Prometheus hits $41B valuation
summary: Prometheus, the AI startup led by Jeff Bezos, raised $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation from JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Bezos himself. The round cements Bezos as one of the most consequential individual investors in the current AI wave. Few details about Prometheus's actual products have been made public.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn at $1.5B

title: Trump signs AI executive order — voluntary, not mandatory
summary: President Trump signed an executive order on June 2 directing federal agencies to harden systems against AI-enabled cyber threats and establishing a voluntary pre-release review process for frontier models — companies are asked, not required, to give NSA and DOD up to 30 days of early access. The order explicitly bans any new licensing or permitting regime for AI development. Industry players including Microsoft and Anthropic endorsed it as innovation-friendly.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over ChatGPT safety risks
summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed the first state-led civil lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly concealed ChatGPT's dangers and marketed it to children. The complaint cites deceptive trade practices including responses that promoted self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and data collection from minors. The lawsuit was partly prompted by a Florida State University shooting in which the gunman had used ChatGPT.

title: Court rules AI prompts are discoverable in litigation
summary: In Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil Company, a federal magistrate judge ordered plaintiffs to produce the AI prompts their expert used when preparing a legal report, treating them as part of the expert's methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that using AI in expert work opens those inputs to discovery. Litigators using AI tools will need to treat prompt design as part of their evidentiary record.

title: Connecticut enacts one of the US's most comprehensive state AI laws
summary: Connecticut's new AI law, enacted May 27, covers companion chatbots, frontier model governance, and AI use in employment decisions — making it one of the broadest state-level frameworks in the country. It adds to a growing patchwork alongside Colorado's revised law (delayed to January 2027 after an xAI lawsuit) and Louisiana becoming the 22nd state to pass a consumer data privacy law. Multi-state companies now face an increasingly complex compliance landscape.

title: UK CMA forces Google to let publishers opt out of AI search
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed new conduct requirements on Google Search, giving publishers the right to opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews and for fine-tuning AI models. Google must also provide clear attribution and links within AI-generated results. The intervention is designed to restore bargaining power for news companies that have seen traffic and leverage erode as AI summaries replace direct clicks.

title: Claude Fable 5 arrives — and it's already rationed
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 today, calling it state-of-the-art on nearly all capability benchmarks, with standout performance in software engineering, vision, and scientific research. Pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens — less than half the cost of Mythos Preview — but subscription access is being staged due to anticipated demand pressure.

summary: GitHub's latest JetBrains update puts Claude into public preview as an agent provider inside Copilot Chat, letting developers pick between agents without leaving their IDE. Cloud agent — previously behind a preview flag — is now generally available.

title: Google's agentic Gemini era, by the numbers

summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag today in beta for Enterprise and Team customers — a version of Claude that lives inside Slack channels, builds memory over time, takes async tasks, and proactively surfaces things teams need to know. summary: Google pushed its June Pixel Drop today, bringing Gemini Omni video creation and AI music generation to Pixel phones — you can now describe an idea or upload a photo and get a full audio track with lyrics. summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, an open-weight multimodal model that fits in 16GB of VRAM and processes vision and audio directly through the LLM backbone — no separate encoders. summary: Groq closed a $650 million round led by existing board investors Disruptive and Infinitum, money earmarked for expanding data center capacity as the company shifts from custom AI chip maker to full-stack inference cloud provider. summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3 billion in new funds — the largest raise in its 50-year history — after its preemptive $500M+ Series D bet on Anthropic in 2024 ballooned to a roughly $14 billion position. The firm also quietly grew its Anthology startup fund with Anthropic from $100M committed to nearly $250M deployed. It's a rare public vindication for a bet that, at the time, was described internally as white-knuckling it.

title: Sarvam hits $1.5B unicorn valuation with $234M round
summary: India's Sarvam raised $234 million led by HCLTech — which alone put in $150M — with Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV also participating, targeting a full $300M Series B. The company launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters earlier this year and is now valued at $1.5 billion, making it India's newest AI unicorn. The raise comes just over two years after Sarvam had collected only $41M across its seed and Series A.

title: a16z backs Ornn, a marketplace for AI compute
summary: Andreessen Horowitz led a $33M seed round into Ornn, a startup building a marketplace where AI compute power can be bought and sold like a commodity. a16z crypto, Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel also participated — and general partner Ali Yahya confirmed it's the firm's first compute-marketplace investment. The bet reflects growing conviction that GPU access will be traded infrastructure, not just leased from hyperscalers.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B valuation for AI in manufacturing
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M in a Series C led by Singapore's Temasek, valuing the company at roughly $2.4 billion — up from nearly $1B at its last round. The startup builds AI models for manufacturing complex components like jet engines and semiconductors, with Nvidia and Applied Materials among its backers. It competes in a field that now includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor the agentic AI layer
summary: Boston-based Coralogix closed a $200M Series F led by Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, valuing it at $1.6B post-money just 11 months after its last $115M raise. The company is positioning itself as the monitoring and observability layer for AI agents — the infrastructure that watches the infrastructure. Total funding now stands at $550M.

title: State AI laws are multiplying faster than anyone can track
summary: This week alone: Rhode Island's governor signed three AI laws covering therapy chatbot bans, self-harm safeguards, and clinical session disclosure; California lawmakers passed a ban on AI public school teachers headed to Governor Newsom; and Arizona's governor vetoed all three AI bills her legislature sent her. The activity underscores a widening patchwork as Congress stalls on the 'Great American AI Act' federal framework that would preempt state rules for three years.

title: Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over consumer harm
summary: Florida's Attorney General filed the first state-led civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly concealed serious risks of ChatGPT — including responses that promote self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and data collection from minors — and actively marketed the product to Florida residents. The suit relies on consumer protection and deceptive trade practices law rather than AI-specific legislation. It adds to a mounting legal pile alongside the New York Times' updated copyright suit against OpenAI and Microsoft.

title: Court rules expert AI prompts are discoverable in litigation
summary: A federal magistrate judge in Connecticut ordered plaintiffs to produce the AI prompts their expert used to prepare her report in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil, treating the prompts as methodology rather than protected drafting material. The ruling is one of the clearest signals yet that using AI in expert work opens up the inputs to discovery — a development that will reshape how litigators and their experts use AI tools. Expect this to be cited widely in other cases.

title: UK's CMA gives publishers opt-out rights on Google AI Search
summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority imposed new conduct requirements on Google Search that let publishers opt out of having their content used in AI Overviews and other AI Search features, and also block fine-tuning use of their material. Google must also provide clear attribution with links in AI-generated results. The intervention is the most concrete publisher-protection measure imposed on a major search engine's AI features so far.

title: Gemini lands inside Apple's Xcode
summary: Google and Apple quietly made a big deal: starting with iOS 27, developers can call Gemini models directly through Apple's Foundation Models framework. Gemini is also now integrated into Xcode itself, letting developers review code, fix bugs, and ship features without switching windows. Firebase AI Logic handles the backend so no separate server infrastructure is needed.

title: NotebookLM becomes a full research engine
summary: Google upgraded NotebookLM with Gemini 3.5 and a secure cloud computer that can run code, generate charts, build PDFs, and even export PowerPoints. You can now start a project with just a loose idea and the tool will find and organise sources from the web for you. The upgrade is live globally for Google AI Ultra subscribers and Workspace business accounts.

title: ChatGPT gets personal finance and a new default model
summary: OpenAI rolled out personal finance features to Plus users, letting them securely connect bank accounts and ask ChatGPT questions grounded in their real financial data. Simultaneously, GPT-5.5 Instant replaced GPT-5.3 Instant as ChatGPT's default model for all users, with improvements across accuracy, image understanding, and STEM. A free ChatGPT for Clinicians tier also launched for verified US healthcare workers.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal open model that fits in 16GB of RAM and handles audio, video, and text inputs without separate encoders. It's the first mid-sized Gemma model with native audio support and benchmarks close to the much larger 26B MoE model. It ships under Apache 2.0, so anyone can build with it commercially.

title: Google's Googlebook and Universal Cart take shape
summary: Google's May recap confirmed the Googlebook — a Gemini-native laptop built with Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo — alongside Universal Cart, a cross-merchant shopping hub that works inside Search, YouTube, Gmail, and Gemini at once. Fitbit Air, described as a tiny pebble tracker with Afib monitoring, also officially launched. Together they represent Google's biggest hardware and commerce push in years.

title: Sarvam is India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Bengaluru-based Sarvam closed $234M at a $1.5B valuation, with HCLTech putting in $150M as lead strategic investor and Bessemer, Khosla, and Peak XV also participating. The company builds open-source models — including 30B and 105B parameter releases — aimed at giving governments and enterprises sovereign control over AI infrastructure. Sarvam is targeting a full $300M Series B.

title: PhysicsX hits $2.4B making AI for jet engines
summary: London-based PhysicsX raised $300M at a $2.4B valuation to build AI models that simulate and optimise physical components like jet engines and semiconductors. Singapore's Temasek led the Series C, with Nvidia and Applied Materials returning as backers. The valuation is roughly three times its last round, reflecting surging demand for AI in deep manufacturing.

title: a16z bets on Ornn, an AI compute marketplace
summary: Andreessen Horowitz led a $33M seed round into Ornn, a startup building a marketplace where AI compute can be bought and sold like a commodity. a16z crypto participated alongside Galaxy Ventures, Nordstar, and SV Angel — marking a16z's first investment specifically in a compute marketplace. The bet reflects growing conviction that compute access, not just models, will be a durable business.

title: Coralogix raises $200M to monitor AI agents
summary: AI monitoring startup Coralogix closed a $200M Series F just 11 months after its Series E, valuing the company at $1.6B. The thesis: as autonomous AI agents proliferate, someone needs to watch them in production. Advent and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board led the round, with Coralogix now having raised $550M total.

title: Swiss startup Prem raises $100M for private AI
summary: Zurich-based Prem AI is closing a $100M Series A targeting a $500M+ valuation, selling private AI infrastructure to hedge funds and law firms that cannot send data to the cloud. The round is expected to close in Q3 2026. It reflects a clear market segment: regulated industries willing to pay a premium for on-premise model deployment.

title: Colorado rewrites its landmark AI law
summary: Colorado's governor signed a substantially revised version of its first-in-the-nation AI legislation in May 2026, after the original law was frozen by a court challenge brought by an AI developer with DOJ support. The new law shifts focus from algorithmic discrimination to adverse outcomes in consequential automated decisions, covering six domains including employment, healthcare, and housing. Organisations doing business in Colorado must be compliant by January 1, 2027.

title: Google's Interactions API goes GA
summary: Google has officially moved its Interactions API to general availability, making it the primary interface for all Gemini models and agents. The release adds Managed Agents, background execution, built-in tool mixing, and a 50% cost reduction via Flex tier. It's now the default in Google AI Studio and all official documentation.

title: Gemma 4 12B runs on your laptop
summary: Google released Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal open-weight model that fits in 16GB of RAM and introduces native audio inputs without any separate encoder. It benchmarks close to the larger 26B MoE model and ships under Apache 2.0, with support across Ollama, LM Studio, Hugging Face, and vLLM. Google also released an official Skills Repository to help agents build with the model.

title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.3-Codex
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5.3-Codex, its first model to merge the Codex and GPT-5 training stacks into a single general-purpose coding agent. It's roughly 25% faster than its predecessor and is available today across the CLI, IDE extension, cloud, and code review surfaces. A smaller GPT-5-Codex-Mini variant also launched, offering up to 4x more usage within existing ChatGPT subscriptions.

title: GPT-5.5 Instant is now ChatGPT's default
summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-5.5 Instant as the new default model for all ChatGPT users, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant with improvements in accuracy, image understanding, and conversational quality. The update also retired the canvas tool from Instant and Thinking tiers, replacing it with native writing and code blocks directly in chat. Paid users get a three-month grace period to continue using GPT-5.3 Instant.

title: Google's May recap: Gemini Omni, Universal Cart, Googlebook
summary: Google's consolidated May 2026 update spans Gemini Omni — a model that generates video from any combination of inputs — and Universal Cart, a cross-merchant shopping hub woven into Search, YouTube, and Gmail. New hardware includes the Googlebook laptop built around Gemini Intelligence, and Fitbit Air, a pebble-sized wellness tracker with Afib monitoring and SpO2. Google also committed $10M via the REPLIQA program to apply quantum AI to life sciences.

title: Zero revenue, $5.1B valuation — meet Ineffable Intelligence
summary: Ineffable Intelligence raised $1.1 billion in seed funding at a $5.1 billion valuation despite having no product and no revenue, in what is being called the largest seed round in European history. Within a single month, its valuation jumped over 70x — from a $55M pre-money figure with Sequoia to $4B pre-money with Lightspeed, Index Ventures, and DST Global. Part of the funding came from UK taxpayers via a new £670M sovereign AI fund.

title: Mega-rounds now dominate: 94% of AI funding
summary: Deals over $100 million now account for 94% of all AI funding, and the median Series D valuation in the US hit $2.5 billion in Q1 2026 — surpassing the 2021 peak. Early-stage funding was up 41% year-over-year, with seed investments rising 31%. The concentration of capital is reshaping what a funding check even means for the average AI startup.

title: Sarvam becomes India's newest AI unicorn
summary: Sarvam raised $234 million in a Series B round led by HCLTech, vaulting the Indian AI startup to a $1.5 billion valuation. The round also includes Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and Peak XV Partners, with Sarvam aiming to close a total of $300 million. The company earlier launched open-source models at 30B and 105B parameters designed for Indian languages.

title: General Intuition in talks for $300M at $2B valuation
summary: General Intuition, which builds foundation models for teaching AI agents to navigate space and time, is in advanced talks to raise $300 million at a roughly $2 billion valuation. The NY-based startup spun out of gaming clip platform Medal just eight months ago with a $134M seed round. Backers in the new round include Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt, Khosla Ventures, and General Catalyst.

title: France's Genesis AI matches Mistral's record seed
summary: Genesis AI, a French robotics startup founded in early 2025, has raised $105 million in seed funding — matching the record set by Mistral AI, Europe's most prominent AI company. The startup is betting on non-humanoid robot designs to differentiate itself in the increasingly crowded AI robotics market. Its valuation has not been disclosed.

title: Florida sues OpenAI over child safety
summary: Florida filed a landmark civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company knowingly concealed ChatGPT's risks and marketed addictive, unsafe technology to children. The complaint cites deceptive trade practices, responses that allegedly encouraged self-harm, dependency-inducing design, and data collection from minors. OpenAI has rejected the claims, and the case is being closely watched as a template for other state attorneys general.

title: AI prompts are now discoverable in court
summary: A federal magistrate judge ruled in Conservation Law Foundation v. Shell Oil that the AI prompts an expert used to prepare their report must be produced in discovery, treating them as methodology rather than protected drafting material. The decision is one of the clearest signals yet that courts will scrutinize how AI was used to build expert testimony. Legal teams using AI for case work will need to document their prompt strategies accordingly.

title: State AI laws multiply as federal preemption stalls
summary: All 50 US states have now introduced AI-related legislation, with over 2,182 bills filed as of May 2026, creating a patchwork of conflicting obligations for multi-state operators. A proposed 10-year moratorium on state AI enforcement was struck down 99-1 in the Senate, and comprehensive federal preemption language was also rejected in the NDAA. Colorado's landmark AI law was gutted after an xAI lawsuit and DOJ intervention, underscoring how quickly state-level frameworks can collapse.

title: Cursor 2.0: eight agents, one prompt
summary: Cursor's 2.0 release lets developers run up to eight parallel agents on a single prompt, each working in an isolated git worktree to avoid conflicts. The update also introduces Composer — Cursor's own frontier coding model described as 4x faster than comparable models — alongside voice control, sandboxed terminals GA, and a full audit log for enterprise teams. It's the most ambitious IDE release since Copilot launched.

title: Google open-sources Medical Data Toolkit, powers India's Aarogya Setu 2.0
summary: India's National Health Authority launched Aarogya Setu 2.0 today, built on Google's Gemma 4 open models and a newly open-sourced Medical Data Toolkit. The toolkit extracts structured FHIR data from messy lab reports and imaging records, making health history portable across hospitals. Google is releasing the toolkit to developers and health organizations at no cost.

title: GLM-5 arrives at 744B parameters with cheaper deployment
summary: Zhipu AI released GLM-5, scaling from the 355B-parameter GLM-4.5 to a 744B-parameter MoE architecture with only 40B active parameters per forward pass. The model integrates DeepSeek Sparse Attention to cut deployment costs while maintaining long-context performance, and is deployable today via vLLM and SGLang. It targets complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks.

title: GPT-5.5 Instant is now ChatGPT's default model
summary: OpenAI has begun rolling out GPT-5.5 Instant as the new default model for all ChatGPT users, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant with improvements to accuracy, image understanding, and STEM reasoning. Alongside it, ChatGPT for Excel and Google Sheets is now available globally, embedding an AI sidebar directly into spreadsheets. Paid users can stick with GPT-5.3 Instant for three more months via model settings.

title: Ornith-1.0 brings self-improving agentic coding to open source
summary: A new MIT-licensed model family called Ornith-1.0 launched today in four sizes — 9B, 31B, 35B MoE, and 397B MoE — post-trained on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 for agentic coding. Its key innovation is joint RL optimization of both the solution and the scaffold driving it, letting the model discover better search trajectories over time. It claims state-of-the-art results on SWE-Bench and Terminal-Bench 2.1 among open-source models of comparable size.

title: China mints two robotics unicorns in one day
summary: AI² Robotics raised nearly 5 billion yuan ($736M) and Alibaba-backed X Square Robot closed consecutive rounds, pushing both companies past 20 billion yuan ($2.9B+) valuations. The back-to-back announcements signal sustained investor appetite for humanoid and industrial robotics despite a crowded field. Both firms are positioning as direct challengers to Tesla and Figure AI.

title: Arena, the AI benchmark everyone uses, hits $100M ARR
summary: Chatbot Arena — the crowdsourced model leaderboard backed by a16z, Kleiner Perkins, and Lightspeed — has grown its annualized revenue from $30M in January to $100M, just five months after its $150M Series A at a $1.7B valuation. The company has now raised $250M in total and is expanding its evaluation platform into enterprise model selection. It's a quiet reminder that AI infrastructure, not models, can be the stickiest business.

title: Omen AI raises $31M to cool data centers with liquid
summary: Omen AI, which uses AI to optimize liquid cooling systems for data centers, closed a $31M Series A led by Nava Ventures with participation from CRV and Vanderbilt University. The startup is already working with a dozen data center customers including AMD-focused compute cloud TensorWave, and has raised $40M in total since founding in 2024. With AI power demand spiraling, cooling optimization is becoming a genuine infrastructure category.

title: Pocket raises $11M for AI note-taking hardware
summary: Y Combinator-backed Pocket has raised $11M from Accel, YC, and ElevenLabs CEO Mati Staniszewski to scale its AI note-taking device, which has already sold over 130,000 units since launching last year. The raise comes as the wearable AI space heats up with multiple competing devices, and Pocket is betting on design and pricing to break through. The ElevenLabs founder's personal investment signals a voice-first roadmap.

title: European deeptech shatters annual funding record in six months
summary: European deeptech startups have already exceeded the all-time annual fundraising record with six months still to go in 2026, according to Sifted data. The surge reflects a broader global shift toward hard-tech and AI infrastructure investment as software multiples compress. Analysts expect the second half to slow, but H1 2026 has already rewritten the playbook for European venture.

title: Pentagon designates Anthropic a supply chain risk — Anthropic fights back
summary: The Department of Defense has made the unprecedented move of listing Anthropic as a supply chain risk, a designation that threatens the $380B company's government and enterprise contracts ahead of its planned IPO. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei immediately vowed to challenge the designation in court, calling it unjustified. The move follows the temporary ban on Anthropic's Mythos 5 model, which reportedly identified real vulnerabilities in classified U.S. government systems during a security test.

title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol restricted to 20 government-vetted partners
summary: The White House's ONCD and OSTP directed OpenAI to limit the initial commercial rollout of its new GPT-5.6 model family — including flagship agentic model Sol — to roughly 20 government-screened commercial partners rather than a public release. The directive invokes the voluntary pre-release framework under Trump's June 2 executive order on AI security. OpenAI has said the review process shouldn't become a permanent default, but for now Sol is effectively off-limits to most businesses.

title: Trump partially reverses Mythos ban after industry pressure
summary: The Trump administration has walked back part of its ban on Anthropic's Mythos 5 model, allowing trusted partners to access it following two weeks of restrictions that rattled enterprise customers and spooked investors. The episode triggered what sources told the WSJ was a $7.4B DeepSeek fundraising round, after China's DeepSeek reportedly accelerated investment plans in response to Mythos' demonstrated cybersecurity capabilities. The reversal underscores the administration's struggle to balance security reviews with economic stakes.

title: Gemini knows your face now
summary: Google's Gemini app launched deeply personalized image generation for all eligible U.S. users today, pulling your actual photos from Google Photos to place you in AI-created scenes. Instead of painstakingly describing yourself in prompts, you can just say 'create an illustration of me and my favorite things' and Gemini figures out the rest. The feature is opt-in and connects to Gmail, YouTube, and Search for broader context.

title: Zhipu's GLM 5.2 closes the gap for free
summary: Chinese AI lab Zhipu released GLM 5.2, an open-source model that is reportedly closing in on top U.S. frontier models on key agentic benchmarks — and it costs nothing to use. Analysts note the AI competition is shifting toward intelligence-per-dollar rather than raw capability, making open-source a serious contender. DeepSeek set the template; Zhipu is running the same playbook even faster.

title: World models are the new LLMs — $3B in six months
summary: Venture capitalists poured over $3 billion into world-model AI startups in the first half of 2026 alone, betting that the future of AI is systems that understand physical environments, not just text. Yann LeCun left Meta and immediately closed a $1.03B seed round at a $3.5B valuation — the largest seed in European history. World Labs, Decart, and Odyssey also each raised hundreds of millions in the same period.

title: Data labeling is the oil crisis nobody planned for
summary: Physical AI — robotics, autonomous vehicles, humanoids — is hitting a wall: there isn't enough high-quality labeled data, and fixing that requires enormous amounts of cash. Meta's $14.3B acquisition of a 49% stake in Scale AI in June underscored just how strategic data infrastructure has become. Investors are pouring into foundational model builders while the labeling bottleneck quietly threatens to slow everything down.

title: Ionic Digital heads to Nasdaq via direct listing
summary: Bitcoin miner and AI infrastructure firm Ionic Digital filed for a Nasdaq direct listing after raising $400M last week at a $2B pre-money valuation from Attestor, Oaktree, and Sachem Head. The company is positioning itself at the crossroads of crypto mining infrastructure and AI compute demand. J.P. Morgan, Jefferies, and BTIG are advising the listing.

title: Musk's turbines spark a Clean Air Act showdown
summary: The DOJ moved to join a lawsuit against xAI over 27 unpermitted gas turbines powering its Memphis-area data center, arguing national security justifies letting them run without standard pollution controls. The NAACP had originally sued, and the DOJ's intervention is being read as a bid to shut down citizen enforcement of the Clean Air Act entirely when the government disagrees. Legal experts warn it could set a precedent allowing any administration to block public pollution lawsuits for politically favored industries.

title: Should the government own a piece of OpenAI?
summary: Trump announced in June his administration is exploring equity stakes of 5–10% in major AI companies, and both Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon have floated government ownership of up to 50%. Critics argue this would hand future administrations a powerful lever over speech and information, with one analysis calling it 'industrial policy strapped to a First Amendment tripwire.' A bipartisan JAWBONE Act is now being pushed to prevent government officials from coercing AI companies on content moderation.

title: U.S. AI regulation: a senior Alphabet board member calls it broken
summary: Martin Chavez, vice chairman at Sixth Street and an Alphabet board member, told Reuters at a London AI event that U.S. AI regulation is 'problematic and inconsistent,' criticizing model-by-model reviews with no transparent process. He compared it to pre-crisis financial regulation and called for something like annual stress tests. His remarks land as the Trump administration restricts GPT-5.6 and plays gatekeeper with Anthropic's models for national security reasons.

title: Bipartisan majority wants formal AI model reviews
summary: A new poll from the AI Policy Institute found 68% of Americans support a formal government review process for advanced AI models before public release — including 64% of Republicans, 76% of Democrats, and 63% of independents. Separately, 70% of Americans in a Gallup survey oppose data centers in their communities, with Monterey Park, California becoming the first city to permanently ban them via ballot initiative. States are increasingly moving ahead on AI rules despite Trump's warning in January to stay out of it.

title: Fable 5 goes global after ban lifted
summary: Anthropic's Fable 5 model is available worldwide starting today after the US Commerce Department rescinded the emergency export controls it imposed on June 12. The nearly three-week suspension—triggered by a classified cybersecurity assessment flagging Mythos 5's ability to identify vulnerabilities in secure government systems—caused significant disruption for enterprise clients. Fable 5 is now live on Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and the API, with AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry access being restored as quickly as possible.

title: Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Science ship
summary: Alongside the Fable 5 redeployment, Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5, billing it as a frontier-performance model optimised for coding, agents, and professional work at scale. The company also launched Claude Science, a customisable AI workbench for researchers that integrates common scientific tools and packages, produces auditable artefacts, and provides flexible compute access.

title: GitHub Copilot gets Sonnet 5 and MAI-Code-1-Flash
summary: GitHub's June changelog is packed: Claude Sonnet 5 is now generally available inside Copilot, bringing stronger agentic coding performance to everyday development workflows. Microsoft's own in-house coding model MAI-Code-1-Flash is also now generally available for Copilot Business and Enterprise, giving teams a purpose-built, cost-optimised alternative for high-volume code tasks.

title: Bending Spoons prices $1.68B IPO above range
summary: Italian tech company Bending Spoons priced its US IPO above the stated range to raise $1.68 billion, with trading starting Wednesday. The Vimeo owner is one of the splashier listings in a reviving IPO market that also saw Uber-backed Lime raise $167 million in its own debut this week.

title: Oxmiq raises $35M to cut AI chip costs
summary: Campbell, California-based Oxmiq has raised $35 million—bringing its total to $60 million—to build chip design architecture and software aimed at reducing the cost of building and running AI applications. The round was led by Samsung Catalyst Fund and Fudomo, with MediaTek and Pegatron Venture Capital also participating.

title: Getty-backed BRIA snags $24M Series A
summary: BRIA, a "responsible" AI image generation startup backed by Getty Images, closed a $24 million Series A that includes investment from top ad agency Publicis Groupe. The round signals continued appetite for brand-safe generative image tools as advertising giants look to control their AI supply chain.

title: The Anthropic export-control saga explained
summary: The three-week government ban on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 marks the first time the US has applied export controls to a software AI model rather than hardware, invoking the Export Control Reform Act in a legally novel way. An Anthropic customer with Canadian employees has already filed suit seeking to vacate the directive, arguing it exceeds the government's statutory authority—a case that could define the limits of federal power over AI software for years.

title: Trump AI order: interventionist shift, contractor bonanza
summary: The Economist notes a dramatic pivot in US AI policy from a libertarian stance to active government intervention—restricting access to frontier models while the June 2 executive order simultaneously opens large procurement opportunities for government contractors building AI cybersecurity tools. The order avoids mandatory licensing but creates a voluntary classified benchmarking regime for "covered frontier models," with NSA at its centre.

title: Together AI surges to $8.3B on $800M raise
summary: Together AI closed an $800 million funding round led by Aramco Ventures, pushing its valuation to $8.3 billion — more than double the $3.3 billion it was worth just 17 months ago. The company focuses on AI infrastructure and model training APIs, competing in the crowded cloud compute market. Aramco's lead position signals Gulf sovereign capital deepening its AI bets.

title: German drone maker Quantum Systems raises $1.2B
summary: Munich-based Quantum Systems secured $1.2 billion in fresh funding, valuing the defence drone company at roughly $8 billion — about eight times its valuation from a year ago. The round marks one of the largest private investment rounds ever in European defence tech. Rival AI defence startup Helsing is also expected to close a $1.2 billion round soon at an $18 billion valuation.

title: AI swallows 89% of US venture deal value
summary: A new PitchBook and NVCA report found AI companies accounted for 88.8% of total US venture deal value in Q1 2026, up from just 14.6% a decade ago. The concentration is squeezing out non-AI growth-stage startups, which face longer fundraising timelines, fewer bidders, and lower valuations than two years ago. The dynamic is creating a two-tier venture market with AI haves and everyone else.

title: Sora is gone — what you need to know
summary: OpenAI's Sora web and app experiences were discontinued on April 26, 2026, with the API set to follow on September 24, 2026. Users relying on the video generation product should migrate before the API cutoff. No direct replacement has been announced under the Sora brand.

title: GitHub hit inbox zero on secret scanning alerts
summary: GitHub's security team published a detailed walkthrough of how they used their own secret scanning tooling to eliminate a backlog of exposed credentials and reach alert inbox zero. The post covers triage strategies, automation hooks, and lessons learned scaling the program internally. It's a rare look at GitHub dogfooding its own security product at scale.

title: ChatGPT workspace agents now generally available
summary: OpenAI has rolled out workspace agents to ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu tiers, letting teams build reusable automated workflows that run on schedule or inside Slack. The release also includes a new Skills feature that turns verified workflows into reusable instructions ChatGPT applies automatically. Updated integrations for Box, Notion, Linear, and Dropbox also shipped alongside.

title: Crusoe eyes $3B raise at $30B valuation
summary: AI data center startup Crusoe is in active talks to raise roughly $3 billion in a new funding round that could triple its valuation to around $30 billion. The company last raised $1.38 billion in a Series E at a $10 billion valuation co-led by Valor Equity Partners and Mubadala Capital. A final valuation has not been set, but the round signals continued investor appetite for AI infrastructure plays.

title: ElevenLabs explores $22B secondary sale
summary: AI voice generation firm ElevenLabs is exploring a secondary share sale that would let employees cash out stock at a valuation of around $22 billion, expected to close by September. That would be double the $11 billion valuation the company achieved in its $500 million Series D just five months ago in February. No IPO timeline has been announced.

title: Alsa raises $6.5M to give AI agents their own payment rails
summary: San Francisco startup Alsa has raised $6.5 million in a seed round led by Alibaba and Tribe Capital to build payment infrastructure specifically designed for AI agents conducting transactions autonomously and at scale. The round also includes backing from Draper and Saison Capital. As agentic AI moves into enterprise workflows, purpose-built financial plumbing for non-human actors is emerging as a new category.

title: Anthropic's Fable model is back — the battle is just beginning
summary: After 2.5 weeks offline due to a U.S. government security directive, Anthropic's Fable AI model has been restored following a deal with the Trump administration. The episode has reignited debate about how the government should regulate frontier model access versus enabling innovation. The WSJ notes the standoff exposed deep divisions inside Washington over the future of AI oversight.

title: India says existing laws aren't enough — standalone AI bill coming
summary: India's IT Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed the government will soon begin stakeholder consultations on a dedicated AI regulatory framework, signaling that existing IT laws are no longer considered sufficient. A draft regulation is expected to be prepared at the ministry level in the near term. The announcement coincides with India also investigating a data breach at Tata Electronics that reportedly exposed Apple iPhone 18 Pro secrets.

title: UN convenes first global AI governance dialogue next week
summary: The first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance opens in Geneva on July 6, bringing together heads of state, AI executives including Microsoft's Brad Smith and Google's Yossi Matias, and representatives from 193 countries. The dialogue builds on UNESCO's AI Ethics Observatory and G20 principles, with a focus on ensuring the Global South shapes — not just consumes — AI development. UN Secretary-General Guterres has separately called on AI companies to disclose their carbon and water usage.

title: LongCat-2.0 is a 1.6T-param beast built on AI ASICs
summary: Meituan has released LongCat-2.0, a massive 1.6-trillion-parameter MoE model with ~48B parameters activated per token, trained on over 35 trillion tokens with no rollbacks. It supports 1M-context windows via a novel LongCat Sparse Attention mechanism and is tightly integrated with tools like Claude Code and Hermes. Crucially, the entire training and deployment stack runs on AI ASIC superpods — no Nvidia GPUs required.

title: GPT-5.3 Instant quietly rolls out to Enterprise
summary: OpenAI has updated its Enterprise and Edu release notes with GPT-5.3 Instant, promising more accurate answers, richer web-search results, and fewer unnecessary hedges or dead-ends. The model is off by default — admins must flip the Early Model Access toggle in workspace settings to enable it. A wave of new MCP connectors including Amplitude, Vercel, Stripe, and Semrush also went live for paid tiers.

title: Nvidia offers startups compute-for-revenue-share deals
summary: Nvidia is launching a program that lets AI-focused startups swap access to compute power for a slice of their future profits, lowering the upfront GPU cost barrier for early-stage companies. The move positions Nvidia deeper in the startup ecosystem as a de-facto financial backer, not just a hardware vendor. It comes as compute scarcity remains a top bottleneck for emerging AI labs.

title: Microsoft launches $2.5B AI implementation unit
summary: Microsoft is spinning up a dedicated company — backed by $2.5 billion and 6,000 employees — to help enterprise customers choose and deploy AI technologies that actually deliver returns. The unit reflects a broader industry pivot from selling AI capabilities to proving AI value, as customers grow impatient with pilots that don't scale. It is Microsoft's most concrete answer yet to the ROI skeptics.

title: Kling AI bags $2.8B from Alibaba and Tencent
summary: Kuaishou Technology has closed a blockbuster 19-billion-yuan ($2.8B) funding round for its Kling AI video-generation arm, with Alibaba and Tencent among the backers. The deal values Kling AI at $15 billion pre-money, cementing it as one of China's most valuable AI subsidiaries. The raise signals that Chinese tech giants are doubling down on generative video as the next major AI battleground.

title: Unitree Robotics clears Shanghai IPO for $619M raise
summary: Chinese humanoid robot maker Unitree Robotics has received regulatory approval to list on the Shanghai exchange, aiming to raise 4.2 billion yuan (~$619M). The IPO is one of China's most watched tech offerings this year as humanoid robotics attracts intense investor interest alongside AI. Unitree's warehouse and general-purpose robots have already gained global attention after viral demos.

title: OpenAI floats 5% government stake to ease DC heat
summary: OpenAI has reportedly discussed offering the Trump administration a 5% equity stake, according to the Financial Times, as the company faces growing scrutiny over model misuse and whether Americans will share in AI profits. Anthropic has separately confirmed it has had no such discussions with the White House. The proposal reflects how profoundly the political winds have shifted for frontier AI labs in Washington.

title: Zuckerberg: AI agents moving slower than expected
summary: In a leaked internal town hall, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees that AI agent development over the past four months has not accelerated as the company hoped. The candid admission is notable given Meta's heavy public investment in agentic AI and its open-source model strategy. It echoes broader industry anxiety that the jump from capable chat models to truly autonomous agents is harder than anticipated.

title: India signals it's finally ready to regulate AI
summary: MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan said publicly that India may now need dedicated AI legislation, the clearest break yet from the government's longstanding position that existing IT laws are sufficient. He indicated the ministry could begin drafting regulation, though a timeline for actual legislation remains unconfirmed. India is simultaneously negotiating with the US and Anthropic for access to frontier AI models as a trusted-nation partner.

title: Trump lifts Claude ban after cybersecurity alarm
summary: The Trump administration has ended its weeks-long restriction on Anthropic's latest Claude models, which had been blocked following cybersecurity concerns. Separately, an official confirmed that one of Anthropic's Mythos models actually identified vulnerabilities in classified US government systems during testing — a finding that apparently helped resolve the standoff. Alibaba, meanwhile, is banning Claude Code internally from July 10 over alleged backdoor risks.

title: AI hallucinations are infecting real courtrooms
summary: India's Supreme Court has formally cautioned against AI-generated legal material after lower tribunals relied on fabricated, hallucinated case citations — and directed the Bar Council of India to set up a committee on the problem. The Economist's parallel report on 'vibe lawyering' shows the same pattern across Britain, America, and Canada, with self-represented litigants using chatbots to file frivolous suits citing cases that don't exist. India's Supreme Court is now circulating draft regulations mandating disclosure and verification of any AI-generated content submitted to courts.

title: America's frontier AI is getting more restricted, not less
summary: The Economist reports that the Trump administration has begun restricting access to advanced OpenAI and Anthropic models, representing a sharp pivot from libertarian hands-off policy to active interventionism. OpenAI is separately holding back GPT-5.6 Sol at the administration's explicit request. The Economist argues this nationalistic approach is both opaque and unsustainable, and that America risks imprisoning its own frontier AI advantage.

title: Alibaba bans Claude Code over spy fears
summary: Alibaba will prohibit employees from using Anthropic's Claude Code in workplace environments starting July 10, citing alleged security risks from embedded backdoors that tracked Chinese users. The Chinese tech giant has classified the tool as 'high-risk' software following an internal investigation. The move signals deepening distrust between Chinese firms and Western AI tooling.

title: Microsoft launches AI adoption firm with $2.5B
summary: Microsoft announced a new standalone company designed to help enterprise customers navigate AI technology selection and generate measurable returns on their AI investments. The venture is backed by $2.5 billion and reflects Microsoft's push to monetize its AI portfolio beyond raw model licensing. It positions the company as an AI systems integrator for large businesses.

title: Zuckerberg: AI agents behind schedule
summary: In a candid internal town hall, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees that AI agent development over the past four months has not accelerated as the company expected. Reuters obtained a recording of his remarks, which underscore the gap between AI hype and operational reality even at the frontier. The admission is notable given Meta's aggressive public commitments to agentic AI.

title: AI startups run leaner — and the data proves it
summary: A study of nearly 50,000 Y Combinator and PitchBook-listed startups found AI-native companies operate with smaller teams and flatter hierarchies while maintaining valuations on par with non-AI peers. AI-tagged startups raise roughly 20% more capital per employee, suggesting structural efficiency gains rather than mere hype. YC AI first-deal counts in 2024 are nearly eight times the 2020 average.

title: Kling AI scores $2.8B from Alibaba and Tencent
summary: Kuaishou's Kling AI video generation arm closed a blockbuster 19 billion yuan raise with Alibaba and Tencent as lead backers, valuing the unit at $15 billion pre-money. The deal cements Kling AI as China's dominant AI video platform and shows Chinese tech giants doubling down on generative media. It is one of the largest single AI fundraises of 2026.

title: Skello pulls €200M for AI-powered HR expansion
summary: French workforce management startup Skello secured a €200 million round led by Bridgepoint Development Capital, with plans to consolidate its French market lead and expand across Europe. The company will use proceeds to hire aggressively in AI in the second half of 2026. The deal highlights sustained investor appetite for vertical AI SaaS outside the US.

title: ElevenLabs eyes $22B valuation in employee stock sale
summary: AI voice generation company ElevenLabs is exploring a secondary share sale that would let employees cash out, with the transaction expected to imply a $22 billion valuation. Bloomberg first reported the move, which signals ElevenLabs has no immediate IPO plans but wants to provide liquidity. The valuation would make it one of the most richly priced audio-AI firms globally.

title: Critics pile up as AI lab bubble math wobbles
summary: A growing cohort of credible venture and academic voices is questioning the financial logic underpinning AI lab valuations, with OpenAI's $852 billion figure drawing the sharpest scrutiny. Forbes reports that the gap between revenue projections and current monetization is widening just as new capital continues to pour in. The skeptics warn that the mismatch could trigger a painful repricing.

title: OpenAI floats 5% US government stake
summary: OpenAI has discussed giving the US government a 5% equity stake — worth roughly $42.6 billion at its current valuation — in exchange for regulatory latitude, the Financial Times reported. Sam Altman has framed the idea as a public wealth fund modelled on Alaska's Permanent Fund, potentially extending to Anthropic, Meta, and Google. Senator Bernie Sanders countered with legislation demanding 50% stakes and full voting rights for the federal government.

title: Trump's AI regime: interventionist and opaque
summary: The Economist reports that the Trump administration has shifted from a hands-off stance to actively restricting access to advanced AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic, framing them as strategic national assets. The policy is described as inconsistent and nationalistic, alarming allies who fear being cut off from frontier AI. The approach echoes export control regimes historically reserved for weapons technology.

title: Voters turn on AI as backlash builds
summary: Three-quarters of Americans now say they want more regulation of AI, with both parties struggling to develop coherent policy responses to public anxiety, according to new polling covered by The Economist. Opposition is crystallising around data centres, job displacement, and distrust of lab governance. The Economist warns the political backlash is 'only getting started' and could threaten billions in planned investment.

title: Argentina legalises AI-run 'non-human corporations'
summary: Argentine President Javier Milei introduced legislation creating legal entities owned and operated entirely by AI agents via blockchain smart contracts, with human shareholders permitted but not required. Reuters notes the companies would still require some human involvement despite the dramatic framing. The move positions Argentina as a radical outlier in global AI governance as most nations tighten controls.

title: Texas governor targets rural data centre sprawl
summary: Governor Greg Abbott called for banning new data centre development in rural Texas communities during a campaign stop, citing pressure on local power grids and community opposition. Texas already confronts at least 248 planned data centre developments, with public hearings intensifying across the state. The move reflects a broader national trend of local and state-level resistance to AI infrastructure.

title: Microsoft's $2.5B AI implementation firm
summary: Microsoft announced a new standalone company, backed by $2.5 billion and 6,000 employees, designed to help customers choose and deploy AI technologies that deliver measurable returns. It's a direct bet that enterprises need hand-holding — not just models — to make AI work. The move signals Microsoft is shifting from selling AI tools to owning the integration layer.

title: Zuckerberg: AI agents slower than expected
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees at an internal town hall that AI agent development over the past four months has not accelerated as anticipated. The candid admission, captured in a recording heard by Reuters, is a rare public-facing crack in Big Tech's relentless AI optimism. Meta has heavily marketed its agentic AI roadmap to investors.

title: Alibaba bans Claude Code over backdoor fears
summary: Alibaba will prohibit employees from using Anthropic's Claude Code in workplace environments starting July 10, citing alleged security risks from embedded backdoors, according to a source familiar with the matter. The ban adds a new wrinkle to the already turbulent relationship between US AI labs and Chinese tech giants. Anthropic has not publicly responded.

title: Samsung profits set to jump 18x on AI chip demand
summary: Samsung Electronics is expected to report an operating profit roughly 18 times higher than a year ago, driven by soaring AI demand straining global memory supply and pushing chip prices higher. The result would mark another record quarter and cement AI hardware as the single biggest driver of semiconductor earnings. Rival SK Hynix is separately pursuing a $29 billion US listing.

title: Kling AI valued at $15B in $2.8B raise
summary: Kuaishou's Kling AI secured over $2.8 billion in fresh funding from a group that includes Alibaba and Tencent, putting its pre-money valuation at $15 billion. The round makes Kling one of the most valuable AI video generation companies in the world, competing directly with Sora and Runway. The backing of two rival Chinese tech titans in the same cap table is unusually rare.

title: US data center leases hit $850B, up 204% YoY
summary: US tech companies have committed a record $850 billion in data center leases, a 204% increase year over year, as the AI infrastructure arms race reaches unprecedented scale. The figure underscores how much of AI's cost is physical — land, power, and cooling — before a single model is trained. Critics warn the pace of commitment outstrips near-term revenue.

title: Bridgepoint leads €200M round in French HR tech Skello
summary: Private equity firm Bridgepoint is set to provide the bulk of a €200 million funding round for Skello, a French AI-powered HR management software company. Bridgepoint will become Skello's lead minority shareholder in the deal, according to a source close to the matter. The investment reflects sustained European appetite for AI-native HR and workforce tools.

title: Bernie Sanders wants public ownership of AI companies
summary: Senator Bernie Sanders unveiled a plan to give Americans direct ownership stakes in the country's largest AI companies, framing AI profits as a public good that shouldn't flow only to shareholders. The proposal is unlikely to pass in the current Congress but signals a growing political push to redistribute AI's economic gains. It arrives as Ark Invest's Brett Winton separately flagged government stakes in AI firms as a live debate.

title: Trump lifts ban on Anthropic's Claude models
summary: The Trump administration ended its weeks-long restriction on Anthropic's latest Claude models, which had been blocked following cybersecurity concerns raised by the Pentagon. Emails reviewed by the WSJ reveal months of back-and-forth between Undersecretary Emil Michael and CEO Dario Amodei over safety guardrails before the relationship fell apart — and was patched. The unblocking keeps Anthropic in the running for federal AI contracts.

title: India's Supreme Court exposes AI liability gap
summary: India's Supreme Court set aside a ruling by the National Company Law Tribunal after finding it relied on AI-generated case citations that did not exist, thrusting questions of AI accountability into the legal spotlight. Experts say India has no law specifically assigning liability for AI-generated errors, leaving courts to apply patchwork tort and contract principles case by case. The court is now drafting its own AI use regulations for the judiciary.

title: Vietnam lists 46 'high-risk' AI systems under new law
summary: Vietnam's government published a decree classifying 46 AI systems as high-risk — spanning transport, banking, healthcare, education, and litigation — that will face mandatory risk reporting and conformity assessments before deployment. The decree takes effect August 15, with transitional periods for existing systems running into 2027. It makes Vietnam one of Southeast Asia's most explicit AI regulatory frameworks to date.

title: NY House primary becomes AI industry family feud
summary: A Democratic primary for a New York House seat has turned into an open clash between pro-regulation and anti-regulation factions of the AI industry, with millions in corporate spending backing opposing candidates. Assemblyman Alex Bores, who supports AI oversight, faces a well-funded campaign reportedly tied to OpenAI interests. The race is being watched as an early test of how much political weight the AI lobby can throw.

title: Tesla driver charged with manslaughter in Autopilot crash
summary: A Texas man has been charged with manslaughter after his Tesla, operating on its automated driving assistance system, crashed into a suburban Houston home and killed a 76-year-old grandmother. The case is among the most serious criminal charges yet tied directly to automated vehicle technology in the US. It is expected to sharpen legal and regulatory scrutiny of driver-assistance systems across the industry.

title: OpenAI drops faster Realtime voice models
summary: OpenAI released gpt-realtime-2.1 and gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, cutting p95 latency by at least 25% through improved caching. The full model adds better reasoning and tool use for complex voice agents, while the mini variant targets speed and cost efficiency. Pricing starts at $0.60 per million text input tokens for the mini.

title: Claude audits Alberta's government code
summary: The Government of Alberta has been using Claude Code since 2025 to review systems, find vulnerabilities, and deploy fixes across its Ministry. The province now plans to expand into autonomous AI agents that can build entirely new software alongside engineers.

title: CISA secretly using Anthropic's Mythos to audit federal code
summary: The US Cyber Defense Agency CISA has been quietly using Anthropic's AI model Mythos to audit government software, according to three sources familiar with the matter. The news comes as Anthropic navigates an ongoing standoff with the White House over safety guardrails.

title: Google proposes a US frontier AI regulator called FARO
